contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a name reaches you
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is meant to remove obvious risk and obvious mismatch, and it is worth being precise about which it does.

Identity and address are verified. Qualifications are checked against the degree and the subject actually studied, since a general science degree does not automatically mean someone can teach Chemistry 0620 at Extended level. Teaching history is recorded by board and paper number rather than as a headline, because 'five years of IGCSE' can hide the fact that all five were Foundation-tier maths.

A subject conversation follows. An economics tutor might be asked how they would teach a student who writes fluent paragraphs but never labels a diagram axis, which is where most 0455 marks quietly go. A maths tutor gets a question about a student who can do the algebra but cannot start a worded problem.

References are taken where prior families exist, and what was taught is noted, not just whether the tutor was pleasant.

What screening cannot establish is chemistry between a tutor and one specific teenager. Nobody can. That is why the four-session review exists and why a change request is treated as routine. Fees are confirmed in writing beforehand, including whether travel is priced in, so the number does not move once sessions start.

Degree matched to the subject taught

Written fee, travel assumption included

Those dates are usually published at the start of the academic year and are the single most useful document a parent can forward before tutoring begins.

A tutor who has that calendar can align properly. Ahead of the class for a hard unit, behind it for consolidation, and clear of the week when a project is due so the student is not being pulled two ways. A tutor without it ends up teaching in parallel to the school, which doubles the workload and confuses the student about which method to use in the exam. Ask for the calendar. Send it on.

contentBlocks.heading: How late is too late for IGCSE tuition in Sector 27 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
There is a real answer to this, and it is not 'never too late'.

With three months or more before a series, method and content can both be repaired, and a tier change is sometimes still possible if the school agrees. With six to eight weeks, method and pacing can improve considerably, and past-paper technique alone often recovers marks that were being thrown away. With under three weeks, the honest plan is to protect what is already secure, drill the highest-frequency question types, and stop introducing new topics entirely.

What cannot be done at any point is promise a grade. Boundaries are set after papers are marked, the paper differs by series, and the student sits it alone. Any tutor quoting a guaranteed outcome should be declined on that basis.

Availability is also conditional rather than guaranteed. Home tutoring near Sector 27 depends on who is teaching in the central sectors this term and which slots they still hold. It can be reviewed as schedules change, and online remains available across Gurugram when the local match is not there.

What should be reliable is the process itself: punctual sessions, marking against real mark schemes, a written plan tied to actual dates, and a straight answer about progress at the four-week mark.

Six to eight weeks: method, pacing, technique
Under three weeks: defend, drill, add nothing new

faqs.question: We are in December and mocks start next week. Is there any point starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the goal changes. A week before mocks, no tutor should be teaching new content. The work is past-paper timing, question selection, and cutting the specific errors that cost marks the student has already earned: unlabelled diagrams, missing units, working done twice. Treat the mock as the diagnostic instead of paying for one. Then use the marked mock in January to plan properly for the series itself, when there is enough runway to fix content rather than only presentation.

faqs.question: Does Pearson Edexcel really offer a January exam session, and does that help us?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a January series for many subjects alongside the summer one, while Cambridge IGCSE runs June and November. For a student who wants a second attempt at a single subject without repeating a year, that extra window can matter. Confirm with the school first, because entries are made by them and not every subject or centre offers every series. Where it is available, it changes how a resit plan is built and how much pressure sits on the summer papers.

faqs.question: Which coursework subjects cause the most trouble in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: The ones with a submission date rather than an exam date. Global Perspectives 0457 involves a team project that depends on other students and cannot be fixed alone in the final fortnight. ICT 0417 practical work needs steady file discipline across months. Where a school runs the English First Language 0500 coursework route, drafts pile up quietly until they are urgent. Tutoring for these should start early and run in short regular sessions rather than long emergency ones near the deadline.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do students near Sector 27 usually take?
faqs.answer: Two per subject is the common pattern during term, dropping to one when a subject is stable and rising to three or four short ones during the mock run-up. More is not automatically better. A student with four tutored subjects and six weekly sessions has no time left to work alone, and independent practice is where most of the learning actually happens. A tutor who suggests cutting frequency once a subject stabilises is usually giving you honest advice rather than losing interest.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach Sector 27 for a 6.30 pm slot on weekdays?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends heavily on where they start from. A tutor already teaching in Sector 28, Sector 29, South City 1 or Sushant Lok 1 can usually manage it. Someone crossing from Sohna Road or the newer sectors during evening traffic on MG Road generally cannot hold it week after week, even with good intentions. Availability is checked slot by slot rather than promised generally, and weekend morning sessions are often the more dependable option for families here.

faqs.question: The school moved my daughter from Extended to Core. Can that be reversed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if the evidence changes before entries close. Schools usually decide tier on mock performance and classwork, and some will revisit a decision when a student shows sustained improvement in the weeks after. That has to be a conversation with the subject teacher, backed by marked work, not a request from a tutor. What tutoring can do is build the evidence quickly by targeting the topics that pulled the mock down. What it cannot do is override the school's entry decision.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after a month of tuition?
faqs.answer: Three concrete signs. Marks lost to avoidable errors should be falling in the areas being drilled, even if overall scores move slowly. The student should be able to name their own weak topics without being asked twice. And homework should be starting without a daily argument. Grades often lag by a term, so judging on the next report alone is unfair to a tutor who is doing the right work. If none of the three signs appear, review the match.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre better than a private tutor for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the student. A centre suits a student who works better with peers present and is following a very standard paper. One-to-one suits anyone with a specific diagnosis, an unusual combination like Additional Mathematics 0606, or a confidence problem that gets worse in a group. Centres near central Gurugram often teach to a mixed board audience, which is a real risk if your school follows Edexcel and the room is being taught Cambridge structure.

faqs.question: Do fees change if we start mid-term rather than at the beginning?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by subject, paper, mode and travel rather than by the calendar, so starting in November costs the same per session as starting in July. What changes is the plan. A mid-term start compresses the diagnostic work into the first session and often means more frequent sessions for the first month to catch up to the school's position in the syllabus. Everything is agreed in writing before the first session, including whether travel is priced separately.

introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 28 Gurugram exist to do a different job from the school, not a louder version of the same one. contentBlocks.heading: What a school teacher cannot do for a Grade 10 student in Sector 28 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A subject teacher has around thirty students, a two-year syllabus, a fixed number of periods and a school calendar that does not bend. Their job is coverage, and most do it well. What the job structurally does not allow is stopping the whole class for six weeks because one student never properly learned to rearrange a formula in Grade 8.

That gap is the tutor's job. So is the other common one: a student who knows the content and still loses marks because they answer every question in the same register. Cambridge and Edexcel both publish command words with specific meanings. 'State' wants a fact. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Suggest' wants a reasoned guess in an unfamiliar context. A student who writes a paragraph for all four gets credit for one.

Nobody can mark thirty scripts to that level of detail every week. One tutor with one student can, and that is most of the value.

There is a line, though. A tutor should not replace the school's method, should not do coursework, and should not tell a student the teacher is wrong. Where the school teaches a valid approach, the tutor reinforces it. Families searching for IGCSE tutors in Sector 28 Gurugram get better results when both roles stay in their lane.
items: Coverage is the school's job, diagnosis is the tutor's
Command words carry fixed meanings in both boards
One student means every script can be marked properly
Old gaps get re-taught without holding a class back
The tutor reinforces the school's method, not a rival one

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year IGCSE course, and where the school hands over
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE typically runs across Grade 9 and Grade 10, with Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel offering broadly parallel routes and quite different paper structures. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended entry. Edexcel International GCSE uses Foundation and Higher tiers, with Foundation capped at grade 5. Schools confirm both board and tier when entries are made.

Through Grade 9 the school owns almost everything: pace, sequence, which components are taken, which practical route is used. A tutor at this stage should be working on foundations underneath the syllabus rather than racing ahead of it. Number sense, algebraic fluency, writing stamina, the habit of reading a whole question before starting.

Grade 10 is where the handover happens. The school finishes content and runs mocks. Independent exam preparation, past papers under timed conditions, and the discipline of checking answers against a mark scheme become the student's own responsibility, and that is precisely the part no school has enough hours for.

After the results, IB Diploma and A Level both assume Extended or Higher content as a starting point. A student who took Core maths and now wants a science-heavy Grade 11 has a real gap to close, and it is better addressed in the summer than discovered in October.
items: Grade 9 and Grade 10, two years, two boards
Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
Grade 9 tutoring: foundations, not acceleration
Grade 10: timed papers and mark-scheme checking
Core to Grade 11 sciences leaves a gap to close

contentBlocks.heading: Where lessons actually happen in Sector 28 Gurugram and the sectors around it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 28 sits in the older central grid, with Sector 27 on one side, Sector 29 and Sector 30 close by, and MG Road, DLF Phase 1, South City 1 and Sushant Lok 1 all within a few minutes on a quiet evening. Housing here is mixed in a way that matters more for tutoring than most people expect.

In Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, homes are usually large enough for a study with a door. That is a genuine advantage. A closed door and a desk change how a session runs, particularly for a student who is easily pulled back into the family conversation.

Independent floors and older builder units are different. Sessions often happen at the dining table, which works if the television is off and the household agrees to leave that hour alone, and does not work otherwise. It is worth deciding this before the tutor arrives rather than three weeks in.

The Sector 29 side gets busy from early evening and parking near the market end is unpredictable, so a tutor driving in for a 7 pm start may prefer a slot fifteen minutes either side of it. Ask. Most will say yes to a small shift and hold the slot better for it.

Heritage City and Richmond Park: room for a proper study
Independent floors: agree the table and the hour in advance
Sector 29 evening parking is unpredictable
A fifteen-minute shift often buys a more reliable tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Marks the mark scheme gives away, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
Every IGCSE paper has a published mark scheme, and reading one alongside a student is the fastest lesson in the year.

In Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1, method marks exist independently of the final answer. A student who shows a correct substitution and then makes an arithmetic slip keeps most of the marks. A student who writes only the wrong answer keeps none. Getting a teenager to write their working down is not neatness, it is money.

In Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620, unit and significant-figure marks are separate from the calculation, and the Paper 6 alternative to practical rewards a very particular vocabulary about variables, repeats and anomalous results. Edexcel 4PH1 and 4CH1 embed similar reasoning inside the written papers.

Biology 0610 answers are marked against specific accepted terms, so a student writing 'the plant makes food' where 'photosynthesis' is required loses a mark they clearly earned.

Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 award marks for the diagram, the labels and the applied example separately from the argument.

English First Language 0500 is marked on assessment objectives rather than impression, which is why a strong writer can plateau without knowing why. An IGCSE science tutor Sector 28 request usually starts here, with the marking, not with the content.
items: Method marks survive a wrong final answer
Units and significant figures marked separately
Paper 6 vocabulary: variables, repeats, anomalies
Accepted terminology in biology answers
Diagram, labels and example scored apart from argument

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 28 Gurugram families, their schools, and the line a tutor should not cross
contentBlocks.body:
Children from these central sectors travel to a spread of schools, and Scottish High International School, Lancers International School, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School come up regularly in conversations with families here.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of these schools. No tutor is offered as a member of school staff, and nothing here should be read as endorsement by a school.

The practical relationship between tutor and school is worth setting early. The school decides board, tier, components, sequence and deadlines. The tutor works within that. Where a school teaches a particular method for solving simultaneous equations or structuring a source answer, the tutor should teach the same one, even if they personally prefer another. A student running two competing methods under exam pressure will use neither well.

Coursework is the sharpest line. A tutor may teach the skills, discuss structure in general terms and help a student plan their own time. A tutor may not write, edit or substantially rework a piece a student will submit as their own. Any tutor comfortable with that request is a liability to the student's entry, and the school is the right place to take questions about what help is permitted.
items: Scottish High International School
Lancers International School
Pathways World School
GD Goenka World School
Coursework: teach the skill, never write the work

contentBlocks.heading: Briefing a tutor properly on the first call
contentBlocks.body:
Matching works better when the parent brings information rather than a request for hours.

The useful brief has four parts. What the school is doing right now, by unit rather than by chapter number. What the student's last two marked assessments show, with the scripts if possible. What has already been tried, including any previous tutor and why that ended. And what the family can realistically commit to for the next three months.

From there a shortlist is built on paper-level experience first. Someone who has taught Extended 0580 to Grade 10 repeatedly is a different proposition from someone who tutors general school maths across boards. Slot compatibility comes second, because a good tutor in an impossible slot is not a match.

The first session is spent marking, not teaching. The tutor reads recent work against the published mark scheme and separates three categories: content the student has not learned, content they know but cannot deploy under time, and marks lost purely to instruction words and presentation. Those three need different treatment and different amounts of time.

A written plan follows, and a review after four sessions. If the student cannot yet describe what they are working on, something in the match is off.
items: Brief by unit, not by chapter number
Bring scripts, not summary grades
Say what was tried before and why it ended
Paper-level experience filtered before availability
Three categories of lost marks, treated differently

contentBlocks.heading: One room or one screen: session formats for Sector 28 Gurugram students
contentBlocks.body:
Home sessions have one advantage that is hard to replicate. The tutor sees the whole desk. They notice the phone face-down but buzzing, the notes written in four different books, the calculator the student has not learned to use properly. Those observations often matter more than the teaching in the first month.

Online has its own advantages, and they are not just convenience. A shared screen lets a tutor annotate a past paper in front of the student and save the annotated copy, which becomes revision material. Specialist papers that no local tutor teaches, Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 for instance, are reachable from anywhere in Gurugram or beyond it. And short sessions become viable, since nobody is losing forty minutes to Sector 29 traffic for a thirty-minute doubt-solving call.

Hybrid is common and sensible. Teaching in the room, marking and revision on screen.

Be honest about the failure case. A student who has not built the habit of working alone will not build it faster online. Where attention is the underlying problem, keep sessions physical while that is being fixed, and accept that this limits which specialists are available. An IGCSE home tuition Sector 28 Gurugram arrangement is worth the narrower choice in that situation.
items: At home the tutor sees the desk, not just the work
Annotated past papers on screen become revision notes
Rare papers matched from anywhere in the city
Short doubt-solving calls only make sense online
Attention problems need the room, even at a cost

contentBlocks.heading: What a tutor should never take over from the school
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor is a supplement with a narrow remit, and the arrangements that go wrong usually go wrong by drifting outside it.

A tutor should not become the reason a student stops paying attention in class. If homework is only ever done in the session, the tuition has quietly replaced the school day and the student is now getting less teaching, not more. A good tutor sets independent work and refuses to fill the hour with things the student could have done alone.

A tutor should not promise outcomes. Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked, papers vary, and the student writes the exam without help. Any guarantee of a specific grade is a claim nobody is in a position to make.

A tutor should not contradict the school in front of the student, or produce a parallel set of notes that doubles the reading.

And availability should be described accurately. Home tutoring near Sector 28 depends on which tutors are currently working in the central sectors and which slots they hold. It can be reviewed when schedules change each term, with online cover across Gurugram in the meantime. Being told plainly that a local match is not free this month is more useful than being sold a fragile one.
items: Independent work must stay independent
No guaranteed grades, from anyone
No parallel notes competing with the school's
No undermining the class teacher in front of the student
Local availability described plainly, reviewed each term

contentBlocks.heading: Checking that a tutor can teach, not just that they know the subject
contentBlocks.body:
Subject knowledge is the easy part to verify and the least predictive on its own. Plenty of people who can solve every question on Extended Paper 4 cannot explain the first line of the solution to a fifteen-year-old who has lost confidence.

So screening covers identity and address, then qualifications against the actual degree subject, then teaching history recorded by board and by paper rather than as a general claim. After that comes the part that separates candidates: a teaching question. How would you respond to a student who gives the right answer but cannot say why it is right. How would you handle a student who has decided they are 'bad at chemistry'. What would you do in the first ten minutes of a session with a student who has not opened the book since the last one.

References from previous families are taken where they exist, with the subject and level recorded.

None of this predicts personal fit, which only appears once teaching starts. That is why a change of tutor is treated as an ordinary request rather than an escalation, and why the review point sits at four sessions instead of at the end of a term. Fees and any travel component are confirmed in writing before the first session.
items: Identity, address and degree subject checked
History logged by board and paper number
Teaching scenarios asked, not just content questions
References recorded with subject and level
Written fees, agreed before teaching starts

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging an IGCSE tutor near Sector 28 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Have three things to hand and the first call takes twenty minutes. The board and syllabus codes as confirmed by the school. The last two marked scripts, since the actual paper shows far more than a percentage does. And the hour each week the household can genuinely leave alone, with the door shut.

What comes back is a short list of two or three tutors, each described by the papers they have taught, the slots they hold and where they are travelling from. Where no suitable tutor is free for home sessions in the central sectors this term, that is said directly and an online match is offered rather than a weaker local one.

The first session is diagnostic, spent marking rather than teaching, and it produces a written plan that separates content gaps from technique losses.

Review at four sessions. If the student cannot describe what they are working on, or if avoidable errors have not started falling, change the tutor rather than adding hours to the arrangement. That request is expected and gets handled without friction.
items: Board and syllabus codes from the school
Two marked scripts, not the report card
One protected hour, door shut
Two or three names with slots and travel stated
Diagnostic first session, written plan after it

faqs.question: My son's teacher says he is fine, but his marks are dropping. What is a tutor going to see that the school does not?
faqs.answer: Usually the same content knowledge but a different problem underneath it. A teacher marking thirty scripts sees a total; a tutor reading one script line by line sees that eight marks went on questions using 'explain' and 'suggest', or that working was never written down so method marks vanished. Both statements can be true at once. He may well understand the subject and still be losing marks in a pattern nobody has had time to notice. That pattern is what the first session is for.

faqs.question: Should a tutor teach a different method from the one used at school?
faqs.answer: No, unless the school's method is genuinely failing for that student and the teacher agrees. Two competing methods under exam pressure produce a student who half-remembers both. Where a school teaches a specific way to structure a source answer or solve simultaneous equations, the tutor should reinforce it and work on execution instead. The exception is a student who has never understood the school's approach at all, in which case an alternative can be introduced carefully and then discussed with the subject teacher.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework, or is that not allowed?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying skills, explain what the assessment criteria reward, talk through structure in general terms and help a student plan their time. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or heavily edit work that will be submitted as the student's own, and any tutor willing to do that puts the entry at risk. Rules vary by board and component, so the safest step is to ask the subject teacher directly what support is permitted for that specific piece before the tutoring starts.

faqs.question: We live in Heritage City. Can a tutor come inside the society for sessions?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, subject to the society's own visitor rules, which are set by the residents' association and not by any tutoring platform. Most families arrange a standing entry pass in the first week so the tutor is not held at the gate every session. Sessions inside Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City or DLF Richmond Park also make back-to-back scheduling easier for a tutor teaching more than one student nearby, which often helps with holding a consistent weekly slot.

faqs.question: How much homework should a tutor be setting?
faqs.answer: Enough that the session is not the only time the student works on that subject. A reasonable pattern is one focused task between sessions, usually a set of past-paper questions on the topic just covered, marked by the student against the mark scheme before the tutor sees it. If a tutor sets nothing, the tuition becomes a weekly performance rather than a study habit. If a tutor sets three hours on top of school work, something has been misjudged about the load the student is already carrying.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for maths in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: For a student with a specific, narrow problem, often yes. For a student with gaps going back to Grade 8, usually not, at least at the start. A common pattern is two sessions a week for the first six to eight weeks while foundations are rebuilt, then dropping to one once independent practice is holding. A tutor who suggests reducing frequency after progress appears is behaving correctly, and it is a reasonable thing to ask about at the four-session review.

faqs.question: What if the tutor and my daughter simply do not get along?
faqs.answer: Ask for a change. Screening establishes qualifications, board experience and teaching reasoning, but nobody can predict how a particular adult and a particular fifteen-year-old will work together, and a mismatch shows within two or three sessions. The written plan from the diagnostic session moves with the student, so a replacement tutor starts from the existing diagnosis instead of repeating it. Requesting a change is treated as routine, and it is far better than persisting for a term out of politeness.

faqs.question: Do you tutor students taking Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606?
faqs.answer: Matching for 0606 is possible and depends on availability, since the pool of tutors who have actually taught that syllabus is smaller than for 0580. It is often matched online for that reason, even when the family would prefer home sessions in the central sectors. The subject matters for anyone heading towards a maths-heavy Grade 11, because it covers calculus and functions that a standard IGCSE maths course does not. Starting it alongside 0580 rather than after tends to work better.

faqs.question: Our previous tutor was pleasant but nothing changed in six months. How do we avoid that again?
faqs.answer: Set checkable expectations at the start rather than at the end. Ask for a written diagnosis after the first session naming specific topics and specific error types. Then at four sessions, ask what has moved on that list. A tutor doing the work can answer immediately and with examples. A tutor filling an hour will answer in general terms about confidence. Confidence does matter, but it should arrive alongside evidence of fewer avoidable losses, not instead of it.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram for Grade 9 and Grade 10
heroSubtitle: Sector 29 sits beside MG Road, next to Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, which makes some evening journeys short and others slow. We match Grade 9 and Grade 10 students by board and paper entry first, then by the lesson slot you can genuinely hold every week.
introSummary: Families looking for IGCSE tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram usually begin with one practical question: can a tutor actually reach the house on a weekday evening. Sector 29 sits on the MG Road side of central Gurugram, close to Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, so travel is quick from some directions and slow from others. IB Gram matches Grade 9 and Grade 10 students by board first, Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel, then by the exact subject entry, then by whichever lesson mode survives your actual week.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Sector 29 Gurugram address actually changes about IGCSE tuition
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor coming to Sector 29 at 6.30 pm on a Tuesday is making a different journey from the one they would make at 4 pm, and the gap is often twenty minutes. That matters far more than most tuition pages admit. Sector 29 sits on the MG Road side of central Gurugram, bounded by Leisure Valley on one edge and by the traffic that gathers around the market strip on the other. A tutor living in DLF Phase 1 or South City 1 can reach Heritage City in a workable window. A specialist sitting out towards Sector 57 or Sohna Road, in evening peak, cannot do that twice a week without something quietly giving way.

So the first decision about IGCSE tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram is not really about the tutor. It is about the slot. Once you know which evenings are genuinely free after school transport, activities and homework, the pool of people who can serve that slot becomes small and honest, which is a better starting point than a long list.

Board comes next. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel use different papers, different exam series and different tiering rules. Somebody who teaches one of them well does not automatically teach the other well.

Short hops from DLF Phase 1, South City 1 and Sushant Lok 1

contentBlocks.heading: Travel times from Sector 29 to Heritage City, MG Road and South City 1
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 29 is ringed by places that behave very differently on a school evening. Sector 28 and Sector 27 sit immediately alongside and are a five-minute drive outside peak. Sector 30 and Sector 31 run towards the older South City side and look just as close on a map, though the turns off the main road can be slow enough to eat a quarter of a lesson. MG Road is the fastest corridor here and the least predictable one.

Heritage City and Unitech Heritage City families tend to have the easiest logistics, because a tutor already heading towards MG Road passes them anyway. DLF Richmond Park sits close enough to DLF Phase 1 that tutors covering Phase 1 will often take a Richmond Park session in the same evening round, and Sushant Lok 1 folds into that pattern too.

One honest caution. This pocket of Gurugram is convenient for tutors who already live in the central sectors and genuinely awkward for those who do not. If the subject you need is a narrow one, insisting on someone at your door can shrink the list to almost nobody. Widening to online, or to a fixed weekend home slot with midweek screen support, usually reopens it.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between a tutor at your door and a screen share in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE home tuition Sector 29 Gurugram families ask for works best where a tutor needs to watch a hand move. Early algebra. Working written under time pressure. The slow habit of showing method in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Paper 4. Those improve faster when somebody is sitting beside the page and can stop the student mid-error rather than after it.

Online does better than parents expect elsewhere. Past-paper walkthroughs, reading a mark scheme line by line, data response in Economics 0455, essay feedback in English, and anything where the tutor wants to annotate a shared document while talking. It also deletes the travel penalty, which is the single biggest constraint on any home slot here after six in the evening.

Hybrid is where most Grade 10 students land by December. One home session a week for the subject that is actually weak, plus one or two online sessions for revision, doubt-solving and paper timing. It looks untidy on paper. It also survives contact with school internal exams, which a neat fixed plan usually does not.

Availability for any of these can be reviewed once you name the slot rather than the wish.

Online for past papers, mark schemes and live annotation
Hybrid usually settles in around the Grade 10 mock season
Travel time is the real cost hidden inside an evening home rate

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel paper codes your Grade 9 will meet
contentBlocks.body:
Board matters because the paper structure differs. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and the tier sets the ceiling: a Core candidate cannot reach the top grades at all. That is why the tiering conversation belongs in Grade 9 and not in the term before the exam. Additional Mathematics 0606 runs alongside for students aiming at Higher Level maths later.

The Cambridge sciences follow a recognisable shape. Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each use a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper matched to the tier, and then either a practical test or the alternative to practical, depending on what the school enters. Students who bleed marks in the alternative to practical are almost never losing them on content. They lose them on variables, table headings and graph plotting.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is built differently. Mathematics A 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher across two papers. The sciences, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Biology 4BI1, assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical component.

An IGCSE maths tutor Sector 29 parents shortlist should be able to name which of these applies to your school entry without checking. If they cannot, treat that as information.

Additional Mathematics 0606 as a bridge towards HL maths
Cambridge 0625, 0620 and 0610 paper patterns
Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher tiers
Edexcel sciences assess practical skills inside written papers

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built for a Sector 29 Gurugram family
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is deliberately boring. First we take the board and the exact subject entry, including the tier if the school has already decided one. Second we take your two or three workable slots and the mode you can sustain through a full term, not just through a good week. Third we look at what the student is actually losing marks on, which needs a recent school report or a marked paper rather than a description of the problem.

Only then do we look at people. Tutors are filtered on the board and the subject, not on a general claim to teach science. A shortlist is normally two or three names. A long list is a sign that nobody filtered anything.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor sets a small piece of work under something close to exam conditions, marks it against the published criteria, and reports back on where the marks went rather than on how the session felt.

Four weeks later you should see the change in marked work: fewer method losses, cleaner definitions, better handling of the command word. If you cannot see it, the match is wrong, and changing tutors is the correct move rather than a failure.
items: Board and tier confirmed before any name is suggested
Two or three slots you can actually keep
Recent marked work beats a verbal description
Shortlists stay short on purpose
Four-week review against marked evidence

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year arc from Grade 9 to the Grade 10 series
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is a two-year course and a surprising number of families treat it as a one-year one. Grade 9 builds content, working habits and the tier decision. Grade 10 is mostly paper technique and coverage under time. A student starting tuition in Grade 9 is usually fixing understanding. A student starting in the November of Grade 10 is triaging, and a decent tutor will say so out loud rather than promise full coverage.

The series shape the calendar. Cambridge runs a March series in India alongside its June and November series, and Edexcel runs January and May-June. Schools around central Gurugram do not all choose the same route, so a tutor planning revision needs your school entry dates and not a generic timetable.

For a younger sibling in the same house, the work that pays off before Grade 9 is reading stamina, written method and the habit of answering the question that was actually asked. None of that is glamorous. All of it is what makes Grade 9 survivable.

After Grade 10 most students here move to the IB Diploma or to A Levels, and the subject choices made now quietly narrow those doors.
items: Grade 9 for understanding, Grade 10 for technique
Cambridge March, June and November series
Edexcel January and May-June series
Tier decisions taken early, not in the final term

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Sector 29 Gurugram families commonly attend
contentBlocks.body:
Children living around Sector 29 travel across a fairly wide arc for school. Scottish High International School out at Sector 57, Lancers International School on the Golf Course Road side, and Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School further towards the Sohna Road region all draw students from these central sectors. Some of those commutes are long, which is precisely why weekday tuition slots here start late.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and holds no affiliation with any of these schools. What we do use is the practical difference between them: internal exam calendars, when mocks are scheduled, how early the Core or Extended decision gets locked, and whether students are entered for the practical test or the alternative to practical.

A tutor who has taught students from a particular school usually knows its marking habits and its reporting language, and that is worth asking about directly. But do not over-weight it. A strong subject specialist who has never taught at your school will still outperform a weak one who has. School familiarity is a convenience. It is not a qualification.
items: Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School
Independent platform, no school affiliation claimed
School entry choices affect which papers are sat

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor reaches your Sector 29 door
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a process, not a badge. Before a tutor is put in front of a family we look at the qualifications they claim and ask for evidence of them, at their teaching history with the board in question, and at whether they can explain a mark scheme rather than only a topic. Identity is confirmed for anyone who will be entering a home.

Subject depth is checked separately from teaching ability, because the two come apart more often than people assume. Somebody with a genuinely strong physics background can still be unable to say why a Cambridge answer earned two marks instead of three. We ask for that explanation directly.

References from previous families are requested where they exist. Their absence is treated as neutral for a newer tutor rather than as a black mark.

For home sessions in Sector 29 there are practical checks too. Can this tutor really hold a fixed weekly time given where they live, and what happens when MG Road breaks the slot. A tutor who moves your time every second week is a scheduling problem wearing the costume of a teaching one, and it is worth naming early.
items: Qualification evidence rather than claims
Board-specific teaching history
Identity confirmed for anyone visiting a home
Ability to explain a mark scheme, not just a topic
Realistic weekly travel checked before the slot is offered

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, cancellations and the awkward questions worth asking
contentBlocks.body:
Fees for IGCSE tuition around here move with three things: the subject, whether the tutor travels, and how close the exam series is. Home sessions cost more than online for the plain reason that an hour spent in traffic is an hour nobody is teaching. Rare subjects cost more because the pool is small. Rates firm up near a series because demand does.

Ask what a session actually includes. Marked homework between sessions, a written note on what went wrong, and a channel for a quick doubt during the week are worth more than a longer session with none of that attached.

Ask about the cancellation window before you need it. And ask what happens when the tutor cancels, not only what happens when you do.

Then ask the blunt one: what happens if this is not working after a month. A tutor change should be an ordinary administrative event rather than a negotiation. Nobody can promise a grade, and a private tutor who does is telling you something useful about themselves. What can be committed to is a clear diagnosis, marked evidence, and an honest answer about how much ground is left.
items: Travel time is priced into every home rate
Narrow subjects, smaller pool, higher fees
Marked homework and between-session doubt access
Cancellation terms that run in both directions
Tutor changes handled as routine admin

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE tuition in Sector 29 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Write down four things before you enquire: the board, the subject and tier, the two evenings that are genuinely free, and the single thing you most want to change. That takes five minutes and it removes most of the back and forth that usually follows.

Send it through the enquiry form and an advisor will come back with what is realistic for a Sector 29 address, including the unwelcome version where a home slot at your preferred hour is not available and an online or weekend arrangement would serve you better. Availability is always subject to tutor schedules, and it tightens around the March and June series.

If you live in Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City or DLF Richmond Park, say so, because tutors already covering DLF Phase 1 and South City 1 may be able to fold you into an existing evening round without a new journey.

Bring a recent marked paper to that first conversation if you have one. It tells a specialist more in two minutes than a careful description of the problem manages in ten.

One last thing worth saying out loud. If the answer that comes back is that nobody suitable can hold your preferred time, that is the useful answer, not a failure of the search.
items: Board, subject, tier and two free evenings
Name your society so routing can be checked
A recent marked paper speeds up diagnosis
Availability shifts around the exam series

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually reach Sector 29 on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often, but it depends on where the tutor starts from. Someone already teaching in DLF Phase 1, South City 1 or Sushant Lok 1 can usually add a Sector 29 session to the same round, and Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park sit on natural routes towards MG Road. A tutor coming from Sector 57 or Sohna Road in peak traffic is a different proposition, and that arrangement tends to collapse after a few weeks. Give us the exact time you want and we will tell you whether it is workable, subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: Our school follows Cambridge. Does the tutor have to be a Cambridge specialist?
faqs.answer: Strongly preferred. The content overlaps a great deal with Pearson Edexcel, but the papers do not. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended, the sciences carry either a practical test or the alternative to practical, and the mark schemes reward particular phrasing. A tutor who has taught Edexcel for years can teach the subject, yet may coach the wrong exam habits without realising it. We filter on the board before the subject for exactly this reason, and we confirm the school entry before suggesting anyone.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the middle of Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the plan changes shape. Starting in Grade 9 usually means repairing understanding with time to spare. Starting after the Grade 10 mocks means choosing what to fix and what to accept, then drilling paper technique on the topics that carry the most marks. That is a legitimate strategy and it often moves results. What it cannot do is cover two years of syllabus properly. A tutor who tells you otherwise in December is selling you something rather than planning with you.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended, and who decides?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge subjects that tier, Core and Extended are different papers with different ceilings. Core candidates sit an easier set and cannot reach the top grades at all. Extended goes the full range but assumes stronger command of the harder content. The school usually decides based on internal performance, though parents can and do open the conversation. The decision matters most in Grade 9, because moving a student up later means covering Extended-only material at speed. Ask your school when the entry is finalised.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for IGCSE science practical papers?
faqs.answer: For the alternative to practical, yes, and often better than home tuition. Those papers test experimental reasoning on paper: identifying variables, reading a method, tabulating results, plotting and drawing a conclusion. All of that responds well to a shared screen where the tutor annotates a past paper live. For a school practical test, online support is more limited, because handling apparatus is the point. In that case we would suggest online for theory and technique, with the school lab doing what only the school lab can.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for an IGCSE tutor near Sector 29?
faqs.answer: Three factors dominate. The subject, because a maths or physics specialist commands more than a generalist. The mode, because a home visit includes travel that nobody teaches during. And the timing, because rates firm up as a series approaches and the pool thins. We do not publish a single figure, since quoting one would be misleading across that range. An advisor will give you a band once the subject, level and slot are known, and it stays subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: What if we see no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Then say so, and ask for the marked evidence rather than an opinion. After four weeks you should be able to compare early work with recent work and see something concrete: fewer method marks lost, cleaner definitions, better use of the command word. If that comparison shows nothing, the match is wrong. Changing tutors at that point is normal and we treat it as routine. It is far cheaper than another two months of sessions that feel productive and change nothing on paper.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both maths and physics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is convenient when it works. Plenty of engineering and physics graduates teach Cambridge 0580 and 0625 competently. The risk is that one of the two is genuinely their subject and the other is a stretch, which shows up in the harder Extended questions rather than in the early ones. If both subjects are weak, two specialists usually produce more movement than one generalist. If one is weak and the other needs light support, a single tutor is a reasonable call.

faqs.question: Do you work with students from Scottish High or Lancers International School?
faqs.answer: Families from Scottish High International School, Lancers International School, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School do live around Sector 29 and the neighbouring sectors, and tutors on the platform have taught students from those schools. IB Gram is independent and is not affiliated with any of them, so we make no claim to represent their teaching. What we do ask about is practical: the mock calendar, the entry decisions, and how the school reports progress, since all three affect how a term of tuition is planned.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram: What to Decide Before You Book
heroSubtitle: Most enquiries from Sector 30 arrive with the subject named and everything else unresolved. Which board, which grade scale, which paper entry, which option block. Settle those four and the tutor search stops being guesswork and becomes a short comparison between two or three real people.
introSummary: Before booking IGCSE tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram, four details decide almost everything: the examining board, whether the subject is graded A* to G or 9 to 1, the exact paper entry the school has made, and how many marks the student is currently losing rather than how many topics feel difficult. Sector 30 sits in the South City and MG Road belt of central Gurugram, so both home and online arrangements are workable. The details, not the postcode, are what make a match land.

contentBlocks.heading: Four things worth settling before you book an IGCSE tutor in Sector 30 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every enquiry we receive from Sector 30 names a subject and stops there. Physics. Maths. English. That is a useful start and it is nowhere near enough to match anybody properly.

Four details do the real work. Which board the school follows, since Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel set different papers. Which grade scale the subject reports on, because A* to G and 9 to 1 are not interchangeable and parents comparing a sibling from an earlier cohort get caught by that constantly. Which paper entry the school has made, including tier. And what the marked work shows, which is different from what the student says is hard.

Parents who bring those four to the first call get a shortlist in days. Parents who bring only a subject name usually spend a fortnight discovering them one at a time, while term keeps moving.

Sector 30 sits in the South City and MG Road belt of central Gurugram, well connected in most directions, so location rarely blocks a match here. The details are what block it. Get them out of the way and the rest is a short comparison.
items: Board: Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel
Grade scale: A* to G, or 9 to 1
Exact paper entry, including tier where one applies
Recent marked work rather than a list of difficult chapters

contentBlocks.heading: How Sector 30 Gurugram enquiries turn into two or three names
contentBlocks.body:
The process runs in four steps and the order is not decorative.

Step one, the board and subject entry are confirmed against what the school has actually registered, not against what a parent believes. Step two, a recent piece of marked work is reviewed, since a lost method mark, a misread command word and a genuine content gap need three different tutors and look identical from the outside. Step three, the timetable is agreed: which days, which mode, and what happens during school internal exams when everything gets suspended. Step four, tutors are filtered against all of that, and two or three names come back.

The shortlist stays small deliberately. Handing a family eight profiles moves the work of filtering onto the person least equipped to do it.

The opening session is a diagnostic, not a lesson. A short piece of work is set under timed conditions and marked against the published criteria, and the tutor reports what the marks did rather than how the student seemed. That report becomes the baseline. Four weeks later there is something concrete to compare against, and either the marked evidence has moved or the match needs changing.
items: School entry confirmed before names are discussed
Marked work read for the type of loss, not the topic
Timetable agreed including internal exam weeks
Two or three profiles, not eight
Diagnostic first session with a written baseline

contentBlocks.heading: Where Grade 9 and Grade 10 actually differ
contentBlocks.body:
The two IGCSE years are not the same job. Grade 9 is where content lands, where the option block is really tested, and where a school forms the view that later drives the tier entry. Grade 10 is where technique either exists or does not, under a clock.

That has a blunt consequence. Grade 9 tuition can change the direction of a subject. Grade 10 tuition, started late, mostly changes the efficiency with which existing knowledge is converted into marks. Both are worth doing. They are not the same purchase, and it is worth knowing which one you are making.

At the far end sits a question most Sector 30 families are already thinking about: IB Diploma or A Levels afterwards. Additional Mathematics 0606 taken in Grade 10 makes Higher Level maths considerably less brutal. A student who drops a science at Grade 9 to lighten the load can find the Diploma group choices narrower two years later.

Younger siblings benefit from something duller. Reading volume, written method, and the discipline of answering the question in front of them rather than the one they revised for.
items: Grade 9 changes direction, late Grade 10 changes efficiency
Option blocks chosen in Grade 9 constrain Grade 10
Additional Mathematics 0606 eases the route to HL maths
Dropping a science early narrows later Diploma choices

contentBlocks.heading: At home, on screen, or some of each
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition earns its premium in a narrow set of situations. A student who will not start a question without prompting. A younger Grade 9 who needs somebody physically present to hold attention. Anything where handwriting, layout and working need correcting as they happen rather than afterwards.

Online earns its place in a wider set. Any subject that lives on past papers and mark schemes. Any narrow entry where the specialist simply does not live nearby, which in practice covers Computer Science 0478, Business Studies 0450, second-language English and most of the humanities. Anything scheduled after nine in the evening, which happens more than parents admit during mock season.

A fair warning about online: it fails badly if the student sits with a phone and no writing surface. It works when there is a desk, a notebook and a device the tutor can see work on. That is a household arrangement, not a technology one.

Mixed weeks are common here. One home session, one online, and the online one is usually the more productive of the two once revision starts.
items: Home for attention, handwriting and live correction
Online for narrow subject entries and late slots
A desk and a notebook matter more than the software
Mixed weeks are normal once revision begins

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the paper structure behind each subject entry
contentBlocks.body:
A subject name tells you very little. The entry code and paper combination tell you what is being examined.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered, and the Core papers carry a hard ceiling that no amount of tuition lifts. Cambridge sciences separate a multiple-choice paper from a theory paper and then add either a practical test or the alternative to practical, so a student can be strong on content and still lose a grade on graph work. English splits sharply: First Language 0500 and Second Language 0510 examine different things, and a student misplaced between them struggles for reasons that have nothing to do with effort. Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 both reward the ability to apply a definition to a supplied case rather than to recite it.

Pearson Edexcel arranges things its own way. Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher over two papers, and the International GCSE sciences fold practical assessment into the written papers.

Ask a prospective IGCSE science tutor Sector 30 families are considering which paper the school enters. The answer arrives in one second or it does not arrive at all.
items: Cambridge 0580 Core ceiling versus Extended range
Practical test or alternative to practical, decided by the school
English 0500 and 0510 examine different skills
Economics 0455 and Business 0450 reward applied definitions
Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher tiers

contentBlocks.heading: The Sector 30 school map and what it changes
contentBlocks.body:
Students living around Sector 30 attend a spread of international schools rather than one dominant campus. Scottish High International School at Sector 57, Lancers International School towards Golf Course Road, Pathways World School, and GD Goenka World School out in the Sohna Road region all appear regularly in enquiries from these central sectors.

IB Gram runs independently of every one of them and claims no partnership, endorsement or affiliation. Naming a school here describes where children go, nothing more.

What the school does change is the calendar and the entry. Mock timings differ by several weeks between campuses. Some lock the Core and Extended decision at the end of Grade 9, others revisit it. Some enter students for the practical test, others for the alternative to practical, and revision has to follow whichever one is real.

So the useful question to a tutor is not whether they know the school. It is whether they will work from the school calendar rather than a generic revision plan. Long commutes to these campuses also compress the usable weekday window, which is worth saying before a timetable is fixed.
items: Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Lancers International School near Golf Course Road
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School
No affiliation or endorsement claimed by IB Gram
Mock dates and entry decisions vary between campuses

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 30 Gurugram and the streets around it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 30 sits between Sector 29 on one side and Sector 31 and Sector 32 on the other, with Sector 28 close by and the older South City 1 development just beyond. MG Road runs along the northern approach and DLF Phase 1 and Sushant Lok 1 are short journeys from here.

That middle position is genuinely useful. Tutors serving South City 1 or DLF Phase 1 pass close by, and Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park sit within the same cluster of societies, so a tutor holding two sessions in the area rarely has to cross the city between them.

The limitation is timing rather than distance. Between roughly five and eight in the evening the approaches from MG Road slow considerably, and a tutor who agreed to a 6.30 start from further out will start drifting to 6.50 by the third week. Better to book a later fixed time that holds than an early one that does not.

For households in the neighbouring societies, tell us which one. Routing is decided at that level of detail here, not at sector level.
items: Between Sector 29, Sector 31, Sector 32 and Sector 28
South City 1 and MG Road on the near approaches
Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park nearby
Evening approaches slow between five and eight
Society name matters more than sector for routing

contentBlocks.heading: What fees buy, and what they do not
contentBlocks.body:
Rates vary by subject, mode and season, and a page that quoted one figure would be lying by simplification. What is worth understanding is the shape of the variation. Specialist subjects cost more because fewer people teach them well. Home visits cost more than screen sessions because part of the hour is spent in a car. Everything firms up as a series approaches.

What a good arrangement includes: work set between sessions and actually marked, a short written note on where the marks went, and somewhere to send a question mid-week. What it does not include, from anybody: a promised grade. No tutor controls how a paper is marked or how a student performs on the morning, and a confident number offered in advance is a sales tactic rather than a plan.

Ask about the cancellation window in both directions before the first session. Ask what a tutor change involves, and expect it to be simple. Roughly one arrangement in several needs changing, usually for reasons of personality or pace rather than competence, and treating that as a crisis helps nobody.
items: Specialist subjects sit at the higher end
Home rates absorb travel that nobody teaches during
Marked homework and a written note between sessions
No grade promises, from any tutor
A tutor change should be simple to request

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a name reaches you
contentBlocks.body:
Three things are examined and they are examined separately.

Credentials, first. Degrees and teaching qualifications are asked for as evidence rather than accepted as statements, and identity is confirmed for any tutor who will visit a home. Board experience, second: how long they have taught Cambridge or Edexcel specifically, and at which levels, since teaching a national board for a decade does not automatically transfer.

Third, and the one that filters hardest, whether they can explain marking. We give a short answer and ask why it scored what it scored. Strong subject knowledge with no feel for the mark scheme produces sessions that feel excellent and change very little on paper. That combination is common and it is what this check is for.

References from earlier families are collected where they exist. A newer tutor without them is not penalised for it, because everyone starts somewhere and a diagnostic first session reveals more than a reference does anyway.

None of this makes a match certain. It makes a bad match unlikely, and it makes the reasons for a mismatch visible early enough to fix.
items: Documented qualifications, not asserted ones
Identity confirmed for home visits
Cambridge or Edexcel experience checked specifically
A live test on explaining why an answer scored what it did
References gathered where available, absence treated neutrally

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IGCSE tutor in Sector 30 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The enquiry that moves fastest contains four lines: board, subject and paper entry, the grade currently coming back on school assessments, and the two days that work every week rather than in a good week.

An advisor will read that, ask one or two follow-up questions, and come back with two or three tutors who fit, along with a straight answer on whether a home session near Sector 30 is realistic at your preferred hour. Sometimes it is not, and in that case saying so early is more useful than a match that quietly fails in three weeks. Availability always depends on tutor schedules and it tightens noticeably in the months before the March, May and June series.

If you have a marked paper or a recent report from school, attach it. A specialist reading two pages of marked work forms a sharper view than a long conversation produces, and it usually shortens the first session by a good twenty minutes.

If you are still deciding between two subjects to support, say both. An advisor can tell you which one is likely to move more in a term, which is usually the subject where marks are being lost on technique rather than the one that feels hardest at home. That comparison takes one conversation and it often saves a family from paying for two tutors when one would do.
items: Board, entry, current grade, two workable days
Two or three matched profiles come back
Attach a marked paper or school report if you have one
Availability tightens before the exam series

faqs.question: My older child was graded A* to G but the school now says 9 to 1. What changed?
faqs.answer: Different subjects and different boards report on different scales. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses the numeric 9 to 1 scale, while many Cambridge IGCSE subjects still report A* to G, and some report numerically. A 9 is above the old A*, and the boundaries do not map one to one, so comparing a sibling from an earlier cohort against a current report is misleading. Ask the school which scale each subject reports on. A tutor should know before setting any target, because targets set on the wrong scale are worse than none.

faqs.question: How do I tell the difference between a topic gap and a technique problem?
faqs.answer: Look at where the marks were lost rather than at the total. A topic gap shows up as blank space or an answer that goes in the wrong direction from the first line. A technique problem shows up as a nearly correct answer that scores half: the working is there but unshown, the command word was read as describe instead of explain, or the final line skips the units. The second kind moves quickly with the right tutor. The first takes longer and needs a plan for what gets sacrificed.

faqs.question: Should my child take Additional Mathematics in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: It depends on what comes after Grade 10. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 covers calculus and functions well beyond the standard syllabus and makes the first term of Higher Level Diploma maths or A Level Mathematics considerably less unpleasant. For a student already stretched across the standard entry, adding it is a poor trade and can drag the core subject down. The honest test is whether the student is comfortably handling Extended maths now. If they are scraping through it, skip it.

faqs.question: Is my child in the right English entry?
faqs.answer: Worth checking properly. First Language English and Second Language English examine genuinely different skills, and a student placed in the wrong one struggles in ways that look like poor effort. Many students in Gurugram schools speak English fluently but write with the structures the second-language paper rewards, or the reverse. A tutor can read a piece of recent written work and give a view within a session. The school decides the entry, but parents can ask for the placement to be reviewed if the pattern of marks is odd.

faqs.question: Can lessons be paused during school internal exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often sensible. Internal exam fortnights in the Sector 30 schools consume the evenings that tuition normally uses, and forcing a session into that week tends to produce an hour nobody remembers. The alternative some families prefer is keeping one short session focused only on the internal exam content. Agree the arrangement with the tutor in advance, along with how notice is given, so a paused week does not turn into an awkward conversation about fees afterwards.

faqs.question: Do you offer group batches or only one to one?
faqs.answer: One to one is the usual arrangement, because IGCSE entries differ so much between students that a group often ends up covering material half the room does not need. Small groups can work where two students share a board, a subject, a tier and a similar level, which happens most often between siblings or close friends from the same school. Tell us if that is what you want and it can be reviewed. It is not always cheaper per hour than it appears, once the pace compromise is counted.

faqs.question: What does the tutor actually do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Sets work and marks it, mostly. A short task under timed conditions, marked against the published criteria, followed by a plain account of where the marks went and what will be tackled first. Very little teaching happens in that hour and that is intentional. Starting to teach before knowing what is broken produces a plan built on assumptions. Parents sometimes find it anticlimactic. It is the session that makes the following ten sessions worth paying for.

faqs.question: How far in advance should we arrange tuition for the exam year?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most people do. Demand for Cambridge and Edexcel specialists rises through the second half of Grade 10 and the good weekday times go first, so a family looking in December for a January start has a much shorter list than one that looked in August. If the exam series is the target, arranging by the start of Grade 10 gives room to change tutors once without losing the year. Availability remains subject to tutor schedules throughout.

mainEntity.name: My older child was graded A* to G but the school now says 9 to 1. What changed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Different subjects and different boards report on different scales. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses the numeric 9 to 1 scale, while many Cambridge IGCSE subjects still report A* to G, and some report numerically. A 9 is above the old A*, and the boundaries do not map one to one, so comparing a sibling from an earlier cohort against a current report is misleading. Ask the school which scale each subject reports on. A tutor should know before setting any target, because targets set on the wrong scale are worse than none.

mainEntity.name: How do I tell the difference between a topic gap and a technique problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at where the marks were lost rather than at the total. A topic gap shows up as blank space or an answer that goes in the wrong direction from the first line. A technique problem shows up as a nearly correct answer that scores half: the working is there but unshown, the command word was read as describe instead of explain, or the final line skips the units. The second kind moves quickly with the right tutor. The first takes longer and needs a plan for what gets sacrificed.
