h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram for Cambridge and Edexcel Students
heroSubtitle: The most expensive belief in this syllabus is that IGCSE is the softer option and Grade 9 is a warm-up year. Marks are awarded for precision against a command word, and the tier decision is taken long before anyone panics. Tutoring here starts by correcting that.
introSummary: Families searching for IGCSE tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram often arrive with one assumption already in place: that the syllabus is lighter than the Indian boards and that Grade 9 is a settling-in year. Neither holds. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel award marks against precise command words and a fixed mark scheme, the tier entry is usually shaped by Grade 9 performance, and content is wide even where individual questions look short. Tuition that starts by fixing that misreading tends to move marks faster than tuition that starts with more content.

contentBlocks.heading: The assumption that costs Sector 31 Gurugram families the most marks
contentBlocks.body:
A parent moving a child from an Indian board into a Cambridge or Edexcel school usually hears the same reassurance from other parents in the society: the syllabus is lighter, there is less rote work, the pressure comes later. Some of that is true. The conclusion drawn from it is not.

IGCSE questions are frequently shorter than the ones on a national board paper, and they are marked against a fixed scheme that rewards a specific verb doing a specific job. Describe, explain, compare and evaluate ask for different things and score differently, and a student who answers all four the same way will lose marks steadily while appearing to know the material. Teachers see it as carelessness. It is usually a habit nobody corrected in Grade 9.

That is the gap most IGCSE tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram are actually hired to close. Not more content. Better conversion of what is already known into what the mark scheme will accept.

And the second half of the assumption fails too. Grade 9 performance often decides the tier a school enters a student for, which sets a hard ceiling on the final grade before the exam year even starts.
items: Shorter questions, stricter marking, not an easier course
Command words carry marks that content alone does not
Grade 9 results shape the tier entry
Conversion problems look like carelessness on a report

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject, what the marks are actually awarded for
contentBlocks.body:
In Cambridge Mathematics 0580 the method is worth marks even when the answer is wrong, so a student who works mentally and writes only the final line is throwing away credit every paper. Extended candidates lose most of their marks in the same three places each year: algebraic manipulation, multi-step problems, and the questions that ask for reasoning in words.

In the Cambridge sciences, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, the theory paper rewards a definition given in the syllabus wording rather than a paraphrase that means roughly the same thing. And the alternative to practical paper is a skills paper: independent and dependent variables, table headings with units, sensible axis scales, a conclusion tied to the data rather than to prior knowledge.

Edexcel International GCSE puts practical reasoning inside its written papers instead, across Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Biology 4BI1, and its Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher.

For English, structure scores. For Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450, the marks sit in applying a definition to the case in front of you, not in reciting it. A good IGCSE maths tutor Sector 31 parents shortlist will teach the mark scheme alongside the topic.
items: Method marks in 0580 lost by unwritten working
Syllabus wording preferred to paraphrase in science definitions
Alternative to practical is a skills paper, not a content one
Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 test practical reasoning in writing
Applied definitions score in 0455 and 0450

contentBlocks.heading: Matching a tutor to the gap, not to the subject name
contentBlocks.body:
Two students can both be at a grade 5 in chemistry for entirely unrelated reasons. One does not know the material. The other knows it and cannot phrase it in a way the mark scheme accepts. Sending the same tutor to both, on the basis that both said chemistry, wastes a term.

So the first thing we ask for is marked work rather than a description. A single paper with a marker's annotations tells us which of those two students we are dealing with, and often which topics have been quietly abandoned.

After that the board and paper entry are confirmed with the school, the workable days are agreed, and a shortlist of two or three tutors comes back. Not more. A longer list transfers the filtering job to the family.

The opening session is diagnostic: timed work, marked against published criteria, followed by a written note on where the marks went. That note is the baseline for the four-week review. If the marked evidence has not moved by then, the honest response is to change the tutor rather than to extend the trial and hope.
items: Marked work requested before any tutor is proposed
Same grade, different cause, different specialist
School entry verified rather than assumed
Shortlist of two or three, no longer
Written baseline and a four-week review

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 31 Gurugram, its neighbours and its evening traffic
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 31 sits below Sector 30 with Sector 32 alongside and Sector 29 a short distance up, in the older central belt where South City 1 and the MG Road corridor define most journeys. Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park are the societies that come up most often in enquiries from this pocket, and DLF Phase 1 and Sushant Lok 1 sit close enough that a tutor working there can reasonably add a session here.

Because this is older Gurugram rather than the newer expressway sectors, the internal roads are narrower and the approaches from MG Road congest early. That is not a reason to avoid home tuition. It is a reason to book a time that survives traffic instead of one that assumes an empty road.

The honest limitation: for a narrow subject entry, the number of specialists who can physically reach Sector 31 on a given weekday is small. Families who insist on home-only for something like Computer Science or a second language often wait weeks and then settle for a weaker match. Online removes that constraint entirely, and for those subjects it is usually the better trade.
items: Sector 30, Sector 32 and Sector 29 immediately around
South City 1 and the MG Road corridor shape the routes
Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park nearby
Older internal roads, early congestion on the approaches
Home-only requests shrink the list for narrow subjects

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 counts, and here is where it shows
contentBlocks.body:
The belief that Grade 9 is preparation and Grade 10 is the real year survives because nothing visibly breaks in Grade 9. The consequences land later, and by then they are expensive to reverse.

Three of them show up repeatedly. The tier entry, which schools commonly decide off Grade 9 internal results, and which caps the achievable grade for Core candidates regardless of how well Grade 10 goes. The option block, chosen in Grade 9, which quietly removes subject combinations from the IB Diploma or A Level choice two years later. And the writing habits, because a student who spends a year answering every question in the same shape carries that into the exam year and then has to unlearn it during revision.

Grade 10 has its own rhythm. Content coverage finishes, mocks arrive, and the work turns to timing, paper order and the discipline of leaving a hard question rather than sinking eight minutes into it.

Starting tuition in Grade 9 is cheaper in every sense. Starting in Grade 10 is still worth doing, provided everyone accepts it is triage rather than repair.
items: Tier entry often decided on Grade 9 internal results
Option blocks close later Diploma and A Level combinations
Answer habits formed early are hard to unlearn
Grade 10 work is timing, paper order and question triage

contentBlocks.heading: Before a tutor is recommended in Sector 31 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The screening is designed to catch a specific failure: somebody who knows a subject thoroughly and cannot get a student marks in it.

Qualifications are asked for as documents. Teaching history is checked against the board the family actually needs, since experience with a national board, however long, does not transfer cleanly to Cambridge or Edexcel papers. Identity is verified for anybody who will enter a home in Sector 31 or the surrounding societies.

Then comes the part that does the real filtering. A tutor is shown a student answer and asked to mark it and justify the score. Somebody who can only say the answer is broadly right has failed the check. Somebody who points at the missing unit, the unsupported conclusion or the command word that was ignored has passed it, and that is the person who moves a grade.

References from earlier families are collected where they exist and their absence does not disqualify a newer tutor.

What this cannot do is guarantee chemistry between a tutor and a fifteen-year-old. That only shows in the first two sessions, which is why the review point exists.
items: Qualification documents requested, not claims accepted
Cambridge or Edexcel teaching history checked specifically
Identity verified for home visits
Marking exercise used as the deciding filter
Rapport tested in the first sessions, not in screening

contentBlocks.heading: When a screen beats a chair at the dining table
contentBlocks.body:
Parents in this part of Gurugram tend to assume home tuition is the premium option and online is the compromise. For some purposes that is backwards.

Mark scheme work is one of them. A tutor sharing a scanned past paper and annotating it live, with the student writing on their own copy, teaches paper technique better than the same conversation across a table with two paper copies and no shared view. Revision timetabling is another. So is anything needing a specialist for a narrow entry, where the choice is a strong tutor on a screen or an adequate one in the room.

Home tuition still wins where presence is the point. A student who stalls without someone beside them. A younger Grade 9 whose attention wanders the moment a session goes remote. Handwriting and layout corrections that need catching mid-sentence.

The practical failure mode for online is a student on a phone with no desk. That is a household decision, not a technology problem, and it is worth settling before the first session rather than after four unproductive ones.

Ask any tutor how they run a session in each mode before choosing. The ones who answer identically for both have not thought about it, and the difference shows by the fourth week.
items: Online is stronger for mark scheme and past paper work
Home is stronger where presence keeps a student working
Narrow entries usually mean choosing the specialist over proximity
A desk and a paper copy make online sessions work

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 31 students go to school
contentBlocks.body:
Enquiries from this pocket of central Gurugram come from families at Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School towards Golf Course Road, Pathways World School, and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region. None of them is next door, and several involve a long bus journey each way, which is why weekday sessions here rarely start before half past six.

IB Gram has no affiliation with these schools and no arrangement of any kind with them. They are named because families ask about them, and for no other reason.

Where school detail genuinely helps is in planning. Mock windows differ. So does the point at which the tier entry becomes final, and whether a science cohort is entered for the practical test or the alternative to practical. A tutor who asks for that information at the start is planning around your school year. A tutor who offers a fixed twelve-week revision programme without asking is planning around their own template, and the two produce noticeably different results in February.

One practical note for families here: the schools do not all run the same reporting cycle, so a grade that looks alarming in one campus system may be a predicted grade in another and a raw internal mark in a third. Check which you are reading before treating it as a target.

Lancers International School near Golf Course Road
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School

contentBlocks.heading: Straight answers on fees, changes and what cannot be promised
contentBlocks.body:
Fees move with subject scarcity, mode and proximity to a series. That is the whole story, and any figure quoted before those three are known is decoration.

What should be included at any price: work set and marked between sessions, a short written record of the marks lost, and the ability to send a question mid-week without booking an hour for it. If a tutor offers none of that, the hourly rate is misleading, because you are paying for contact time rather than for progress.

What cannot be offered by anybody: a grade. Not a 7, not a 9, not a promised improvement. The person marking the paper has never met the tutor, and a confident prediction offered in advance says more about the seller than the student.

On changing tutors, treat it as normal. A reasonable share of matches need adjusting, usually over pace or personality rather than competence, and the request should take one message. Availability of any replacement remains subject to tutor schedules, and is harder to arrange close to a series than in the quieter months.
items: Scarcity, mode and season set the rate
Marked work between sessions is part of the price
No grade promises are made or accepted
Tutor changes requested in one message
Replacements are harder to arrange near a series

contentBlocks.heading: Getting started with IGCSE tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the evidence rather than the description. Photograph the most recent marked paper, note the board and the exact subject entry, add the two days that reliably work, and send it through.

An advisor reads the marked work first, because it usually shows within a page whether the problem is content or conversion, and that determines which kind of specialist gets shortlisted. You will get two or three names back with a note on why each one fits, plus an honest read on whether a home session in Sector 31 is realistic at your hour or whether online will get you a better tutor for the same money.

If you are in Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City or DLF Richmond Park, mention the society, since routing here works at that level and not at sector level.

And if the exam series is close, say that too. It changes the plan from repair to triage, and the plan should reflect it honestly rather than pretend otherwise.

Enquiries move faster in the quieter months, roughly between July and October, than they do once mock season begins. If the exam year is still ahead of you, that is the window worth using.
items: Send a marked paper, not a description of the problem
Board and exact subject entry included
Name the society for routing
Say how close the exam series is

faqs.question: Is IGCSE genuinely easier than CBSE or ICSE?
faqs.answer: Different, not easier. The volume of memorised content is lower and the questions are shorter, which is what creates the impression. What replaces it is precision: answers are marked against a scheme that expects a particular verb to be answered in a particular way, and marks are lost for vagueness that a national board paper might have tolerated. Students transferring in usually find the first two terms deceptively comfortable and then hit a wall at the first properly marked assessment. That wall is technique, and it responds well to targeted work.

faqs.question: What is a command word and why does my child keep losing marks on them?
faqs.answer: A command word is the instruction verb at the start of a question, and each one has a defined meaning in the syllabus. State wants a bare fact. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a reason attached. Evaluate wants both sides and a judgement. Students who write everything they know, in the same style, satisfy one command word by accident and miss the rest. The fix is mechanical rather than intellectual, which is why it moves marks quickly once a tutor starts drilling it.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE have coursework we should be worried about?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect. Most Cambridge subjects are examined entirely by written papers, and coursework components exist only in certain subjects and only where the school chooses that route. Art and Design is the common example. Some schools also enter students for Global Perspectives, which does carry project work. Ask the school directly which of your child's subjects, if any, include an assessed component outside the exam, because planning revision around coursework that does not exist wastes weeks.

faqs.question: We moved to Sector 31 mid-year from another curriculum. Where does a tutor start?
faqs.answer: With a mapping exercise rather than teaching. The first job is finding what the previous syllabus did not cover, because content sequences differ and a mid-year transfer almost always leaves specific gaps rather than general weakness. The second job is answer format, which is usually the bigger obstacle. A diagnostic session with timed work marked against the criteria will surface both. Expect the first month to feel slow and unglamorous, and expect the useful movement to arrive in the second.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help decide between Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: They can give you an informed view, though the school makes the entry. A tutor who has marked several weeks of a student's work can say honestly whether Extended is within reach with sustained effort or whether the student is likely to lose more marks than they gain by attempting it. Bring that view to the school conversation as evidence rather than as an argument. The decision matters because Core caps the achievable grade, and moving up late means covering Extended-only content under time pressure.

faqs.question: Our school starts sessions late because of the bus. Can tutors work after 7.30 pm?
faqs.answer: Some can and it needs saying at the enquiry stage rather than later. Late slots in this part of Gurugram are in demand precisely because school commutes to Sector 57 and the Sohna Road campuses are long. Online tutors handle late timings far more readily than travelling ones, for obvious reasons. If a home tutor agrees to a late slot that requires a long drive, ask what happens on a bad traffic evening, since a session that shrinks by twenty minutes every week is not the session you booked.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does one subject usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the common starting point for a subject that is drifting, with work set in between that takes about the same time as the session itself. Two a week suits a subject that is genuinely behind or an exam year with a short runway. More than two rarely helps, because the limiting factor is usually how much independent practice the student can absorb, not how many hours a tutor talks. If a plan proposes four sessions a week, ask what the student is expected to do alone.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE performance affect IB Diploma or A Level admission later?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Schools often use Grade 10 results to decide whether a student may take a subject at Higher Level or at A Level, and some set minimum grades for entry to particular subjects. Separately, the subjects taken at IGCSE shape which combinations remain open, since dropping a science or a second language early can close routes. That is why the option block choice in Grade 9 deserves more attention than it usually receives in a single parent meeting.

faqs.question: What if my child simply does not get on with the tutor?
faqs.answer: Say so early and ask for a change. It happens often enough to be routine, and rarely because the tutor is weak. Pace mismatches, a manner a teenager reads as impatient, or a tutor who explains at a level the student has already passed all produce the same result: sessions that are polite and unproductive. Two sessions is usually enough to tell. Waiting a term out of politeness costs far more than the awkwardness of asking, and a replacement can be reviewed subject to availability.

mainEntity.name: Is IGCSE genuinely easier than CBSE or ICSE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Different, not easier. The volume of memorised content is lower and the questions are shorter, which is what creates the impression. What replaces it is precision: answers are marked against a scheme that expects a particular verb to be answered in a particular way, and marks are lost for vagueness that a national board paper might have tolerated. Students transferring in usually find the first two terms deceptively comfortable and then hit a wall at the first properly marked assessment. That wall is technique, and it responds well to targeted work.

mainEntity.name: What is a command word and why does my child keep losing marks on them?

acceptedAnswer.text: A command word is the instruction verb at the start of a question, and each one has a defined meaning in the syllabus. State wants a bare fact. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a reason attached. Evaluate wants both sides and a judgement. Students who write everything they know, in the same style, satisfy one command word by accident and miss the rest. The fix is mechanical rather than intellectual, which is why it moves marks quickly once a tutor starts drilling it.

mainEntity.name: Does IGCSE have coursework we should be worried about?

acceptedAnswer.text: Less than parents expect. Most Cambridge subjects are examined entirely by written papers, and coursework components exist only in certain subjects and only where the school chooses that route. Art and Design is the common example. Some schools also enter students for Global Perspectives, which does carry project work. Ask the school directly which of your child's subjects, if any, include an assessed component outside the exam, because planning revision around coursework that does not exist wastes weeks.

mainEntity.name: We moved to Sector 31 mid-year from another curriculum. Where does a tutor start?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a mapping exercise rather than teaching. The first job is finding what the previous syllabus did not cover, because content sequences differ and a mid-year transfer almost always leaves specific gaps rather than general weakness. The second job is answer format, which is usually the bigger obstacle. A diagnostic session with timed work marked against the criteria will surface both. Expect the first month to feel slow and unglamorous, and expect the useful movement to arrive in the second.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help decide between Core and Extended?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can give you an informed view, though the school makes the entry. A tutor who has marked several weeks of a student's work can say honestly whether Extended is within reach with sustained effort or whether the student is likely to lose more marks than they gain by attempting it. Bring that view to the school conversation as evidence rather than as an argument. The decision matters because Core caps the achievable grade, and moving up late means covering Extended-only content under time pressure.

mainEntity.name: Our school starts sessions late because of the bus. Can tutors work after 7.30 pm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some can and it needs saying at the enquiry stage rather than later. Late slots in this part of Gurugram are in demand precisely because school commutes to Sector 57 and the Sohna Road campuses are long. Online tutors handle late timings far more readily than travelling ones, for obvious reasons. If a home tutor agrees to a late slot that requires a long drive, ask what happens on a bad traffic evening, since a session that shrinks by twenty minutes every week is not the session you booked.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions a week does one subject usually need?

acceptedAnswer.text: One a week is the common starting point for a subject that is drifting, with work set in between that takes about the same time as the session itself. Two a week suits a subject that is genuinely behind or an exam year with a short runway. More than two rarely helps, because the limiting factor is usually how much independent practice the student can absorb, not how many hours a tutor talks. If a plan proposes four sessions a week, ask what the student is expected to do alone.

mainEntity.name: Does IGCSE performance affect IB Diploma or A Level admission later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in two ways. Schools often use Grade 10 results to decide whether a student may take a subject at Higher Level or at A Level, and some set minimum grades for entry to particular subjects. Separately, the subjects taken at IGCSE shape which combinations remain open, since dropping a science or a second language early can close routes. That is why the option block choice in Grade 9 deserves more attention than it usually receives in a single parent meeting.

mainEntity.name: What if my child simply does not get on with the tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so early and ask for a change. It happens often enough to be routine, and rarely because the tutor is weak. Pace mismatches, a manner a teenager reads as impatient, or a tutor who explains at a level the student has already passed all produce the same result: sessions that are polite and unproductive. Two sessions is usually enough to tell. Waiting a term out of politeness costs far more than the awkwardness of asking, and a replacement can be reviewed subject to availability.

finalCta: Send a recent marked paper, the board and exact subject entry, and the two days that reliably work. An advisor will read the marked work before suggesting anyone, then come back with two or three tutors and a candid view on whether a home session in Sector 31 is realistic or whether online buys you a better specialist.

heroSubtitle: Predicted grades and final grades are produced by two different machines. This page explains what closes the distance between them for a Sector 32 student: the right board specification, the right tier, and a tutor who marks to the actual scheme rather than to a feeling.
introSummary: Parents looking for IGCSE tutors in Sector 32 Gurugram usually want one thing: someone who can move a child from the grade the school predicted to the grade the child is capable of writing in the hall. That work is specific. It depends on the board, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, on the tier the school has entered the student for, and on paper technique that most students never get taught directly. Sessions can run at home around Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, or online, subject to tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: The gap between a predicted grade and a final grade in Sector 32 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Predicted grades land in Sector 32 households at roughly the same point each year, usually the fortnight after the first proper mock, and they rarely arrive the way families expect. A prediction is not a promise. It is the school reading the evidence it happens to hold: class tests, one or two mock papers, homework that may have been finished at eleven at night. The final grade comes from something much narrower, which is two or three timed papers written in a hall during a single exam series.

The distance between those two numbers is the whole job.

Most of the time that distance is not a content problem. A student living near Heritage City or DLF Richmond Park, travelling out to school along MG Road or towards Sohna Road, has generally met every topic on the syllabus at least once. What they have not practised is writing forty marks inside fifty minutes with a clock running, or reading a stem closely enough to see that the command word was explain and not describe. Those are trainable habits, and they move on a timescale of eight to twelve weeks rather than eight to twelve days.

So the families who begin in the autumn term have room to work with. The ones who call in March are working with what is left. Both are worth doing, but they are not the same piece of work, and any tutor who pretends otherwise is selling you something.
items: Prediction built on classwork; final grade built on timed papers
Command words: state, describe, explain, justify
Eight to twelve weeks to shift technique, not days
March starts are triage, autumn starts are planning
Content recall is rarely the actual bottleneck

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions, online sessions and the traffic between Sector 32 and MG Road
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 32 sits in an awkward and useful spot. It is close enough to MG Road, DLF Phase 1 and South City 1 that a tutor living in central Gurugram can reach a home in twenty minutes on a quiet evening. It is also close enough to the MG Road corridor that the same trip on a Friday at seven can take three times as long. That single fact decides more about tutoring quality than any brochure will admit.

Home tuition works well here for younger students, for anyone who needs supervision as much as instruction, and for households where a parent wants to hear what is being said. It works badly for a rare combination such as Edexcel Economics or Cambridge Computer Science, because the pool of people willing to drive across Gurugram for one subject is thin, and you end up choosing on proximity instead of on competence.

Online changes that calculation. A screen with a shared document and a scanned past paper is honestly close to a table for most written subjects, and it removes the travel penalty from both sides. Practical-heavy work is where it loses ground. Diagram-drawing, apparatus description and the alternative-to-practical papers benefit from a person sitting beside the student pointing at a page.

A hybrid arrangement is common near Sector 32: home sessions for the core weekly subject, online for the specialist one.
items: MG Road evening traffic dictates realistic slot times
Home tuition: better supervision, narrower tutor pool
Online: wider specialist match, weaker for diagram work

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: where Sector 32 Gurugram students actually lose marks
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the subject most families ask about first, and the loss pattern is consistent. On Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, marks disappear on multi-step problems where the method is right and the arithmetic collapses halfway, and on questions that ask for a reason rather than a value. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, tests similar ground but sets its questions with a different flavour, so a tutor drilling the wrong board's past papers is doing careful work in the wrong direction.

Sciences split differently. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each carry a practical strand, taken either as a laboratory paper or as the written alternative-to-practical paper, and the alternative is heavily about reading tables, spotting anomalies and describing method. Students who are strong in theory often score poorly there simply from lack of exposure. The Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical understanding inside the written papers instead, which is a real structural difference worth confirming with the school.

English carries its own trap. Cambridge First Language English 0500 rewards directed writing that changes register on demand, and students in Gurugram international schools usually write fluently but ignore the audience instruction.

Economics, Business and Computer Science are the ones where a specialist match matters most and a nearby generalist matters least.
items: Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are not interchangeable practice
Alternative-to-practical: tables, anomalies, method description
0500 directed writing: register and audience marks
Method-mark discipline in multi-step algebra
Specialist subjects: match on subject, not on distance

contentBlocks.heading: Heritage City, DLF Richmond Park and the streets around Sector 32
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 32 is defined less by its own boundary than by what surrounds it. Heritage City and Unitech Heritage City sit inside the pocket, DLF Richmond Park is a short hop away, and the sector opens directly onto the MG Road stretch that connects it to DLF Phase 1 and Sushant Lok 1. Sector 31 and Sector 30 are the immediate sector neighbours, close enough that a tutor booked for a family in one is often already coming from the other.

This matters practically. A tutor who already teaches two evenings a week in South City 1 can slot a Sector 32 family into the same corridor without adding an hour of driving, which usually means better slot options and steadier attendance. Requests that cut against the corridor, for instance a family in Sector 32 asking for a tutor based out towards Golf Course Extension, tend to produce later start times and more cancellations in monsoon months.

Families in the Heritage City blocks often prefer sessions immediately after school pick-up, before activities begin. Households closer to the MG Road side more often ask for a later slot, once the working parent is home and traffic has thinned.

None of this is a rule. It is a pattern we plan around when building a shortlist for this pocket of central Gurugram.

Corridor towards MG Road, DLF Phase 1, Sushant Lok 1
Heritage City and Unitech Heritage City inside the pocket
DLF Richmond Park within a short drive

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended: the tiering decision that sets your ceiling
contentBlocks.body:
Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. A student is entered either for the Core papers or the Extended papers, and the two routes do not have the same top grade available. Core is designed for a lower band of the grade range and caps out well below the top; Extended runs to the highest grades on the scale. Once the school has submitted entries, that ceiling is fixed for that series, no matter how good the tuition is afterwards.

This is the single most consequential decision in a Sector 32 family's IGCSE year, and it is often made quietly by the department in a term-end meeting.

Pearson Edexcel handles this differently. Its International GCSE sciences are untiered, so every candidate sits the same papers, while Mathematics A does run Foundation and Higher tiers with separate grade ranges. Grading scales also vary: the 9 to 1 scale is used across Edexcel International GCSE and across most Cambridge IGCSE subjects, though some Cambridge syllabuses still report on the older A* to G scale depending on the subject and the region. Confirm your child's exact entry code and tier with the school rather than assuming.

Where a student is sitting near a tier boundary, the honest conversation is about whether a term of concentrated work makes the higher tier survivable, or merely humiliating.
items: Cambridge Core papers cap the maximum grade available
Extended papers run to the top of the scale
Edexcel International GCSE sciences: untiered entry
Edexcel Maths A: Foundation and Higher tiers
Entry codes and tier confirmed by the school, not assumed

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist for Sector 32 is put together
contentBlocks.body:
A useful match starts from information most enquiry forms never ask for. Which board. Which syllabus code, if the parent knows it. Which tier. What the last mock paper actually looked like, including the marks lost rather than only the total. What time the child gets home, and what is already booked on which evenings.

With that, an advisor filters for people who have taught that specification recently, not merely the subject. Recency matters because specifications get revised, and a tutor working from a set of notes assembled several years ago will teach content that is still true and technique that is no longer rewarded.

We then look at the practical constraints. Travel time from wherever the tutor is based to Sector 32, weekday slot availability, and whether the family wants home, online, or a mix. Only after that do we send names.

The first session is diagnostic. A good tutor spends most of it watching the student attempt questions rather than lecturing, because the aim is to find where marks are leaking. You should receive a short written read-out afterwards saying what they saw, what they plan to do about it, and roughly how long they think it takes. If that read-out never comes, that is your signal.
items: Board, syllabus code and tier captured before matching
Last mock paper reviewed for lost marks, not totals
Filter on recent experience with that specification
Travel time and weekday slots checked before names go out
Written diagnostic read-out after the first session

contentBlocks.heading: What honest tutoring looks like when the mocks come back badly
contentBlocks.body:
Nobody enjoys the call after a poor mock. It is also the moment that reveals what kind of arrangement you have entered into.

A tutor worth keeping will tell you plainly which of three things happened: the student did not know the content, knew it and could not retrieve it under time pressure, or knew it and answered a different question from the one asked. Those three failures have completely different fixes, and lumping them together as needs more practice is the standard evasion.

We cannot promise grades and will not. No platform can, because the person who writes the paper is a sixteen-year-old in a hall on a particular morning, and nobody controls that morning. What can reasonably be described is process: a weekly plan, papers marked against the published mark scheme rather than by impression, and a fortnightly note to the parent about what changed.

Fees are quoted before the first session and depend on the subject, the level and the mode. Rare subjects and Extended-tier work cost more than Core-level support in a common subject, because the pool of people who can do it well is smaller.

If progress genuinely is not happening after several weeks, a tutor change can be requested. That is a normal part of the arrangement, not a complaint.
items: Three failure modes: content, retrieval, misreading
Marking against the published scheme, not by impression
Fortnightly written update to the parent
Fees vary by subject, level and mode; quoted upfront
Tutor changes can be requested without friction

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Sector 32 Gurugram families send children to
contentBlocks.body:
Children living around Sector 32 are spread across a wide set of schools rather than concentrated in one. Scottish High International School out towards Sector 57, Lancers International School on the Golf Course Road side, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road direction all draw families from this part of central Gurugram. The commute varies from a fifteen-minute run to a bus route that starts before seven.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. We name them because the school a student attends changes what tutoring should look like, not to imply any endorsement.

The practical consequence is scheduling. A child on a long bus route reaches home tired and late, which makes an early-evening home session in Sector 32 unrealistic on weekdays and pushes serious work to Saturday mornings. Schools also differ in how much internal assessment and how many school-set mocks they run, and a tutor needs to work around that calendar rather than against it.

Boards differ too. Some of these schools follow Cambridge IGCSE, others Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a few run both across different departments. Always check which specification your child's department has entered before booking subject support.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor is recommended in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on this platform is a set of checks, and it is worth being precise about what those checks do and do not cover.

Identity is confirmed against government photo identification. Teaching background is reviewed, which means degree or qualification evidence relevant to the subject being taught, plus a record of where and for how long they have taught it. For IGCSE specifically we ask which board and which syllabus they have most recently prepared students for, because Cambridge and Edexcel experience are not automatically transferable at paper level.

Subject competence is assessed through a structured conversation with someone who knows the specification, not through a form. A tutor who cannot describe the structure of the papers they claim to teach does not go on a shortlist.

What verification does not do is predict chemistry with your particular child. A tutor can be qualified, experienced and entirely wrong for a quiet fifteen-year-old who shuts down when pushed. That is why the first session is treated as a trial and why a change is easy to request.

Parent feedback after the early weeks feeds back into whether a tutor keeps being recommended for that subject and level in this part of Gurugram.
items: Government photo ID verified
Qualification and teaching history reviewed
Board-specific IGCSE experience asked for explicitly
Structured subject conversation, not a self-declaration form
Early parent feedback affects future recommendations

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with IGCSE tutors in Sector 32 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one short conversation. Tell an advisor the board, the subjects, the tier if you know it, and the two or three evenings that are genuinely free after school and activities. Send a photograph of the most recent marked mock paper if you have one, because the marks lost tell us far more than the grade did.

An advisor comes back with a small set of names suited to Sector 32 and the corridor around it, each with their background, their board experience, and the slots they can realistically hold given travel from their own base. Availability is subject to tutor schedules, and rare subject requests take longer to fill than Mathematics or the sciences.

The first session is a diagnostic. You should expect a written note afterwards describing what the tutor found and what they intend to do in the first month. If that note is vague, say so immediately rather than waiting a term.

One honest caveat before you begin. If the exam series is six weeks away and the gaps are wide, tuition can protect the grade the student already has and sharpen paper technique. It cannot rebuild two years of a syllabus. Starting earlier is worth more than starting intensively.

Send the last marked mock if available
Names come back with board experience and real slots
First session is diagnostic, with a written note after
Late starts protect and sharpen; they do not rebuild

faqs.question: My son's school predicted a 6 in Maths. Can a tutor in Sector 32 realistically get him to an 8?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends almost entirely on why the 6 was predicted. If he understands the content and loses marks to arithmetic slips, misread command words and running out of time, that is technique, and technique moves fastest of anything. If the prediction reflects genuine gaps across several topics, two grades is a long climb and needs most of an academic year. Ask the tutor to look at the marked mock before anyone promises anything. No honest tutor will commit to a specific grade in advance, and one who does is telling you something about their judgement.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The school's examinations officer or the head of department will tell you, and the statement of entry issued before the series lists the board, the syllabus code and the tier. It is worth asking early rather than assuming, because some schools in this part of Gurugram run Cambridge IGCSE in one department and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in another. The distinction changes which past papers are useful, how practical work is assessed, and in some subjects which grades are even available to your child. Tutoring against the wrong board wastes months quietly.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor coming to Heritage City better than online sessions?
faqs.answer: For a younger student, or one who needs someone physically present to stay on task, home tuition in the Heritage City and Sector 32 pocket is usually the better arrangement. For a specialist subject it often is not, because insisting on a tutor who can drive to your gate narrows the pool sharply and you end up choosing on convenience rather than on subject depth. Many families here settle on a split: home sessions for the subject taken twice a week, online for the one specialist paper. Home availability depends on tutor schedules and traffic on the MG Road side.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: In the Cambridge sciences, students who do not sit the laboratory practical take a written paper about practical work instead. It asks them to read results tables, identify anomalous readings, describe how an experiment was or should be carried out, suggest improvements, and handle simple errors. It rewards precision of language more than laboratory skill. Students strong in theory often underperform on it purely because they have not practised the phrasing examiners accept. Pearson Edexcel structures this differently, assessing practical understanding within the main written papers, so confirm which route your child's school uses.

faqs.question: We live near DLF Richmond Park. How late can weekday sessions start?
faqs.answer: Most families in this pocket end up booking somewhere between five and eight in the evening, and the constraint is rarely the tutor. It is the child's school bus and activity schedule. A student on a long route from the Sohna Road side may not be home and settled before six thirty, which makes a productive hour before seven difficult. Later slots exist but attention drops noticeably after eight. Saturday mornings are often the most useful session of the week and get booked out first. Actual timings are subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees depend on?
faqs.answer: Subject, level and mode, mainly. Support at Core level in a widely taught subject sits at the lower end. Extended-tier Mathematics, the sciences at the top of the scale, and rarer subjects such as Economics or Computer Science cost more, because fewer tutors can teach them to that standard. Home sessions carry a premium over online, since the tutor is absorbing travel time across Gurugram. Fees are quoted before the first session, not after, and you should get the figure per session together with the expected number of sessions per week.

faqs.question: The first tutor did not work out. What now?
faqs.answer: Say so early. Four weeks is enough to know whether a student is engaging, and dragging an unproductive arrangement through a whole term costs more than the fees do. Tell the advisor specifically what went wrong: too fast, too slow, no marking, no plan, or simply a personality mismatch. That detail makes the second match considerably better than the first. Requesting a change is treated as normal and does not require a complaint or justification beyond describing what you observed. Replacement timing depends on availability in the subject and level you need.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework components?
faqs.answer: Where a syllabus includes a coursework or portfolio element, a tutor can help the student plan it, understand the assessment criteria, and review drafts for structure and clarity. They cannot write it, supply content to be submitted as the student's own, or work around the school's authentication rules. Schools take that seriously and so do we. Note that coursework routes are optional in several Cambridge syllabuses and absent in others, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses most subjects entirely by examination, so check what your child's department has actually chosen.

faqs.question: How soon should we start if exams are in the May and June series?
faqs.answer: Ideally the previous autumn. That gives a full term for content repair, a term for paper technique, and the final weeks for timed practice under real conditions. Starting in January still works and is common. Starting in April changes the goal: at that point the sensible plan is to secure the marks the student can already reach, tighten timing, and drill the highest-frequency question types rather than attempt full syllabus coverage. Ask the tutor to tell you honestly which of those two plans they are running.

Requesting a change is treated as normal and does not require a complaint or justification beyond describing what you observed. Replacement timing depends on availability in the subject and level you need.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with coursework components?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where a syllabus includes a coursework or portfolio element, a tutor can help the student plan it, understand the assessment criteria, and review drafts for structure and clarity. They cannot write it, supply content to be submitted as the student's own, or work around the school's authentication rules. Schools take that seriously and so do we. Note that coursework routes are optional in several Cambridge syllabuses and absent in others, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses most subjects entirely by examination, so check what your child's department has actually chosen.

mainEntity.name: How soon should we start if exams are in the May and June series?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ideally the previous autumn. That gives a full term for content repair, a term for paper technique, and the final weeks for timed practice under real conditions. Starting in January still works and is common. Starting in April changes the goal: at that point the sensible plan is to secure the marks the student can already reach, tighten timing, and drill the highest-frequency question types rather than attempt full syllabus coverage. Ask the tutor to tell you honestly which of those two plans they are running.

An advisor will come back with names suited to Sector 32 and the roads around it, with real slot times attached. The first session is a diagnostic, and you get a written summary of what it found.

contentBlocks.heading: Two names on a shortlist: comparing IGCSE tutors in Sector 38 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
You have two names. Both hold a decent degree. Both have taught for years. Both are free on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, both will travel to Sector 38, and the difference between their fees is small enough to ignore. Now choose.

Most families choose on warmth, or on who replied to the message faster, and about half the time that works out. The other half of the time a term goes by and the marks have not shifted.

There is a better test, and it takes about ten minutes on a phone call. Ask each of them to describe the structure of the papers your child is actually sitting. Not the subject, the papers: how many, what each one is for, what the mark distribution looks like across the components. Somebody who has prepared candidates for that specification in the last year or two will answer without hesitating. Somebody who has taught the subject broadly, in a school following a different board, will give you a general answer about strong fundamentals.

That is the whole comparison, more or less. Everything else on this page is detail hanging off it.

Families around The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden ask us for this comparison constantly, so it is worth setting out in full rather than repeating on calls.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 38 shortlist gets built before you see it
contentBlocks.body:
Nothing useful happens until an advisor knows four things: board, subject, the tier or entry route if one applies, and what the last piece of marked work looked like. A screenshot of a returned script is worth more than a paragraph describing the problem, because the pattern of red pen tells you where marks are actually leaking.

After that the filtering is unglamorous. Tutors are narrowed to those who have prepared candidates for that specific specification recently. Then narrowed again on geography, because a person based near Golf Course Road can hold a Sector 38 slot at six without difficulty, while somebody coming across from the far side of the city cannot hold it reliably through a rainy August.

What reaches you is a small set of names with their background, their board history and the slots they can genuinely commit to.

Then comes the part that decides everything. The first session is a trial, and it should be a diagnostic rather than a lesson. A tutor who spends ninety minutes explaining is showing you they can talk. A tutor who spends most of it setting questions, watching how the student attacks them and noting where the thinking stalls is doing the job. Ask for their findings in writing afterwards.

Written findings requested after the trial

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the specification first: subject choices in Sector 38 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Subject requests from this pocket skew towards the combinations that decide sixth-form entry, and each carries its own comparison test.

For Economics, Cambridge runs syllabus 0455 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics is coded 4EC1. Ask a candidate tutor how they teach evaluation, because that is where the top band lives and where most students plateau at a competent middle grade. History and Geography, Cambridge 0470 and 0460, reward source handling and case-study specificity; a tutor who cannot name the case studies your child's school has chosen has not asked the right question yet.

Business Studies, Cambridge 0450, is deceptively easy to teach badly. The content is readable, so students feel confident, then lose marks by giving textbook definitions where the question wanted application to the stimulus firm.

English splits by route. Cambridge First Language English and Pearson Edexcel English Language A, 4EA1, do not ask for the same things, and Edexcel English Literature 4ET1 has its own anthology requirements.

ICT and Computer Science need someone with hands on the software, not just the theory, and that is a genuinely smaller pool around Sector 38 than the sciences are.
items: Economics 0455 and 4EC1: evaluation is the ceiling
History 0470, Geography 0460: named case studies matter
Business 0450: application to the stimulus, not definitions
Edexcel English 4EA1 and Literature 4ET1 run their own routes
ICT needs practical software fluency, not theory alone

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel put different things in the paper
contentBlocks.body:
The specification document is public, free and boring, and almost no parent reads it. It is also the fastest way to hold a tutor to account, because it states exactly what will be assessed and how the marks are distributed.

Two things in it are worth your attention. The scheme of assessment lists the components: how many papers, roughly how long each runs, and what proportion of the total each carries. The assessment objectives explain what the marks are for, usually split between knowledge, application and analysis or evaluation. A student stuck below the top band is almost always losing marks in one objective while performing fine in the others, and a tutor who works in those terms can tell you which.

The boards differ structurally. Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects run a tiered entry with different papers and different grade ranges, and some offer an optional coursework component instead of a fully examined route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses most subjects entirely by written examination, with its sciences untiered, though Mathematics A does run separate tiers.

Where a detail matters to your decision, check the current specification on the board's own site or ask the school, because syllabuses are revised and the version your tutor learnt on may not be the one your child sits.
items: Scheme of assessment: components, durations, weightings
Assessment objectives: knowledge, application, evaluation
Cambridge tiering and optional coursework in some subjects
Edexcel International GCSE: largely examination only
Confirm the live specification version with the school

contentBlocks.heading: The Aralias, The Magnolias and the pocket around Sector 38
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 38 sits behind the Golf Course Road frontage rather than on it. The Aralias and The Magnolias are on that side, low-rise and set back, with Suncity and Mayfield Garden closer to the sector's other edge. Sector 39 and Sector 40 are the immediate neighbours, and Sushant Lok 1 and South City 1 are close enough that many tutors treat the whole run as one working area.

For scheduling this is mostly good news. A tutor with an existing Thursday commitment in Sushant Lok 1 can add a Sector 38 family at a sensible hour without a long drive between them, which is why evening slots here are usually easier to fill than in the outer sectors.

The complication is gate access. The larger complexes on this side run visitor registration, and a tutor who has not been pre-registered can lose fifteen minutes at the boundary. Families who send the tutor's details to their facility desk in advance simply do not have that problem, and it is worth doing once at the start rather than every week.

Weekend availability is the real constraint. Saturday mornings across Sector 38 and Sector 39 are the most requested slots of the week and they close early in the term.

Immediate neighbours: Sector 39 and Sector 40
Shared tutor corridor with Sushant Lok 1 and South City 1

Saturday morning slots fill first each term

contentBlocks.heading: At the dining table, or on a screen after nine
contentBlocks.body:
Both formats work. They fail in different ways, and knowing which failure you are more exposed to is the useful part.

A tutor sitting at your table can see the student's page, catch a wrong method at the moment it is written, and cannot be quietly ignored while a phone sits under the desk. Attendance is more visible to the parent. Against that, you are restricted to people who can physically reach Sector 38 in the window you need, and for a niche subject that restriction is expensive in quality even when it is free in rupees.

Online removes the geography. It opens up specialists who would never drive here, allows sessions late in the evening after a working parent gets home, and makes recordings possible so revision can revisit a difficult explanation. It also asks more of the student's self-discipline. A fourteen-year-old who drifts in class will drift faster on a screen.

One practical note specific to written subjects. Online sessions work far better when the family can scan or photograph the student's written work and share it before the session starts, so the tutor arrives having already seen the errors instead of discovering them live.

Availability in either format depends on the subject and the tutor's own schedule.
items: Home: visible attendance, immediate correction of method
Home: narrow pool for niche subjects
Online: specialist access, late slots, recorded explanations
Online: demands more self-discipline from the student
Share scanned written work before an online session

The reason it matters is that these schools do not all follow the same board, and some run different boards in different departments. A neighbour's recommendation is therefore only useful once you have checked that the neighbour's child sits the same papers as yours. Families in Sector 38 pass tutor contacts around constantly, and this is the step that gets skipped.

School internal calendars matter too. Mock weeks, submission deadlines for any coursework component, and school-set revision schedules all pull on the same evenings tutoring wants. A tutor who asks for the school's term calendar in the first week is planning around it. One who never asks will collide with it in February.

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a name reaches you
contentBlocks.body:
Screening on this platform covers identity, credentials and subject competence, and it is worth being exact about the boundaries of each.

Identity is matched against government photo identification. Credentials means qualification evidence relevant to the subject, plus a teaching history with places and durations that can be described specifically rather than in vague ranges. Subject competence is judged in a structured conversation with somebody who knows the material, and for IGCSE that conversation includes which board and which components the tutor has most recently prepared candidates for.

A tutor who describes the papers of a specification they claim to teach in loose, generic terms does not progress. That single question filters more applicants than any document check.

What screening cannot do is guarantee fit. Temperament, pace and the way a person handles a student who has stopped trying are things you only observe in a room. That is precisely why the trial session exists and why changing tutor early is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint.

Parent feedback from the first few weeks feeds back into whether a tutor continues to be put forward for that subject and level around Sector 38 and the neighbouring sectors.
items: Government photo identification matched
Qualification evidence tied to the subject taught
Teaching history stated with places and durations
Board-specific component knowledge tested in conversation
Fit is judged in the trial, not on paper

contentBlocks.heading: The questions that make a weak tutor uncomfortable
contentBlocks.body:
Four questions, asked early, will tell you more than a month of sessions.

What is my child losing marks on, specifically? A good answer names an assessment objective or a question type. A poor answer says concepts are weak.

Show me how you marked this. You want to see a mark scheme, or at least reasoning tied to what earns credit. Marking by impression is the commonest failure among otherwise capable tutors, and it produces students who feel encouraged and score the same.

What do you expect to see in four weeks? Any answer involving a guaranteed grade is a red flag. We do not promise outcomes and no honest tutor will. The exam is written by a teenager on one morning, and nobody controls that morning. What can be described is process and observable change: fewer method errors, faster starts, cleaner structure in extended answers.

And finally, what would make you tell me this is not working? A tutor willing to name that in advance is one who will actually say it later.

Fees are quoted before the trial, vary with subject, level and format, and are not the place to economise on a specialist paper.
items: Name the assessment objective, not a vague weakness
Marking shown against a scheme, not by impression
Four-week expectations stated as observable change
No grade promises, from us or from any tutor
Fees quoted upfront and vary by subject and format

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging a trial with IGCSE tutors in Sector 38 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Send an advisor four things and the rest is quick: the board, the subjects, the year group, and the evenings that survive after school buses and activities. Add a photograph of a recently marked script if you can find one, because it shortens the diagnosis considerably.

What comes back is a short set of names with their board history and slot times they can realistically keep, given where they are travelling from. Availability depends on the subject and on tutor schedules, and the specialist subjects take longer to fill than Mathematics does.

Use the trial session as a test rather than a formality. Ask for written findings afterwards, compare those findings against the four questions above, and say plainly if something is missing.

One caution worth stating. Comparing carefully takes a week or two, and in November of an examination year those weeks are expensive. If you are already close to a series, pick quickly on board experience alone and refine later. Careful comparison is a luxury of starting early.

There is no obligation attached to the trial. If the findings do not convince you, say so and ask for a different name rather than settling because the paperwork felt done. Most families in Sector 38 who end up happy changed something after the first attempt.
items: Share board, subjects, year group and free evenings
Attach a recently marked script if available
Names arrive with board history and holdable slots
Treat the trial as a test, ask for written findings
Close to a series, choose fast on board experience

faqs.question: Both tutors I shortlisted seem good. What is the single best tie-breaker?
faqs.answer: Ask each one, separately, to walk you through the components of the exact papers your child will sit and say where students most often drop marks in each. The person who has prepared candidates for that specification recently will answer in specifics and will probably volunteer a detail you did not know. The other will talk about building strong fundamentals. That distinction predicts the next six months better than qualifications, fees or years of experience do. If both answer well, choose the one your child spoke more freely with during the trial.

faqs.question: Is it rude to ask a tutor for their marking to be shown against a mark scheme?
faqs.answer: No, and a competent tutor expects it. Published mark schemes exist precisely so that credit is awarded for identifiable things rather than for general quality of effort. When a tutor marks by impression, students receive encouraging feedback and then find the examiner disagrees with them in June. Asking to see one marked script with the scheme alongside is a normal request. If it produces defensiveness rather than a page of annotations, you have learned something useful about how the sessions will run.

faqs.question: We are in The Magnolias. Do tutors have trouble getting through the gate?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is entirely avoidable. The larger complexes on this side of Sector 38 run visitor registration at the boundary, and a tutor arriving unannounced can lose a chunk of the session waiting for a call to go through to your flat. Send the tutor's name, number and expected slot to your facility desk once at the start of the arrangement and ask for a standing entry. Families who do this never think about it again. Those who do not tend to raise it in week three, having already lost time.

faqs.question: My daughter takes Economics. Why is a specialist harder to arrange than for Physics?
faqs.answer: Simple supply. Many more people can teach Physics to this level than can teach IGCSE Economics well, particularly the evaluation writing that separates the top band from a solid middle grade. That narrows the pool around Sector 38 considerably, and it is a subject where insisting on somebody who can drive to your building often means accepting weaker subject depth. Online is frequently the better trade for Economics, Business and Computer Science, while Mathematics and the sciences can usually be matched locally. Availability still depends on tutor schedules.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should we book to begin with?
faqs.answer: For one subject, start with a single weekly session plus set work, and review after a month. Two sessions a week make sense when a student is behind on content rather than on technique, or in the term immediately before a series. Booking heavily from day one usually backfires: the student is already carrying school work, and an overloaded week produces attendance that quietly collapses by February. It is easier to add a session later than to cut one without the student reading it as a verdict on their progress.

faqs.question: What if my child gets on well with the tutor but the marks stay flat?
faqs.answer: That is the most common version of this problem and the hardest to act on, because nobody wants to disrupt a comfortable arrangement. Give it four to six weeks, then ask the tutor for evidence rather than reassurance: marked scripts, a record of what was set and returned, and a specific account of what changed. If the answer is warm but unevidenced, ask for a different approach or a different tutor. Enjoying the sessions is necessary and not sufficient. Changing tutor can be requested at any point.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach two siblings together in the same session?
faqs.answer: It works when the two are in the same subject, close in level and genuinely willing to be corrected in front of each other. It works badly across different year groups, where one ends up idle for half the hour, and it works badly when one sibling is noticeably stronger, because the weaker one stops attempting anything. If the aim is to reduce cost, a shorter individual session usually beats a longer shared one. Discuss it with the advisor before booking, since arrangements and fees differ for paired sessions.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to see my child's school notes and worksheets?
faqs.answer: Yes, and early. School-issued booklets tell the tutor which textbook and which case studies the department has chosen, how the teacher phrases things, and which topics have already been covered. Working against that rather than alongside it confuses students, especially in subjects such as History and Business where schools select their own material. Sharing the term calendar and mock dates in the first week matters just as much, so that revision is planned around school assessments instead of colliding with them.

faqs.question: Do you offer group classes near Sector 38 or only one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Arrangements here are built around individual matching, because the whole comparison method described on this page depends on a tutor diagnosing one student's specific pattern of lost marks. A small group can work for revision of a shared topic close to a series, where the content is the same for everyone in the room. It works less well for the diagnostic phase. If a group format is what you want, say so when you enquire and the advisor will tell you what is realistically available in your subject.
