contentBlocks.heading: What tutoring will not fix for a Sector 77, Gurugram student
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor cannot create time that the week does not contain. If a Grade 10 student has school until four, an activity three evenings a week and two hours of homework, adding four tutoring hours on top produces a tired child rather than a better result. Something has to be removed first, and that decision belongs to the parent.

Starting late limits the outcome. A student who begins in January for a May-June series can usually repair technique, exam timing and one or two weak topics. Rebuilding two years of shaky foundations in a subject like Physics inside four months is not realistic, and anyone promising otherwise is selling something.

No grade is guaranteed here. No score, no percentage improvement, no promise about a particular result. What can be described is process: what the first session covers, how the plan is written, how progress is reviewed, and what you should be seeing after four weeks.

After a month, expect the student to attempt a past paper question without asking where to begin, to use command words correctly, and to be able to explain one topic they previously avoided. If none of that has shifted, the match is wrong and the honest step is to change it rather than wait.
items: Adding hours without removing any rarely works
Late starts repair technique, not foundations
No grade, score or percentage promises
Four-week markers: independent attempts, command words, one recovered topic
Changing a tutor early costs less than waiting

contentBlocks.heading: Speaking to an advisor about IGCSE tutors in Sector 77 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Send four things and the conversation moves quickly: the board your school follows, the subjects you want covered, the grade and tier, and the two evenings that are genuinely free once school transport and activities are subtracted. If you already know the exam series being targeted, add it. If you do not, an advisor will help you work backwards from it.

What comes back is two or three names with the reasoning behind each, including where a candidate is a weaker fit for your particular case. Nobody benefits from a shortlist presented as though every option were equal. A first session is then arranged subject to tutor availability, usually as a diagnostic hour built around a recent school test or a past paper rather than a general introduction.

After that first session, ask for the six-week plan in writing. It should name the topics, the papers to be attempted and roughly when marked work will come back. Then review at the four-week mark against the markers described above. If the fit is wrong, say so then. Sector 77 families who treat the first month as a trial rather than a commitment tend to end the year with the right tutor.
items: Share board, subject, grade and tier
Name the evenings that are actually free
Two or three suggestions with reasoning
First session arranged subject to availability

faqs.question: Our school follows Cambridge. Does that rule out a tutor who has mostly taught Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but it should be raised in the first conversation. The physics and the algebra are common ground; the paper structure, the tiering and the mark scheme language are not. A tutor who has taught Edexcel for years and Cambridge occasionally can be a strong fit for a Grade 9 student with time to spare. For a Grade 10 student sitting papers in five months, ask directly which Cambridge syllabus they last prepared students for and in which series. If the answer is vague, keep looking.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can a tutor realistically reach Godrej Air or Vatika India Next?
faqs.answer: Tutors already working inside the New Gurgaon sectors can usually manage a 7pm or 7.30pm start without difficulty. Someone travelling in from Golf Course Road or the DLF phases will find the same slot much harder on a weekday, and the sessions that get cancelled first are the ones that were always marginal. If your only free window is late, ask specifically for a tutor based nearby, or plan that subject online. Availability depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed once the timetable settles.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Sector 77 actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Four things mostly. The subject, because Additional Mathematics or a science with a practical component draws from a smaller pool than general English. The tier and grade, since Grade 10 Extended work is more demanding to prepare than Grade 9 revision. The mode, as home visits carry travel time that online sessions do not. And the frequency, because a twice-weekly commitment is priced differently from occasional pre-mock support. An advisor will give you a range for your combination rather than a single number.

faqs.question: My son has been entered for Core maths. Can he move to Extended?
faqs.answer: That is a school decision with a deadline attached, not a tutoring decision, so speak to the maths coordinator first. Schools generally look at recent internal marks before agreeing to move a student up, because the Extended paper assumes topics the Core route treats lightly. Tutoring can build the case by covering the gap over a term and producing evidence in school assessments. Leave it too close to entry deadlines and the answer becomes no regardless of ability, so raise it early in Grade 10 rather than late.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring workable for a subject with a practical component?
faqs.answer: For the alternative-to-practical written route, yes, comfortably, because that paper tests reading apparatus diagrams, tabulating results, spotting sources of error and drawing conclusions from given data. All of that transfers well to a shared screen. For a laboratory practical test, online tutoring can cover technique, expected observations and recording conventions, but it cannot replace bench time in the school lab. Confirm with the school which route your child is entered for, then decide the mode around that rather than the other way round.

faqs.question: We only need support for the November series. Is a short engagement possible?
faqs.answer: Yes. Short engagements are common for resits, for a single weak subject, or for a student who missed a term through illness or relocation. Say clearly at the start that the arrangement is time-bound so the tutor plans backwards from the paper date rather than teaching at a general pace. Six to ten weeks is usually enough to fix exam technique and two or three topics. It is not enough to cover a subject that was never properly taught, and a good tutor will tell you that in week one.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see four weeks after starting?
faqs.answer: Three observable changes. Your child should begin a past paper question without asking where to start. Answers should show command word discipline, so a question asking for an explanation gets reasoning rather than a definition. And there should be at least one topic previously avoided that can now be explained aloud. Marks may not have moved yet, particularly if the next school test falls outside the topics covered. If none of those three things has shifted, raise it rather than waiting for the term to end.

faqs.question: The first tutor is not working out. What happens then?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor what specifically is not working, because the reason changes the replacement. Pace too fast, no marked work coming back, sessions turning into lectures, repeated rescheduling, or simply no rapport all point to different second choices. A replacement is arranged from the same shortlist process, subject to tutor availability. Families who raise this in week three usually lose a fortnight. Families who wait until the mock results arrive lose most of a term, which is a much harder position to recover from before the exam series.

faqs.question: Do you arrange help for Grade 9, or only for the exam year?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 is arguably the better time to start. The syllabus for most two-year IGCSE courses begins there, and the topics introduced in Grade 9 are the ones students are weakest on by the time mocks arrive, simply because they were learned longest ago. Starting early also allows a lighter schedule, often one session a week rather than two, which is easier to sustain alongside activities. Support can equally be arranged for younger students working towards Lower Secondary checkpoints, depending on tutor availability.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 78, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Most enquiries begin with four words: we need a tutor. The useful version carries five more pieces of information, and this page sets out what those are for a family in Sector 78 before moving on to how a shortlist gets built and what a first session should look like.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 78 Gurugram are matched most accurately once five facts are on the table: the board the school enters students for, the tier within that subject, the exam series being targeted, which components apply including any practical or coursework route, and the child's current grade on the school's own reporting scale. contentBlocks.heading: Five things to establish before booking a tutor in Sector 78, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
An enquiry that says "my daughter needs help with IGCSE science" is honest but almost unusable. Science across two boards and two tiers covers a dozen different preparation routes, and the tutor who suits one of them can be actively wrong for another.

So before any names are discussed, gather five facts. One: the board, meaning Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Two: the tier your child has been entered for within each subject, since the lower tier carries a hard ceiling on the grade available. Three: the exam series, because a November sitting and a May-June sitting produce completely different plans from the same starting point. Four: which components apply, particularly whether a science subject follows a laboratory practical route or a written alternative. Five: the current grade the school is reporting, not the grade you hope for.

The school office or the subject coordinator can supply the first four in one email. The fifth sits on the last report card.

Parents in Sector 78 who arrive with all five typically have a tutor in place inside a week. Parents who arrive with none usually lose a fortnight to clarification, and a fortnight in Grade 10 is not free.
items: Board: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel
Tier within each subject, and the grade ceiling it carries
Target exam series and the entry deadline behind it
Practical route, alternative-to-practical or coursework component
Current reported grade, not the target

contentBlocks.heading: Boards and tiers: what the school has already decided for you
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a two-year IGCSE course, both feed into an international A Level route, and both look similar in a prospectus. The differences that matter to a tutor sit lower down.

Cambridge tiers most of its popular syllabuses into Core and Extended. Core covers less content and caps the achievable grade some way below the top; Extended goes further and opens the full range. Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher on subjects such as International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, with a comparable ceiling on the Foundation route. In both systems the school makes the entry decision, usually during Grade 10, and usually on the basis of internal assessment marks.

Grading adds a second layer of confusion. Certain IGCSE subjects report on a 9 to 1 scale while others still use A* to G, and the mapping between them is not intuitive. A parent reading a 6 alongside an older sibling's B is not comparing like with like.

Series dates are the third piece. Cambridge examines in June and November, with a March series available in India for a limited set of syllabuses. Edexcel adds a January window. Entries close months earlier, so a change of tier is a school conversation with a calendar attached.

Lower tiers carry a fixed grade ceiling
9 to 1 and A* to G both still appear on IGCSE certificates
June, November, a limited March series in India, and Edexcel's January
Tier changes are decided by the school, not by the tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 78, Gurugram sits, and why that changes the shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 78 falls in the middle of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, with Sector 77 and Sector 76 on one flank and Sector 79 and Sector 80 on the other. It is a comfortable belt to live in and a slightly awkward one to tutor across, because the density of experienced IGCSE subject teachers is still concentrated in the older parts of the city.

What that produces in practice is a two-speed shortlist. General subjects, Grade 9 support and mathematics up to the middle of the syllabus draw plenty of nearby names. Narrower requests, meaning Additional Mathematics, Edexcel Chemistry or First Language English at the top end, often draw candidates who are not local at all.

Societies help where they can. Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next sit near enough to one another that a tutor already visiting one address can take a second booking the same evening, which makes consecutive slots easier to hold than isolated ones.

The Dwarka Expressway side opens the route towards Delhi and the newer sectors. Sohna Road connects downward. Both are usable for weekend sessions and unreliable between six and eight on a working evening.
items: Sector 76 and Sector 77 to one side, Sector 79 and Sector 80 to the other
Common subjects draw local names, narrow ones usually do not
Consecutive society bookings hold better than isolated slots
Dwarka Expressway and Sohna Road are weekend-friendly, weekday-difficult
Weekend mornings often the easiest slot to secure

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: the question to ask before the first session
contentBlocks.body:
For mathematics, ask which syllabus and which tier, then ask the tutor to describe the difference in their own words. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel Specification A overlap heavily in content and diverge in paper structure and phrasing. A tutor who cannot articulate that difference has not taught both recently.

For Physics, Chemistry and Biology, ask which practical route the school uses. Cambridge schools enter students either for a laboratory test or for the alternative-to-practical written paper, and preparation for those two is genuinely different work. Edexcel folds practical understanding into the written papers instead. Getting this wrong wastes a term of revision on the wrong skill.

For English, establish whether the child is entered for a first language syllabus or an English as a second language one. They are separate courses with separate assessment objectives, and a tutor strong in one can be mediocre in the other.

For Economics, Business Studies, Geography and History, the question is about marking rather than content. Ask how the tutor teaches command words: define, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate. Students in Sector 78 who lose marks in these subjects are usually writing accurate answers to a question they misread.
items: Maths: syllabus, tier, and can the tutor describe the difference
Sciences: laboratory test or alternative-to-practical written paper
English: first language and second language are separate syllabuses
Additional Mathematics for students heading to AS Level
Humanities: command word discipline decides the marks
ICT and Computer Science need someone who has marked the practical work

contentBlocks.heading: School timetables around Sector 78, Gurugram and the evening they leave
contentBlocks.body:
Families here send children out across the city rather than around the corner. Scottish High International School sits in Sector 57. Lancers International School is off Golf Course Road. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School lie towards the Sohna Road side. Bus routes to all of them are long.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named because they describe where Sector 78 students actually study.

A long bus route eats the evening from both ends. A child collected before seven in the morning and dropped after four is running on less than the timetable implies, and a 5pm tutoring slot often collides with the only hour that child had to do nothing. Push the first session to 6.30pm or 7pm and attendance improves noticeably.

Mock timing is the other school variable worth knowing. Internal mocks in most of these schools land in the months before the main series, and the four weeks around them are when tutoring hours are most valuable and most contested. Book that stretch early, because tutors fill it first and availability then depends on schedules already committed.
items: Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School
Later starts hold attendance better than 5pm slots
Pre-mock weeks book out first
Platform is independent, with no school affiliation

contentBlocks.heading: How the enquiry becomes two or three names
contentBlocks.body:
Once the five facts are in, matching is mechanical rather than mysterious.

The request is written up as a specification: board, syllabus, tier, series, components, current grade, target subjects and the evenings available. That specification goes against tutor records that carry syllabus-level detail, so a search for Edexcel Chemistry returns tutors who have prepared students for Edexcel Chemistry rather than tutors who list chemistry.

Two or three profiles come back, each with a short note explaining why it was suggested and where it is weaker. A tutor might be excellent on content and only free on Saturdays. Another might be local and available but stronger in Grade 9 than Grade 10 work. Both are worth seeing, and neither should be presented as flawless.

A first session is then arranged, subject to tutor availability. It works best as a diagnostic hour: a recent school test or a past paper section attempted while the tutor watches, followed by a plain description of what the next six weeks will cover.

Ask for that plan in writing. Families in Sector 78 who do tend to get a sharper second month, because the plan makes drift visible.
items: Request written up as a syllabus-level specification
Matched on syllabus experience, not subject name
Two or three profiles, each with a stated weakness
Diagnostic first session on real marked work
Written six-week plan requested at the end of it

contentBlocks.heading: A nearby home tutor or a stronger specialist online
contentBlocks.body:
This is the trade-off almost every family here reaches, and there is no universal answer.

Home tutoring wins on supervision. A student who drifts within four minutes of being left alone, or whose real problem is that nothing gets started, benefits from someone physically present. It also wins on the small things: the school folder is there, the marked script is there, the parent can hear how the hour is going without asking.

Online wins on depth. Restricting a search to tutors willing to drive into the New Gurgaon sectors on a Wednesday evening narrows the field sharply, and for a narrow subject that narrowing can cost you the person who actually knows the paper. Online sessions also return marked work faster, since a photographed script can be annotated the same night.

Online does not fix motivation. If the student will not open the book, a screen makes that easier to hide, not harder.

Most Sector 78 families land on a mix by the second term, with the supervision-heavy subject at home and the specialist subject online. Modes can be reviewed once the timetable settles and can change mid-year without starting over.
items: Home tutoring for supervision and organisation
Online for narrow subjects and faster marking
Neither mode fixes an unwilling student
Mixed weeks are common by the second term
Mode is reviewable, not a permanent decision

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, value and what nobody can promise in Sector 78, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Fees depend on four variables and any quote that ignores them is guesswork. The subject matters, because Additional Mathematics or a top-tier science draws from a smaller pool than general English. The grade and tier matter, since Grade 10 Extended preparation is harder to deliver than Grade 9 consolidation. The mode matters, as a home visit carries travel time that an online hour does not. And the frequency matters, because a sustained twice-weekly arrangement prices differently from six weeks of pre-mock work.

Ask for a range against your specific combination, and ask what is included: marking between sessions, past paper supply, a written plan, contact with the parent. Two tutors at the same hourly figure can differ enormously on those.

Now the part that is less comfortable. No grade is promised on this platform. No score, no percentage improvement, no claim about a particular result in a particular series. Anyone offering that is describing a sales position rather than an academic one.

What can be committed to is process, and process is checkable. You should see a plan, marked work returning, and a student who begins questions without asking where to start. If those are absent after a month, the arrangement is not working.
items: Fees vary by subject, tier, mode and frequency
Ask what marking and planning are included in the hour
No grade, score or improvement percentage is promised
Process commitments are checkable, outcome promises are not
One month is enough to judge whether it is working

contentBlocks.heading: What the checks cover, and the three weeks that tell you the rest
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shared, identity is verified and teaching history is confirmed. Where a tutor claims IGCSE experience the claim is examined at syllabus level: which board, which tier, which components, which series they last prepared students for and what those students were working towards. General answers get followed up. A tutor who says they have taught IGCSE physics for years but cannot say whether their students sat the practical test or the written alternative is describing something older or vaguer than they suggest.

Subject depth is checked by asking how a common misconception would be handled, and by asking the candidate to mark a sample answer. Generous marking is a warning sign. An examiner does not award marks for effort, and neither should a tutor preparing a student for one.

What none of this establishes is fit. Screening cannot tell you whether a particular adult will hold your particular teenager's attention on a Thursday evening in August, and it cannot forecast reliability across a monsoon.

That becomes visible in weeks two and three. So treat the first month as a trial, say something the moment it feels wrong, and expect the arrangement to remain reviewable rather than fixed.
items: Identity and teaching history verified before sharing a profile
Syllabus claims probed by board, tier and component
Sample marking used to test examiner discipline
Fit and reliability only show up in weeks two and three
First month treated as a trial by default

contentBlocks.heading: Getting a shortlist for IGCSE tutors in Sector 78 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start by collecting the five facts. Email the class teacher or subject coordinator for the board, the tier, the series and the component route if you are not sure, then take the current grade from the last report. That email usually comes back within a day and saves a fortnight later.

Then send the specification along with the evenings that are genuinely free, the society or address for home sessions, and whether you are open to online for at least one subject. Say plainly if the budget has a ceiling; it changes which suggestions are sensible rather than which are possible.

An advisor will return two or three profiles with reasoning attached and the weaker points stated. A first session can be arranged after that, subject to tutor availability, and is best used diagnostically rather than as an introduction.

Set a review date four weeks out at the same time you set the first session. Put it in the calendar. Families in Sector 78 who plan the review in advance change course early when they need to, and the ones who do not tend to discover the problem after the mock results arrive, which is a far harder place to start from.
items: Email the school for board, tier, series and components
Take the current grade from the last report card
Send free evenings, address and openness to online
State any budget ceiling up front
Diarise a four-week review before the first session happens

faqs.question: The school has not told us which board they follow. How do we find out quickly?
faqs.answer: One email to the class teacher or the examinations coordinator settles it, and it is a routine question that offices answer within a day. Ask for the board, the syllabus name for each subject, the tier your child has been entered for and the series being targeted. If the subject teacher replies directly, also ask which practical route applies for the sciences. Keep that reply; a tutor will ask for exactly the same details in the first conversation, and having it in writing prevents second-hand confusion later.

faqs.question: My daughter is on the Foundation tier for maths. Is a top grade still possible?
faqs.answer: Not on that tier, and it is better to know now. Lower tiers on both Cambridge and Edexcel carry a fixed ceiling on the grade available, which is exactly why tier is one of the five facts to establish before booking. What is possible is a move to the higher tier, but that is a school decision taken on internal assessment evidence and bounded by entry deadlines. Tutoring can build the evidence over a term. Raise it early in Grade 10 rather than after the mocks.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three subjects, or do we need separate people?
faqs.answer: Two related subjects are often workable, for example Physics with Mathematics, or Economics with Business Studies. Three is usually a stretch at Grade 10 level, because depth at the top of each syllabus is where the marks actually sit. A tutor stretched across three subjects tends to be strong in one and adequate in the others. If budget is the reason for asking, a better use of the same hours is one specialist for the weakest subject and school support for the rest.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do families in Sector 78 usually arrange?
faqs.answer: Two hours a week per subject is the common pattern in Grade 10, often as two separate hours rather than one long block, because retention is better across two contacts. Grade 9 students frequently manage on one. The number rises in the weeks before mocks and before the main series, then drops again. What matters more than frequency is whether the sessions are actually kept. Three booked hours with one regularly cancelled is worse than two that always happen.

faqs.question: We are moving to Gurugram mid-year from another city. Does that complicate things?
faqs.answer: It complicates the syllabus alignment more than the tutoring. If the previous school followed a different board, some topics will have been covered in a different order and a few may not have been covered at all. The first task is a gap audit against the new school's syllabus, which a diagnostic session can produce quickly. Ask the new school for the scheme of work so the tutor can map what is missing. Expect the first month to be catching up rather than deepening.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who teaches at one of the local international schools make a better choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth less than parents assume. A serving teacher knows the internal calendar, the mock timing and the house style of assessment, all of which help with planning. But knowing a school is not the same as knowing a syllabus deeply, and current teaching commitments often make availability poor and cancellations frequent. Judge on syllabus fluency, marking discipline and whether the slot will actually be kept. School familiarity is a tiebreaker rather than a reason on its own.

faqs.question: What if we book a tutor and the school changes my son's tier afterwards?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor immediately, because the plan should change with it. A move from the lower tier to the higher one adds topics that the previous plan may have skipped entirely, and the pace has to lift to cover them before the series. A move downward changes the priority towards securing the achievable range rather than chasing the top of the paper. Either way it is a replanning conversation, not a reason to change tutors, unless the tutor is only comfortable at one level.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions easier to arrange here than weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and it is one of the few real advantages of living in this belt. Saturday and Sunday mornings avoid the weekday evening congestion on the Dwarka Expressway and Sohna Road approaches, which widens the pool of tutors willing to travel to Sector 78 and makes longer double sessions practical. The trade-off is that weekend slots fill early, particularly before mocks. If weekends suit your family, ask for them at the enquiry stage rather than after a weekday arrangement has failed.

faqs.question: How do we know progress is real and not just a tutor being encouraging?
faqs.answer: Look at marked work rather than at reports of how the session went. Ask for past paper sections marked to the mark scheme, with the marks written on, and keep them. Over a month a genuine improvement shows as fewer marks lost to method and structure rather than as a general sense of confidence. Also watch how questions are started. A student who reads a question and begins without asking what to do has changed something real, and that change usually precedes the marks.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 79, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Families in this part of New Gurgaon lose more time to four wrong assumptions than to any shortage of tutors. This page takes each one apart, then explains how Cambridge and Edexcel papers are actually marked and what a first month of tutoring should produce.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 79 Gurugram are most often hired on a false premise: that IGCSE is simply a harder Class 10 board, so any strong school teacher will transfer across. The content overlaps, certainly. The assessment does not. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel award marks against published mark schemes built on command words, tier the entry so the achievable grade differs before a student writes anything, and split several subjects into components a general teacher may never have prepared. That gap is where a term usually goes.

contentBlocks.heading: The assumption that costs Sector 79, Gurugram families a term
contentBlocks.body:
The most common opening line in an enquiry from this part of the city is some version of: he is bright, he just needs a good teacher for Class 10. The intention is fine. The premise is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that shows up around the first mock.

IGCSE overlaps heavily with a national board on content. Quadratic equations are quadratic equations. Where it separates is in how marks are awarded. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel publish mark schemes that reward specific things in a specific order, and questions are built around command words that carry defined expectations. Describe wants observation. Explain wants a reason. Evaluate wants a judgement supported on both sides. A student who writes a good essay in answer to a question asking for two points will be marked down without ever being told why.

Then there is tiering, which decides the ceiling before the paper is opened.

A teacher who has spent a decade with a different examination system may know the subject better than the tutor you eventually hire. But knowing the subject and knowing how this examination pays out are separate skills, and for a Grade 10 student the second one is what buys marks.
items: Content overlaps, assessment does not
Command words carry defined mark scheme expectations
Tier fixes the grade ceiling before the exam
Subject knowledge and examination fluency are separate skills
The gap usually surfaces at the first mock

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 79, Gurugram and the belt running out to Sector 81
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 79 sits towards the outer end of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, with Sector 78 and Sector 77 behind it and Sector 80 and Sector 81 continuing outward. Being further along that belt has one practical consequence: tutors travelling from the older, denser parts of Gurugram treat it as a longer trip than Sector 77, and they price and schedule accordingly.

So the second wrong assumption follows quickly, which is that a local tutor will always be found. For a Grade 9 mathematics request, usually yes. For Additional Mathematics or a top-tier science, often no, and holding out for a nearby name can cost six weeks that the student did not have.

What does work here is clustering. Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next are close enough that a tutor already teaching in one of them will take a second booking the same evening, so ask whether a slot exists next to an appointment the tutor already keeps.

Dwarka Expressway carries traffic from the Delhi side. Sohna Road runs down towards Vatika Chowk and Sector 49. Both are usable, and both are considerably less predictable between six and eight on a working evening.
items: Sector 78 and Sector 77 behind, Sector 80 and Sector 81 further out
Longer perceived trip than the inner sectors
Ask for a slot adjacent to a booking the tutor already holds
Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella, Vatika India Next cluster well
Weekday six to eight is the least reliable window

contentBlocks.heading: A tutor in the house is not automatically the better tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Assumption three is that physical presence equals quality. It does not. Presence buys supervision, and supervision is genuinely valuable for a student who cannot start work alone or who quietly does nothing for forty minutes. If that describes your child, book at home and accept the smaller pool.

For everyone else the calculation runs the other way. Insisting on a tutor who will drive to Sector 79 on a Wednesday evening removes most of the specialists from consideration before the search begins. Online sessions bring back the person who has actually prepared students for the exact paper your child is sitting, and marked work returns faster because a photographed script can be annotated the same night rather than waiting for the next visit.

There is a limitation worth stating. Online sessions make it easier for a disengaged student to appear present while doing nothing, and a laboratory practical test cannot be rehearsed over a screen, only discussed.

Most families in this belt end up mixing the two by the second term. Home for the subject that needs watching, online for the subject that needs expertise. Availability for either depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed once a routine exists.
items: Presence buys supervision, not subject depth
Insisting on local removes most specialists from the search
Photographed scripts marked between sessions
Laboratory practical technique cannot be rehearsed online
Mixed weeks are normal by the second term

contentBlocks.heading: Where marks actually go missing, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
In mathematics, marks are lost to method rather than to answers. Both Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A award method marks along the way, so a student who writes only a final answer and gets it wrong scores nothing, while a student who shows working and slips at the last step keeps most of the marks. Training that habit is worth more early on than covering extra topics.

In the sciences, marks go to precision of language. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 want observations stated exactly, variables controlled explicitly and conclusions tied to the data given. Whether the school enters students for a laboratory practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper changes what needs rehearsing, so confirm that before the syllabus is planned.

In English, the loss is structural. Students write fluently and answer a slightly different question from the one asked.

In ICT and Computer Science, marks disappear in the practical work, where a task done correctly but saved or presented against the wrong instruction earns nothing. Humanities subjects come down to command words again, and to the discipline of answering the question that carries eight marks with eight marks worth of material.
items: Maths: method marks are lost by not showing working
Sciences: exact language, controlled variables, data-linked conclusions
Confirm laboratory test or written alternative before planning
English: fluent answers to the wrong question
ICT practical work: instructions followed literally or not at all
Humanities: mark allocation should dictate answer length

contentBlocks.heading: What a request from Sector 79, Gurugram is matched against
contentBlocks.body:
A request is turned into a specification before anyone looks for a name. That specification carries the board, the syllabus, the tier, the components in play, the exam series being targeted, the grade currently being reported by the school, and the evenings the family can actually protect once school transport and activities are removed.

That last item is the one families understate, and understating it produces a shortlist that collapses in week three.

Matching then runs against tutor records held at syllabus level rather than subject level. A request for Edexcel Biology returns tutors who have prepared students for Edexcel Biology, not everyone who lists biology. Two or three profiles are shared with the reasoning written out, including what is weak about each. A candidate might be strong on the syllabus and only free on Sunday. Another might live twenty minutes away and be better suited to Grade 9 than to Grade 10.

A first session is arranged after that, subject to tutor availability, and is best spent diagnostically. Give the tutor a recent school test and let them watch it being attempted. What comes out of that hour should be a plain description of the next six weeks, ideally written down.
items: Specification built before names are searched
Protected evenings recorded honestly, not optimistically
Tutor records matched at syllabus level
Profiles shared with stated weaknesses
Diagnostic first hour on a real school test

contentBlocks.heading: Extended is not always the right entry, and Core is not a failure
contentBlocks.body:
The fourth assumption is that the higher tier is always worth chasing. Cambridge splits many syllabuses into Core and Extended, Edexcel into Foundation and Higher, and parents often push for the upper route on principle.

Sometimes that is right. A student comfortably in the middle of the class who is being held back by patchy technique usually belongs on the higher tier and will be under-served on the lower one, because the ceiling is fixed and no amount of good work lifts it.

Sometimes it is wrong. A student genuinely struggling with the fundamentals may score better on the lower tier, where the questions sit within reach, than on a higher paper where half the marks are unavailable to them in practice. Schools make this call on internal assessment evidence, and they make it during Grade 10 against entry deadlines that sit months before the papers.

The series matter too. Cambridge examines in June and November, with a March series available in India for a limited set of syllabuses; Edexcel adds a January window, which is useful for resits or for splitting a heavy subject load across two sittings. Any of that is a school conversation, and the earlier it happens the more options remain open.
items: Cambridge Core and Extended, Edexcel Foundation and Higher
Lower tier caps the grade regardless of performance
Higher tier can lower a struggling student's actual score
School decides on internal evidence, before entry deadlines
June, November, limited March in India, Edexcel January

The scheduling consequence is blunt. There is a second consequence, less obvious. contentBlocks.heading: A long CV is weak evidence of IGCSE marking discipline
contentBlocks.body:
Screening starts with what can be confirmed: identity, and teaching history that stands up when checked. Then it moves to the part that matters more, which is whether the claimed IGCSE experience is real and recent.

The useful questions are narrow. Which board. Which tier. Which components did the last cohort sit. Was that the practical test or the written alternative. Which series, and what were the students working towards afterwards. A tutor with genuine recent experience answers these in a sentence each. A tutor who has taught the subject broadly and the examination rarely will generalise, and generalising is the signal.

Candidates are also asked to mark a sample answer. This is where long CVs come apart. Marking generously feels kind and produces a student who is confident until the results arrive. An examiner awards what the mark scheme allows and nothing else, and a tutor preparing a student for that examination has to work the same way.

None of this predicts rapport, punctuality through a Gurugram monsoon, or whether the tutor will still be free in March. Those emerge in weeks two and three, which is why the arrangement stays reviewable and why early feedback is worth giving.
items: Identity and teaching history confirmed first
Board, tier, component and series asked specifically
Vague answers treated as the warning they are
Sample marking tests examiner discipline, not kindness
Rapport and reliability judged in weeks two and three

contentBlocks.heading: What a tutor can and cannot change for a Sector 79, Gurugram student
contentBlocks.body:
Start with what tutoring genuinely moves. Examination technique responds quickly, often within a month. Command word discipline, showing working, allocating answer length to mark allocation, reading the question twice: these are habits, and habits change faster than understanding does. Two or three specific weak topics can also be rebuilt in a term.

Now the limits. A student who has not understood the first year of a two-year course cannot be brought to the top of the paper in eight weeks, and any tutor suggesting otherwise is describing a sale. Adding tutoring hours to a week that is already full produces exhaustion rather than marks; something has to come out first, and that is a parent's decision rather than a tutor's.

No grade is promised here. No score, no percentage improvement, no claim about a result in a particular series.

What is offered instead is a process you can check. After four weeks, expect your child to begin unfamiliar questions without asking where to start, to use command words correctly, and to explain one topic they previously avoided. If none of that has shifted, the match is wrong. Saying so in week four is far cheaper than discovering it after the mocks.
items: Technique and habits move within a month
Two or three weak topics can be rebuilt in a term
Two years of missing foundations cannot be fixed in eight weeks
No grade, score or improvement percentage is promised
Four-week markers: independent starts, command words, one recovered topic

contentBlocks.heading: Asking about IGCSE tutors in Sector 79 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Send the board, the subject list, the grade and tier, the series being targeted and the evenings you can genuinely protect. If any of that is unclear, one email to the subject coordinator settles it and is worth sending before the enquiry rather than after.

An advisor will come back with two or three names, the reasoning behind each and the point on which each is weaker. A first session can then be arranged subject to tutor availability. Use that hour diagnostically: hand over a recent test, let it be attempted, and ask at the end what the next six weeks will cover and in what order.

One last piece of advice, offered because it is the thing families here most often skip. Fix a review date four weeks out at the same moment you fix the first session, and hold it even if things seem fine. Four weeks is long enough to judge whether technique is shifting and short enough that changing course costs almost nothing. Families in Sector 79 who plan that review get to act on it. The ones who do not usually find out from a mock result.

Email the subject coordinator first if anything is unclear
Two or three names with reasoning and stated weak points
Use the first session diagnostically, not as an introduction
Fix the four-week review before the tutoring starts

faqs.question: My son topped his class in a different board last year. Why would he need an IGCSE tutor at all?
faqs.answer: He may not. But strong performance in one examination system does not transfer automatically, because the marks are awarded differently. Students moving across often write more than the question needs, skip the working that carries method marks, and answer command words loosely. That costs marks that have nothing to do with ability. A single diagnostic session on a past paper will show whether the gap is real. If it is not, you have spent one hour finding out rather than a term assuming.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring a tutor purely to teach exam technique rather than the subject?
faqs.answer: For a student who understands the content and underperforms on paper, yes, and it is often the highest value hour you will buy. The work is narrow: reading command words correctly, matching answer length to the marks available, showing method, managing time across a paper and checking what a question is genuinely asking. Six to eight sessions can shift that meaningfully. For a student who has not understood the material, technique work is decoration and the tutor should be spending the time elsewhere.

faqs.question: How far in advance should families in Sector 79 book before the mock exams?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks earlier than feels necessary. The weeks immediately before mocks are when demand across the New Gurgaon sectors peaks, so the tutors worth having are already committed, and the ones still free at short notice are free for a reason. Booking early also means the diagnostic session happens while there is still time to act on it. If you are reading this within a month of mocks, book anyway, but plan for narrower goals than a full syllabus review.

faqs.question: Can a student resit an IGCSE subject if the grade is disappointing?
faqs.answer: A subject can generally be entered again in a later series, but the rules on entry, timing and how results are reported vary by board and by what the school permits, so confirm the specifics with your examinations coordinator before planning around it. The more useful question is whether a resit serves the next step. If an A Level or IB offer depends on the grade, it can be worth it. If it does not, the same effort spent on the following year usually returns more.

faqs.question: We want help with only one topic my daughter has never understood. Is that too small a request?
faqs.answer: No, and narrowly scoped requests often work better than open-ended ones. Say clearly that the engagement is topic-limited so the tutor plans backwards from a specific outcome rather than settling into a weekly rhythm. Three to five sessions on a single stubborn topic, with a marked past paper question at the end to test whether it has actually landed, is a reasonable shape. If the diagnosis turns out to be broader than one topic, a good tutor will tell you in the first session.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know my child's specific school to be useful?
faqs.answer: It helps at the margins and is often overrated. Familiarity with a school's internal calendar and mock timing makes planning easier, and that is a genuine convenience. It tells you nothing about whether the tutor can mark to a Cambridge or Edexcel mark scheme, which is the skill the exam actually rewards. Because students here travel out to schools across the city, insisting on school familiarity also shrinks an already thin local pool. Weigh syllabus fluency first and school knowledge second.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first tutoring session, and should a parent sit in?
faqs.answer: The first session should be diagnostic. The tutor gives a recent school test or a past paper section, watches it being attempted, and identifies where marks are being lost rather than delivering a lesson. Sitting in for the first ten minutes is reasonable if it settles a younger student. Staying for the whole hour rarely helps, because most teenagers perform for the room rather than working. Ask for the findings and the six-week plan at the end instead, preferably in writing.

faqs.question: My daughter says she understands everything in the session but still scores badly. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always the difference between following an explanation and producing an answer alone under time pressure. Understanding while someone else drives is a much easier task than starting from a blank page. Ask the tutor to spend at least half of each session with your daughter attempting questions unaided while they watch and say nothing, then marking to the scheme. Sessions that are entirely explanation feel productive and produce exactly this pattern. It is one of the more common reasons for changing approach.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE tutors here able to help with school coursework or project components?
faqs.answer: Support with a coursework or project component is possible where the syllabus includes one, but it has to stay on the right side of a line. A tutor can teach the skills the component assesses, explain the assessment criteria, and discuss an approach. The work submitted must be the student's own, and schools require declarations to that effect. Check your school's policy on outside help before starting, because policies differ, and a component disqualified for authenticity is worse than one done imperfectly.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram for Core and Extended Papers
heroSubtitle: A report card that says predicted 6 and target 8 does not tell you what to fix. This page explains where IGCSE marks are usually lost, how a tutor shortlist gets built for families around Godrej Air and Vatika India Next, and what a first session should cover.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram are usually hired to close the distance between a school's predicted grade and the grade a student actually earns in the June or November series. That distance is rarely about ability. It comes from paper technique, a Core or Extended tier chosen without much discussion, and revision aimed at material already secure. IB Gram matches a student to a tutor by the specific component losing marks, then keeps the arrangement reviewable rather than locked in.

contentBlocks.heading: The gap between a predicted grade and a final grade in Sector 80 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents on this page started looking after a report, not before one. The predicted grade says 6. The target says 8. The subject teacher's comment runs to two lines and explains nothing about what the student would have to do differently.

Predicted grades come from evidence a school already holds: mocks, class tests, coursework drafts in the subjects that carry them. They are honest readings of current performance under something close to exam conditions. The final grade comes from a real series, marked by an examiner against a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel mark scheme, who has never met your child and cannot guess what a half-written method was meant to say.

So the gap is almost never about intelligence. It comes from three ordinary places. Paper technique that was never taught explicitly. A tier decision, Core or Extended, made quickly in Grade 9 and never revisited. And revision hours spent on topics the student already knows, because those are the comfortable ones.

Tutoring only closes that gap when it is aimed at the actual leak. A student who loses marks on structured questions in a theory paper needs something quite different from one who understands the content but runs out of time in the multiple-choice paper. On a report card, both of them look like a 6.
items: Predicted grade set from mocks and classwork
Final grade set by an external examiner and a mark scheme
Tier choice made in Grade 9, rarely reopened
Comfortable revision on already-secure topics
Timing failures mistaken for content gaps

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 80 Gurugram shortlist gets built, step by step
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist is only useful if it is short and the reasons behind it are visible. The sequence IB Gram follows is deliberately unglamorous.

First, the board and the syllabus are established, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel ask for different things in a written answer even where the physics is identical. Then the exact component. Not 'Chemistry' but 'the extended theory paper and the alternative to practical'. Then the timetable that is genuinely available once school hours, the bus, and any sport or music commitment are subtracted. Only after that does the question of home or online tutoring come up, and it is answered by geography rather than preference.

Parents in Sector 80 usually give a wider evening window than parents closer to Golf Course Road, because school buses reach the New Gurgaon sectors later. That works in your favour for home tutoring and against you for the 6 pm online slots that fill first.

A shortlist is then put in front of you with the reasoning attached: which tutor has taught this component recently, who is stronger on written explanation than on speed, who has an actual slot at 7.30 pm on a Tuesday. Availability is confirmed at that point and not before, because a tutor free in March may not be free in April.
items: Board and syllabus confirmed before anything else
Component-level diagnosis, not subject-level
Real weekly window after school bus and activities
Home or online decided by travel distance
Slots confirmed only at shortlist stage

contentBlocks.heading: Lower Secondary, Grade 9 and the two years that actually count
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is a two-year run in most schools, taught across Grade 9 and Grade 10, with the certificate decided entirely by the terminal series. Nothing from Grade 9 carries forward as marks. It carries forward as habit, which is a slower and more useful thing.

Before that, students in the New Gurgaon sectors are typically in a Cambridge Lower Secondary or a school-designed middle programme, where Checkpoint-style testing is used diagnostically. Support at this stage is worth more per rupee than support in Grade 10, and almost nobody buys it. Reading stamina, the habit of showing working, and the ability to write a paragraph that answers the question asked rather than the question hoped for are all built here.

Grade 9 is where the tier decision lands. Core papers cap the grade available; Extended papers open the top of the scale but assume more. Some schools decide early, some hold the choice until after the first set of mocks. Ask which policy your school follows, because a tutor can help you argue for a change while the entry is still open and cannot do anything about it afterwards.

Grade 10 is triage. By then the sensible plan is narrow: past papers, mark schemes, examiner phrasing, and the two or three topics that keep costing marks.

No marks banked from Grade 9

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix: what works from Godrej Air and Godrej Summit
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Sector 80 is practical for the common subjects and awkward for the rare ones. A Maths or Physics tutor living around New Gurgaon or the Dwarka Expressway corridor can reach Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next inside a reasonable drive on a normal evening. A specialist in a smaller subject may live in DLF Phase 4 or across the Delhi border, and insisting on a home slot there means paying for travel time and getting a tired tutor at 8 pm.

Online suits late slots, single-topic repair work, and any subject where the pool of good teachers is thin. It suits younger students less. A Grade 9 student who has not yet learned to sit still with a past paper will drift on a screen in a way they will not with someone at the dining table.

Hybrid is the arrangement most Sector 80 families settle into without planning it: one session at home each week for the subject that needs supervision, one online for the one that needs a specialist. In the six weeks before a series, some families flip everything online purely to reclaim the travel time.

Home tutoring, subject to tutor availability, can be reviewed for the sectors listed on this page.

Online stronger for thinly-taught subjects
Screen sessions harder for younger students

contentBlocks.heading: Where marks leak, subject by subject, on Cambridge and Edexcel papers
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the subject families ask about first. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics carries a Core and an Extended tier, and the Extended route is where the top grades live. Additional Mathematics is a separate qualification that some schools run alongside it for students heading towards A Level Mathematics or a mathematically demanding Diploma route. Edexcel's International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is the equivalent most commonly seen in Gurugram schools. Marks leak in the same two places on either board: unshown working in method-marked questions, and the last two questions on the paper, reached in a panic.

The sciences split their assessment between theory papers and a practical component. Cambridge Physics, Chemistry and Biology each offer a practical test or an alternative to practical, and most schools in this area enter students for the alternative. It is a written paper about experiments, which sounds easier than it is. Students who have never been asked to criticise a method, identify a control variable or read a scale to the right precision lose marks there routinely.

English, Economics and Business Studies reward command-term discipline. Describe, explain, evaluate and justify each buy a different number of marks. Confirm your child's exact syllabus code with the school, since schools change specifications between cohorts.
items: Method marks lost to unshown working
Alternative-to-practical papers treated as an afterthought
Command terms scored differently: describe, explain, evaluate
Additional Maths taken alongside by A Level-bound students
Cambridge and Edexcel mark schemes reward different phrasing

Families living in the Sector 80 belt are generally driving or busing towards a small set of international schools rather than anything on their doorstep. Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School near Golf Course Road, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road direction are the names that come up most often in enquiries from these sectors.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Board offerings also change, so confirm directly with your school whether it enters students for Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel or another route before you brief a tutor.

The practical effect of that commute is time. A bus that leaves the sector before 7 am and returns after 4 pm removes the entire afternoon. Coursework deadlines, mock windows and report dates are set by the school calendar and do not move for tutoring, so a good tutor plans backwards from those dates rather than running a parallel syllabus of their own.

One more thing worth knowing: mock timetables at these schools tend to cluster in the same weeks. If your tutor is also teaching other students in the same cohort, ask early about that fortnight.

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 79, 81, 82 and the Dwarka Expressway side of New Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 80 sits in the New Gurgaon residential belt, with Sector 79 and Sector 78 on one side and Sector 81 and Sector 82 on the other. The whole strip is served by the same set of approach roads, which is why a tutor who already teaches in one of these sectors can often add a second family two lanes away without much extra travel.

Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next are the addresses that appear most in enquiries from here. Several of them are gated, so the practical detail nobody mentions on a first call is guest entry. A tutor who has to argue at the gate for ten minutes twice a week will quietly stop being punctual.

Be honest with yourself about the map before booking a home slot. A tutor who is a marginally better fit but forty-five minutes away is usually the worse choice across a full academic year.

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, cancellations and the questions parents in Gurugram avoid asking
contentBlocks.body:
Ask about money in the first conversation. Fees for IGCSE tutoring in this part of Gurugram vary by subject, by level, by whether the tutor travels, and by how close the series is. A tutor who teaches Extended Physics and alternative-to-practical technique will not charge what a general Grade 9 Maths tutor charges, and pretending otherwise wastes everyone's second call.

Then ask the awkward operational questions. What is the notice period for cancelling a session. Who absorbs the cost when your child has a school trip. What happens in a school holiday. Whether the rate changes in the two months before the series, when demand is at its highest.

Ask what happens if the match is wrong. It sometimes is, and the honest answer is that a tutor change after three or four sessions is normal and not a failure. What matters is that the change is easy to request and does not require an argument.

No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about their judgement rather than their teaching. What a good arrangement can offer is a clear view, after about four weeks, of whether the work is landing.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor reaches your shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Verification on IB Gram is about relevance as much as identity. Identity and qualification documents are collected and reviewed. Teaching background is checked against the specific curriculum a family needs, because someone excellent at CBSE Class 10 Maths is not automatically the right person for Extended Cambridge papers with their own phrasing and mark allocation.

Subject depth is tested through the tutor's own account of how they teach a difficult component. A tutor who can describe how they would rebuild a student's approach to a six-mark structured question is more useful than one who lists degrees. References and prior tutoring history are reviewed where they exist.

What is not claimed here matters too. There is no ranking of tutors, no star rating gathered from a handful of families, and no performance statistic attached to any profile. Those numbers are easy to publish and almost impossible to substantiate honestly.

So the shortlist you receive is a small set of people who fit the component, the schedule and the location, with the reasoning shown. You still take the trial session and form your own view. A tutor who reads well on paper and does not hold your child's attention on a Tuesday evening is the wrong tutor, whatever the file says.

Curriculum-specific teaching history checked
Component-level subject questioning
No ratings, rankings or outcome statistics published

contentBlocks.heading: Starting an IGCSE tutor search in Sector 80 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with the last paper your child sat, not with a description of their strengths. Bring the actual script if the school returns it, or the mark breakdown if it does not. A tutor can read more from four lost marks on one structured question than from a page of general comment.

Say which board and which tier. Say which subjects are genuinely in trouble and which ones you are anxious about but which are probably fine. Two subjects taught properly beat four subjects taught thinly, and most families over-order in the first month and then quietly drop sessions in the second.

Give the real weekly window, including the days when the bus runs late and the evenings already spoken for. Then the location: your society, and whether you want a tutor at the table or on a screen.

A shortlist comes back with reasoning attached. You speak to the people on it, run a trial, and decide. If the fit is wrong, say so early rather than waiting for the next report to confirm what you already suspected in week two.

Slots close to the June and November series fill first, so the earlier conversation is the more useful one.
items: Bring the last script or mark breakdown
Name the board and the tier
Prioritise two subjects over four
Give the honest weekly window
Book earlier for pre-series months

faqs.question: The school has predicted a 6 in Physics. Can a tutor realistically change that before the June series?
faqs.answer: It depends on how much of the syllabus is secure and how many weeks remain. A predicted 6 usually means the content is broadly there and the marks are being lost in structured answers, calculation layout or the alternative-to-practical paper. Those are learnable and respond to focused work over a term. If the prediction reflects large untaught gaps and there are eight weeks left, be realistic and prioritise the papers with the most recoverable marks. No tutor can promise a grade, and a good one will tell you in the first fortnight what is actually reachable.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended for Maths?
faqs.answer: Look at mock performance on Extended-style questions rather than overall percentage. Core caps the grade available, so a student who is comfortably scoring in the middle of Extended papers should not be moved down for the sake of a safer mark. The opposite is also true: a student who is drowning on Extended and losing confidence may finish stronger on Core. The school controls the entry and sets its own deadline for changing it, so raise the question early. A tutor can give you an evidence-based opinion, but the school makes the decision.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram typically charge?
faqs.answer: Rates depend on the subject, the level, whether the tutor travels to your society and how close the exam series is. Sciences and Extended Mathematics at Grade 10 sit above general Grade 9 support. Home tutoring carries a travel component that online does not, which is why some families keep one subject at home and take the rest online. Ask for the hourly rate, the session length, the cancellation terms and whether the rate changes in the run-up to a series, all in the first conversation rather than the third.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to Godrej Air or Mapsko Casa Bella in the evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, subject to tutor availability, particularly for Mathematics and the sciences where more tutors live in or near the New Gurgaon sectors. The realistic constraint is the slot, not the address. Sessions starting after 7 pm are easier to fill than 5.30 pm ones, because school buses reach these sectors late. Arrange a standing gate entry for your tutor in the first week. Repeated arguments at the security desk are the most common reason a promising home arrangement quietly becomes unpunctual by the second month.

faqs.question: Our school follows Pearson Edexcel rather than Cambridge. Does that change who we need?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most parents expect. The underlying subject knowledge overlaps heavily, but paper structure, question phrasing and the way mark schemes reward wording differ between the boards. A tutor who has recently taught your board can tell a student which verb in a question is doing the work and how much detail earns the mark. Say the board on the first call, along with the specification your school uses, since schools sometimes run different boards for different subjects within the same year group.

faqs.question: What should the first session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, not teaching. A good first session works through a recent paper or a set of past-paper questions with the student explaining their reasoning aloud, so the tutor can see where the thinking breaks rather than where the answer is wrong. Expect a short summary afterwards: which topics are secure, which are shaky, what the pattern of lost marks looks like, and what the first month will target. If a first session is spent lecturing through a chapter, the tutor has skipped the only part you cannot get from a textbook.

faqs.question: How soon should we see something change, and what if we do not?
faqs.answer: Give it about four weeks and judge process before grades. By then you should see the student attempting harder questions without stalling, showing working without being told, and being able to say what a question is asking before answering it. Marks tend to move a term later. If none of that is visible after a month, raise it directly. Ask for a plan revision or ask for a different tutor. A change after three or four sessions is routine and should not need a difficult conversation.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both Maths and Physics for our child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it can work well at Grade 9 where the overlap in algebraic technique is genuinely useful. At Grade 10, be more careful. Physics at Extended level rewards written explanation and experimental reasoning that a Mathematics specialist may not teach with the same precision. If one tutor covers both, ask specifically how they would prepare a student for the alternative-to-practical paper. A vague answer there is a reasonable signal to split the subjects between two people.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the practical or alternative-to-practical science papers?
faqs.answer: Most do, and it is worth asking for explicitly because it is the component families forget to request. The paper tests experimental thinking on paper: reading instruments to a sensible precision, spotting the control variable, criticising a method, plotting and interpreting a graph, and explaining anomalies. Past papers with mark schemes are the main tool, since the phrasing expected is quite specific. Confirm with your school which component your child is entered for, as this varies by subject and by cohort.
