items: Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Lancers International School near Golf Course Road
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School, Sohna Road side
Late bus returns argue against a five o'clock start
Coordinator email supplies mock dates and entry decisions

contentBlocks.heading: Continuity, and the point at which changing tutor is the right call
contentBlocks.body:
Sticking with a tutor has real value. Someone who has watched a student for six months knows which excuses are genuine, which topics were faked, and how the student behaves under pressure two weeks before a mock. That knowledge is expensive to rebuild and it is why we push families to repair an arrangement before replacing it.

But there are signs that a change is overdue rather than optional. Sessions that always run as content delivery with no written work attempted. A tutor who cannot say what specifically improved in the last month. Repeated rescheduling. A student who is polite about the tutor but has stopped bringing questions.

And sometimes the fault is not the tutor's. A parent expecting a grade jump in six weeks from twice-weekly sessions on a subject the student never attends to in between will change tutors twice and blame both. Effort in the house between sessions is the variable nobody can outsource.

A fair review point is four weeks. Name one thing the student could not do at the start that they can do now. If nothing comes to mind, and the tutor cannot name it either, the arrangement is not working, and a second change now is cheaper than a bad one carried into exam term.
items: Continuity is worth defending before replacing
Warning sign: no written work attempted in session
Warning sign: tutor cannot name a specific gain
Between-session effort is not the tutor's to supply
Four weeks, one concrete improvement, then decide

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an tutor for Sector 84 Gurugram from here
contentBlocks.body:
Before you call anyone, collect four things. The board and syllabus codes from your child's past papers. The tier the school has entered them at. Whatever the previous tutor left behind, even if it is only a WhatsApp thread listing chapters. And the two evening slots that are honestly free after the bus and the activities.

The call itself takes about ten minutes. An advisor asks what went wrong last time, checks who is available near Sector 84 or online for that subject and tier, and sends a small shortlist. Nothing is confirmed until the tutor agrees to the exact slot, because a tutor who is broadly available and a tutor who is free at 7pm on Wednesday are different people.

The first session should be diagnostic even for a replacement. Ask for a written note afterwards: what they found, whether it matched the handover, and the plan for the next four weeks.

And if it is wrong again, say so in week two. The second change is much less costly than the first if you make it quickly.
items: Gather syllabus codes, tier, old notes, free evenings
Ten-minute call covers what failed and what is needed
Slots confirmed individually, subject to tutor availability
Written diagnostic note requested after session one
Flag a poor fit in week two, not in exam term

faqs.question: Our tutor stopped coming in October. How fast can a replacement start in Sector 84?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot rather than on the sector. A mathematics tutor for an early evening weekday slot is usually the quickest to arrange. An Extended-tier chemistry or a less common subject can take longer, and may be resolved online rather than in person. An advisor will check actual availability against the exact time you need instead of confirming a name and negotiating hours afterwards. Nothing is promised before the tutor has agreed to that specific slot.

faqs.question: What exactly should I ask our current tutor to hand over?
faqs.answer: Three things, requested politely and before the final session rather than after. A topic log showing what was covered and when, so nobody re-teaches finished chapters. The last few marked past papers with the wrong answers still visible, since the errors carry more information than the score. And two or three lines describing the recurring mistakes they were working on. Most tutors provide this without objection. It turns a replacement's first session into a confirmation instead of a full re-diagnosis.

faqs.question: Will a new tutor insist on starting the syllabus again?
faqs.answer: A good one will not, provided they have the handover material. They should test across the topics that were supposedly covered, which takes part of one session, and then continue from where the evidence says the student actually is. If a tutor proposes restarting from chapter one in November, ask them to justify it against a specific piece of work. Sometimes the answer is genuinely yes, because the earlier ground was never secure. More often it is a scheduling habit rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does the school need to be told that we changed tutors?
faqs.answer: There is no obligation, and most families do not mention it. What is worth doing is the reverse: getting information from the school to the new tutor. The subject coordinator can confirm the tier your child has been entered at, the practical route for the sciences, mock dates, and any coursework deadlines. Those decisions belong to the school and are not visible to a tutor otherwise. One email supplies all of it and prevents weeks of work aimed at the wrong assessment format.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if we have already changed tutors twice this year?
faqs.answer: It is worth pausing over rather than panicking about. Two changes can mean bad luck, particularly if the first tutor relocated. Three or more usually points to something in the brief rather than in the tutors: an unclear target, sessions scheduled at an hour when the student is exhausted, or an expectation of progress without any work between sessions. Being honest about that pattern on the call produces a much better match than describing the previous tutors as unsuitable.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from Sector 83 or Sector 85 realistically take us on?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, and it is one of the better features of this location. Tutors here build routes rather than isolated appointments, so a person already teaching in a neighbouring sector on a given evening can add a Sector 84 student with almost no extra travel. Movement between Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next is quick. The constraint is the hour, not the distance, since the popular early evening slots on a route fill first.

faqs.question: We are switching tutors while coursework is in progress. Is that risky?
faqs.answer: It carries more risk than switching in a purely exam-assessed subject, so timing matters. Where a subject includes a coursework or portfolio component, the deadline sits with the school and the work must remain the student's own. A new tutor can teach technique and discuss structure, but cannot take over drafting. Ask the school for the exact submission date first, then decide whether to change now or hold the arrangement until the piece is submitted. Sometimes waiting three weeks is the safer choice.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor make a repeat handover less likely?
faqs.answer: It removes one common cause of it. A large share of the arrangements that collapse in New Gurgaon do so because travel stopped being practical, or the tutor moved to another part of the city. An online tutor is unaffected by either. What online does not fix is a mismatch of teaching style, a wrong time slot, or a subject the tutor was never strong in. Continuity improves; the quality of the original match still has to be right.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the new tutor is better than the old one?
faqs.answer: Set the test at four weeks and make it concrete. Name one thing the student could not do when the new tutor started and can do now: setting up a stoichiometry calculation, structuring a six-mark answer, reading a question and identifying the command word. If neither you nor the tutor can name that thing, the arrangement is not producing value, whatever the sessions feel like. Progress that cannot be described specifically is usually progress that has not happened.

heroSubtitle: Every useful tutoring plan in this house starts from a date on the exam timetable and works backwards. Which series the school has entered, when the mocks land, when the practical component is sat, and how many usable weeks are left once school assessments are removed.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 85 Gurugram are best chosen by deadline rather than by subject alone. Cambridge International runs a February and March series in India alongside the May and June and October and November sessions, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE offers January and summer entries. The school decides which series a student sits, and that date fixes how many weeks of teaching remain. Home and online sessions across the New Gurgaon sectors depend on tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: The exam calendar that sets the tutoring timetable in Sector 85 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Open the exam timetable first. Everything else in an IGCSE year is downstream of it.

A parent in Sector 85 Gurugram who rings in July with a June paper ahead has roughly forty teaching weeks, minus school assessments, minus the mock block, minus two festival gaps and a family trip. Call it twenty-eight usable weeks. That is a comfortable plan. The same call made in January leaves perhaps twelve weeks, of which four are consumed by mocks and study leave. Same subject, same student, completely different job.

So the sequence runs like this. Find the series the school has entered the child for. Find the mock window, usually somewhere between late November and January depending on the school. Find whether the science subjects are sat as a practical test or the written alternative, because the practical is often scheduled separately. Then count what is genuinely left.

Only after that does it make sense to ask which tutor, how often and at what level. A plan built forwards from today drifts. A plan built backwards from a date produces a weekly target that either fits or visibly does not, and both answers are useful.

Confirm your exact timetable and entry details with the school, since series arrangements vary by subject.
items: Series date first, tutor second
Subtract mocks, study leave and school assessments before counting weeks
Practical components are often timetabled apart from written papers
Twelve usable weeks and twenty-eight need different plans
School office holds the entry and timetable detail

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel series: March, June, November and January entries
contentBlocks.body:
Two board families and four broad entry points shape the year for international-school students here.

Cambridge International offers a February and March series that runs in India, alongside the main May and June session and the October and November session. That March series is genuinely useful for Indian schools because it sits before the summer holidays, though not every subject and every syllabus is offered in it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a January series as well as the summer one, which gives a different set of options again.

Why this matters for tutoring: a student who is weak in one subject but sound in the rest can sometimes sit that subject in a different series rather than dragging the whole set. That is a school decision, not a parent's or a tutor's, and it has to be raised well before entries close.

Tiering interacts with the calendar too. In Cambridge subjects offering Core and Extended routes, the tier is fixed once entries are submitted, and Core caps the grade available. A student improving fast in October may still be locked into the entry made earlier.

Grading appears as 9-1 on some syllabuses and A*-G on others, so a report card can carry both.
items: Cambridge February and March series available in India, subject dependent
Cambridge May and June, plus October and November sessions
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE January and summer entries
Tier locked at entry; Core limits the top grade
9-1 and A*-G scales can appear together on one report

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 85 Gurugram at the outer edge of the New Gurgaon belt
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 85 sits towards the far side of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, with Sector 84 and Sector 86 immediately alongside, Sector 83 a short run back, and Sector 87 continuing outward. The everyday addresses in enquiries from here are Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next.

Being at the edge has one consequence that matters during exam term. When a plan calls for three sessions a week in March rather than one, the tutor's journey stops being an occasional inconvenience and becomes the thing that decides whether the plan survives. A tutor coming in from Sohna Road or across the Dwarka Expressway approaches can manage a weekly visit. Three a week, in the weeks that matter most, tends to break.

That is the argument for setting the format before the intensity rises, not during. Families who move to online in February, having already used it once a week since August, lose nothing. Families who try to switch format in the fortnight before a paper lose two sessions to setup and adjustment.

Movement within the belt is easy. Movement in and out of it at peak is not, and the exam calendar has no interest in traffic.
items: Sector 84, Sector 86, Sector 83 and Sector 87 form the immediate run
Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella, Vatika India Next
Weekly home visits scale badly to three sessions a week
Choose the exam-term format months before exam term
Inbound journeys from Sohna Road are the weak link

contentBlocks.heading: Which components fall where, subject by subject
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is written papers only, which makes it the easiest subject to plan around. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits by tier, and Additional Mathematics 0606 sits alongside it for students taking mathematics further. Revision here is about accuracy and timing, and the last six weeks are best spent on full timed papers rather than topic sheets.

The sciences carry an extra date. Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each include a practical strand, sat either as a laboratory practical test or as a written alternative-to-practical paper, and schools choose the route. The written alternative rewards a specific kind of preparation: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying variables, spotting the flaw in a described method, drawing results tables correctly. That is trainable, and it is often the cheapest set of marks available late in the year.

English needs the earliest start. First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 both reward writing that has been marked repeatedly over months, and nothing in that process compresses well.

Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450 and ICT 0417 sit somewhere between: definitions and case-study technique respond quickly, application to unseen scenarios does not.

Verify paper numbers, durations and weightings against the syllabus version your school follows.

Sciences add a practical or alternative-to-practical component
Alternative-to-practical technique is trainable late
English 0500 and 0510 need the longest lead time
Economics 0455 and ICT 0417 respond fast on definitions, slowly on application

contentBlocks.heading: Mock windows at the schools Sector 85 Gurugram families use
contentBlocks.body:
The school-set calendar is often more disruptive than the board one, because it arrives first and it eats the weeks you were counting on. Students from this sector travel to Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School towards Golf Course Road, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School on the Sohna Road side.

Each runs its own internal assessment and mock cycle, typically somewhere across late November through January, followed by a period of study leave. During that block, a tutor teaching new content is working against the school. The sensible move is to shift to paper technique and error correction for those weeks and resume content afterwards, if any content is genuinely left.

Mock results are also the single most useful diagnostic a tutor will get all year. Not the grade, the script. Ask the school for the marked paper rather than only the mark, and give it to the tutor. Marks lost to misread command words, unfinished final questions or missing units are a different problem from marks lost to not knowing the topic, and they need opposite responses.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of these schools unless specifically stated.

Lancers International School towards Golf Course Road

Give the tutor the marked script, not just the mark

contentBlocks.heading: Matching a tutor to a deadline, not just a subject
contentBlocks.body:
An advisor asks the date before the subject. It changes which tutor is right.

With six months or more, the match should favour someone who teaches properly: builds understanding, sets written work, is willing to go back and repair foundations from earlier years even when it feels slow. With eight weeks, that same tutor may be the wrong choice. Late-stage work is triage, and it needs a tutor comfortable saying that a topic will not be recovered and the time is better spent securing the marks that are still reachable.

The brief taken on the call therefore covers: series and date, subjects and tier, mock performance if it exists, which components remain, and how many sessions a week the family can realistically sustain once the student's own revision time is protected. Piling on sessions until there is no time left to revise alone is a common and self-defeating mistake.

A short shortlist follows, checked against the exact slots needed rather than general availability, since the popular hours in the Sector 84 to Sector 86 run fill early in the exam term.

After the first session, ask for a written view of what is realistically achievable in the time remaining. A tutor who will not commit that to writing is worth questioning.

Long runway favours foundation repair; short runway favours triage
Session frequency capped so solo revision time survives
Slots confirmed individually during exam term
Written statement of what the remaining weeks can realistically deliver

contentBlocks.heading: Session formats that survive the exam term in Sector 85 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Intensity changes what format works. A ninety-minute weekly home visit is a fine shape for September. It is a poor shape for the last six weeks, when what a student needs is shorter, more frequent contact: a timed paper attempted alone, then forty minutes going through the errors while they are still fresh.

Online handles that pattern far better. A short Tuesday and Friday slot costs a tutor nothing in travel, so they will agree to it. The same tutor asked to drive to Sector 85 twice a week in March will either decline or charge in a way that reflects the road.

In-person keeps two advantages worth protecting. Practical technique for students sitting a laboratory paper is genuinely better taught with equipment in front of them. And some students simply do not work honestly on a screen, muting and drifting through the difficult twenty minutes. If that is your child, pay for the presence and plan the frequency accordingly.

The workable compromise most families here land on: keep one in-person session as the anchor, add short online sessions as the date approaches, and stop adding anything three weeks out so the student has quiet hours of their own.
items: Weekly ninety-minute visits suit early months, not the final weeks
Short twice-weekly online slots fit paper-and-review cycles
Laboratory practical technique still favours in-person
Some students need presence to work honestly
Stop adding sessions three weeks out

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits of a revision plan built backwards
contentBlocks.body:
Working backwards from a date is clarifying, but it also exposes things families would rather not see, and a tutor who hides them is not doing the job.

A calendar cannot manufacture weeks. If a student has genuinely not learnt two thirds of a syllabus and the paper is nine weeks away, no schedule of sessions produces a strong grade. What it can produce is a decent grade on the material that is reachable, and an honest conversation with the school about the tier or the series. Parents are often relieved by that conversation. It is the pretending that exhausts everyone.

There is a second limit. Tutoring adds hours to a student who is already tired. Past a point, more sessions reduce output, because revision needs solitary hours to consolidate and those hours get eaten first. A student doing five tutoring hours a week and no independent work is being taught, not learning.

And a caution about last-minute intensity: paying for daily sessions in the final fortnight rarely returns what it costs. Those weeks belong to timed practice and sleep.

Judge any arrangement at four weeks against something specific the student can now do. Vague reassurance is not evidence.
items: No schedule replaces content never learnt
Tier and series conversations belong with the school, early
Solitary revision hours are the first thing over-scheduling destroys
Daily sessions in the last fortnight are poor value
Review at four weeks against one concrete gain

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a recommendation, and what is never claimed
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers the unremarkable things properly. Government photo identification is verified. Qualifications are confirmed against documents rather than accepted from a CV. Subject depth is tested with a real question from a real past paper, and for exam-term matches the question chosen is usually a marking one: why did this answer lose two marks. Tutors who can explain the mark scheme are the ones who help late in the year.

Board familiarity is checked separately from subject knowledge, because a strong physics teacher who has only worked with a different board will need a few weeks to internalise how questions are phrased, and a family nine weeks from a paper does not have those weeks to spare.

Reliability history is considered: notice given, slots kept, engagements completed rather than abandoned mid-term. Feedback from families a tutor has worked with is collected and does influence later recommendations.

What you will not find here: promised grades, invented ratings, testimonials nobody wrote, or a number of tutors on the platform. Availability is described as conditional because it is conditional, and a specific slot is confirmed with the tutor before you are asked to commit to anything.

Depth tested on mark-scheme reasoning, not content recall
Board familiarity assessed separately for late-stage matches
Reliability history weighed for exam-term work
No grade promises, no invented ratings or reviews

contentBlocks.heading: Planning IGCSE tutoring in Sector 85 Gurugram around your next series

Start by getting three facts from the school: which series each subject is entered for, which tier where tiering applies, and whether the sciences are sat as a practical test or the written alternative. Add your child's most recent marked script if one exists.

Then a short call. An advisor counts the usable weeks with you, which frequently produces a different number from the one in your head, and works out whether the goal fits the time. If it does not, you will hear that on the first call rather than in March.

A small shortlist follows, checked against the exact evenings you need, covering tutors who can reach Sector 85 and tutors who teach the subject online. Every slot stays subject to the tutor's own schedule until confirmed.

The first session is diagnostic, ideally built around the mock script. Ask afterwards for a written view of what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve, and hold the plan to that at four weeks.

One practical note on timing. Families who arrange the format early, while the schedule is still light, keep the option of raising intensity later. Families who wait until the term before the papers find that the good evening slots in this part of New Gurgaon have already gone, and that switching between home and online in the final weeks costs sessions nobody can spare. Starting the conversation early does not commit you to starting lessons early.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE papers in the February and March series in India?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a February and March series that operates in India, and many schools here use it. Not every syllabus is offered in that series though, and the decision to enter a student sits with the school rather than with parents. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE offers a January series and a summer series instead. Ask your subject coordinator which series each of your child's subjects is entered for, because the answer can differ across a single subject set and it changes the whole tutoring plan.

faqs.question: How many usable weeks do we really have before the papers?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. From your starting date, subtract the school's mock block, the study leave that follows it, internal assessments, and any travel already planned. In practice a family starting in July before a summer series has somewhere near twenty-eight teaching weeks, while one starting in January has closer to twelve, and four of those are consumed by mocks. Doing this arithmetic on the first call is uncomfortable but it produces a plan that survives contact with the term.

faqs.question: Should tutoring pause during the school mock block?
faqs.answer: It should change shape rather than pause. Teaching new content during mocks and study leave works against the school and confuses the student. What helps in those weeks is paper technique, timing practice and error correction on work already covered. Once mock scripts come back, they become the most useful diagnostic available all year. Resume content teaching afterwards if there is genuinely content left, and if there is not, spend the remaining weeks on timed papers instead.

faqs.question: How do we prepare for the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: First confirm with the school that your child is entered for the written alternative rather than the laboratory practical test, because the preparation differs completely. The written version rewards a trainable set of skills: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying dependent and control variables, spotting the weakness in a described method, recording results in a properly headed table with consistent decimal places. Those marks are often the cheapest available late in the year, which makes this component worth targeting when time is short.

faqs.question: Is daily tutoring in the final two weeks worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Usually not. By that stage the material is either known or it is not, and what raises marks is timed practice done alone followed by careful review of the errors. Daily sessions eat the solitary hours that consolidation needs and leave a tired student who has been taught a great deal and revised very little. A better pattern is a timed paper attempted independently, then a shorter session going through the mistakes, twice a week rather than every day.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach Sector 85 three times a week during exam term?
faqs.answer: A weekly visit is realistic for a tutor already working within the Sector 84 to Sector 86 run. Three a week from outside the belt is where arrangements break, because the inbound journey from Sohna Road or across the New Gurgaon approaches is unpredictable at exactly the hours you need. The practical answer for most families here is to keep one in-person session as an anchor and add short online slots as the date approaches. All of it remains subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: My child improved after entries were submitted. Can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Tier decisions rest with the school and are fixed once entries for a series are submitted, so the honest answer for the current series is often no. What can be done is to raise it immediately, since some schools have a short amendment window before the deadline passes. If the window has closed, the sensible plan is to teach at the higher standard anyway, secure the best result available at the entered tier, and use that evidence when the next series entry is being decided.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first tutoring session?
faqs.answer: The most recent marked script, ideally a mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks visible, matters more than anything else. Add the syllabus codes printed on your child's past papers, the tier where tiering applies, and the exam series each subject is entered for. With those four things a tutor can diagnose in one session rather than three. Without them the first fortnight goes on rediscovering information the school could have supplied in a single email.

faqs.question: How soon will we see whether the plan is working?
faqs.answer: Set the checkpoint at four weeks and make it specific. There should be something nameable the student can now do that they could not before: complete a full paper within the time allowed, structure a longer written answer, set out a calculation with units carried through correctly. Score movement on timed papers is the other honest signal. If neither you nor the tutor can point at something concrete after a month, the arrangement needs changing rather than more time.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 86, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Sector 86 sits in the New Gurgaon residential sectors, between Sector 85 and Sector 87, with Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next close to one another. Tutors can be matched for home sessions here or online, subject to availability.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 86 Gurugram are usually engaged for one of three reasons: a Grade 9 student who has moved in from a CBSE school and met Extended tier algebra for the first time, a Grade 10 student whose mocks came back below the predicted grade, or a family still deciding between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entry. Sessions run at home inside the Godrej and Vatika societies or online. A first session should end with a written view of where the marks are actually going.

contentBlocks.heading: What a first IGCSE session in Sector 86 Gurugram should actually produce
contentBlocks.body:
Most families book a first session hoping the tutor will start teaching immediately. Ninety minutes spent on diagnosis is worth considerably more. Bring the last two school assessments, the syllabus the school has entered your child against, and any teacher comments from the report card. A tutor who cannot tell you by the end of that session whether the student is on the Core or the Extended tier has not done the job you paid for.

By the close, you should be holding three specific things. A list of topics where marks are being lost, not a general impression that maths is weak. A view on tier, because Core and Extended are different papers with different ceilings. And a plan for the next four weeks that names topics in order.

That third item is the one families skip. Sector 86 households often arrive at this point late: a student joins in Grade 9 from a CBSE background, meets algebraic manipulation at Extended pace, and the first honest signal comes with the Grade 10 mocks. By then the runway is short.

So the first session is also a decision point for you. If the hour went on the tutor explaining their own credentials, or on a random past paper with no reference to what the school has covered, you have your answer. Ask for a different name.
items: Last two school assessments in hand
Board and syllabus confirmed, not assumed
Core or Extended tier established
Four-week topic order written down
A named starting target, never a promised grade

contentBlocks.heading: Reaching a tutor from Godrej Air, Godrej Summit and Vatika India Next
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 86 belongs to the New Gurgaon residential sectors, sitting directly between Sector 85 and Sector 87, with Sector 84 and Sector 88 a short drive further out. The practical consequence for tutoring is simple. Almost everything a family needs is inside a two or three kilometre radius, and almost nothing beyond that radius is quick.

Inside the sector, Godrej Air and Godrej Summit sit close enough that a tutor taking a slot in one can realistically take a second slot in the other on the same evening. Mapsko Casa Bella and the Vatika India Next township add to that density. This is the main reason a home tutor agrees to an outer-sector address at all. Two or three students in one cluster makes the travel worth the fuel and the hour lost.

Travelling the other way is harder. The run towards Sohna Road or the older Golf Course Road sectors is slow at 6pm on a weekday, and a tutor based there will usually decline a 5pm slot in Sector 86 rather than turn up twenty minutes late every week. The Dwarka Expressway side moves faster off-peak, less so during the school run.

Which is why the honest answer for many families here is a mixed arrangement rather than a purely local one.

Sector 84 and Sector 88 a short drive out

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix for a Sector 86 Gurugram address
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring works reasonably well in Sector 86 for the subjects a large number of tutors teach. Extended maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Business Studies. Availability can be reviewed for a specific society and a specific slot, and it depends heavily on whether a tutor already has a student nearby.

Online is the better choice in three situations, and it is worth being blunt about them. Rare subjects come first: Additional Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics taught at real depth, or a second language the school offers. The pool of people who teach those well and will also drive into New Gurgaon on a Tuesday evening is thin. Second, late slots. A 9pm session after football finishes is realistic on a screen and unrealistic in a car. Third, short bursts. Twenty minutes of doubt-solving the night before a class test is a call online and a wasted trip in person.

The mixed pattern most Sector 86 families settle into looks like one weekend home session for the subject that needs a person in the room, plus one or two online sessions midweek for everything else.

Grade 6 to Grade 8 students are the exception worth naming. Attention holds better in person at that age, and a screen after a full school day is a genuine struggle rather than a preference.
items: Home sessions strongest for maths and the separate sciences
Online better for Additional Maths, Computer Science, second languages
Late-evening slots realistic only online
Weekend home plus midweek online is the common pattern
Younger students usually do better face to face

contentBlocks.heading: Maths tiering and science practicals: where Sector 86 Gurugram students lose marks
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics runs on two tiers. Core covers a reduced content list with a lower grade ceiling, Extended covers the full list. The school decides entry, sometimes as late as Grade 10, and a student sitting the wrong tier is the most common fixable problem we come across. Some schools run Cambridge International Mathematics instead, which expects a graphic display calculator and includes an investigation-style component. The two are not interchangeable, so check which one appears on your child's syllabus sheet rather than assuming.

The separate sciences follow a recognisable shape: a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper set at Core or Extended level, and then either a practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper. That last component is where marks quietly disappear. It rewards a narrow, teachable skill set. Reading a scale to the right precision. Describing a control variable in the language a marker recognises. Spotting the anomalous result and saying why it is anomalous. Very few students are taught this properly in class, and it takes a handful of sessions to fix.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE arranges its science papers differently, so a tutor should establish the board before planning anything.

For English, the split between First Language English and English as a Second Language changes the whole approach. Ask the school which entry applies.
items: Core and Extended are different papers with different ceilings
Cambridge International Mathematics expects a graphic display calculator
Alternative-to-practical marks lost on scales, variables and anomalies
First Language English and ESL need different preparation
Board confirmed before any revision plan is drawn up

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built after your first message
contentBlocks.body:
You send the subject, the grade, the board if you know it, and where in Sector 86 you live. What happens next is not an automated match against a subject name.

An advisor asks a short set of questions first. Which school, because pace and internal deadlines differ between them. Which tier for maths and the sciences. Whether the student needs content taught from the beginning or technique repaired on content already covered. Whether home sessions in your society are a requirement or a preference you would trade for a stronger subject specialist.

Only then does a shortlist go out, and it is deliberately short. Two or three names, each with a note on what that person actually specialises in and what their availability looks like for your slot. Fees are discussed at this stage rather than after a trial, because a fee that does not work for you is not a match however good the teaching is.

You then speak to the tutor yourself. Not to us on their behalf.

If the first session does not land, say so plainly and a second name goes out. Nobody takes it badly. A tutor who is excellent with a confident Extended maths student can be entirely wrong for a student who has stopped believing they can do maths at all.
items: School, tier and board captured before any name is shared
Two or three names rather than a directory
Fees discussed before the trial, not after
You speak to the tutor directly
Re-matching on request, without argument

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 to Grade 10, and what follows the IGCSE year
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is normally a two-year course spanning Grade 9 and Grade 10, with subjects chosen at the start of Grade 9. Those choices carry further than families expect, because they constrain what is realistic at the next stage.

A student who drops the separate sciences for a combined route, then decides in Grade 11 to take Physics at higher level in the IB Diploma or Chemistry at A Level, starts from behind. Not blocked, but behind, and the first term is spent catching up rather than learning. Additional Mathematics taken alongside the main maths syllabus works the other way: it makes the jump into Math AA HL or A Level Maths noticeably gentler.

Tutoring in Grade 9 is therefore mostly about content and working habits. In Grade 10 it shifts towards paper technique, timing and command terms, because the syllabus is largely finished by mid-year and the remaining marks are lost in execution rather than knowledge.

Below IGCSE, in the Lower Secondary years, most students who later struggle were already unsteady on fractions, ratio and algebraic manipulation. Repairing that in Grade 7 costs a term of easy work. Repairing it in Grade 10 costs the grade.

For primary-age children, sessions look nothing like exam prep: reading fluency, written structure, number sense.
items: Subject choices locked in early in Grade 9
Separate sciences ease the route to A Level or IB higher level
Additional Maths smooths the Grade 11 transition
Grade 10 work is mostly technique and timing
Lower Secondary gaps are cheapest to fix early

contentBlocks.heading: The school run from Sector 86 Gurugram: Scottish High, Lancers, Pathways and GD Goenka
contentBlocks.body:
Families in Sector 86 draw on a small set of international schools, and none of them is next door. Scottish High International School sits in Sector 57, Lancers International School is off Golf Course Road, while Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School lie out towards the Sohna side. Bus routes from the New Gurgaon sectors are long, and that single fact shapes almost everything about tutoring here.

A student who leaves at 6:45am and gets home at 4:30pm has a real ceiling on what can be absorbed at 5pm. Tutors who work with this cluster tend to push the first weekday slot to 6pm or later, and to keep midweek sessions to sixty or seventy-five minutes instead of ninety. Longer is not better with a tired student.

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a tutor reaches your shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Verification means a set of checks described plainly, not a badge on a profile picture.

Identity is confirmed against a government-issued document. Qualifications are checked against the certificate rather than the claim. Teaching history is discussed in a conversation, and the questions are specific: which boards, which syllabuses, which grades, and how recently. A tutor who taught Cambridge IGCSE Physics five years ago and has taught only state board since is a different proposition from one currently teaching it every week.

Subject depth is tested by asking the tutor to talk through a real teaching problem. How they would prepare a student for the alternative-to-practical paper. How they would move someone from a middling to a strong Extended maths grade. Vague answers end that conversation.

References are requested where a tutor has worked with families before, and they are actually contacted.

What none of this establishes is whether a particular adult will work well with your particular child. No screening process can. Which is why the first session is treated as a genuine trial and why changing tutor is made easy rather than awkward.

Availability across Sector 86 is subject to tutor schedules and shifts through the year, so a name with a free Tuesday in September may not have one in January.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a tutoring arrangement usually goes wrong
contentBlocks.body:
Three failure patterns account for most arrangements that quietly stop working.

The first is homework outsourcing. The session becomes an hour of the tutor completing the school assignment while the student watches, class marks hold up, and exam marks do not. If your child cannot explain the method a day later without prompting, that is what has been happening.

The second is a plan nobody writes down. Sessions run, everyone is pleasant, and by November no one can say what was covered in September. Ask for a short record after each session. Three lines and a topic name is enough.

The third is starting too late. A student beginning in February of Grade 10 with weak algebra will not cover two years of content before the June series, and a tutor who suggests otherwise is selling rather than teaching. What is possible in that window is triage: secure the topics carrying the largest weighting, drill paper technique, accept the rest.

Real progress over four to six weeks looks like this. Fewer careless errors. Method marks appearing where the page was previously blank. A student who attempts an unfamiliar question instead of leaving it.

If none of that is visible by week six, change the tutor rather than waiting politely.
items: Homework being finished rather than taught
No written record of what each session covered
Late starts no tutor can fully recover
Falling careless errors as the first honest signal
Week six is a fair point to reassess

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child should be sitting Core or Extended maths?
faqs.answer: The school decides entry, so start by asking the subject teacher directly which tier your child is currently pencilled in for. Core covers less content and carries a lower grade ceiling; Extended covers the full syllabus. A tutor can give you a second opinion within two sessions by working through Extended-level algebra, trigonometry and functions questions and seeing what holds. Some students are entered for Core defensively when a term of focused work would have made Extended realistic. Others are on Extended and drowning. Both situations are worth checking before Grade 10 begins.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Godrej Air or Vatika India Next for an evening session?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, but it depends on the slot and on whether that tutor already has a student in the New Gurgaon sectors. A 6:30pm or 7:30pm weekday slot in Sector 86 is more likely to be accepted than a 5pm one, because the drive in from the older sectors is slow at that hour. Weekend mornings are the easiest to fill. Availability is checked against current schedules before anything is confirmed, and it changes through the year, so a slot that exists in September may not survive into the exam term.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tutors near Sector 86 charge, and what drives the difference?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with subject, grade and mode rather than with a fixed price list. Grade 10 Extended maths, Physics and Chemistry sit higher than Grade 6 to Grade 8 support. Home sessions in the outer sectors typically cost more than online because the tutor is giving up travel time as well as teaching time, and specialists in thinner subjects command more. You will be told the fee for each shortlisted tutor before the first session rather than after it, so you can decline on price without having to sit through a trial first.

faqs.question: My child does well in school tests but badly in the mocks. What explains that?
faqs.answer: Usually the gap is exam technique rather than knowledge. School tests cover one recently taught chapter; a mock paper mixes topics, uses unfamiliar phrasing and enforces timing. Students who have only ever revised a chapter at a time have never practised deciding what a question is asking. Command terms matter here. Describe, explain, calculate and justify carry different mark expectations, and a good answer to the wrong instruction earns nothing. This is repairable fairly quickly with past papers marked against real mark schemes, which is a specific skill to ask a tutor about.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely effective for a Grade 10 student?
faqs.answer: For Grade 10, yes, provided the setup is right. The student needs a tablet or a document camera so the tutor can see working as it happens, not a finished answer photographed afterwards. Where online often beats home tutoring is subject depth: you can reach a specialist who would never drive to the New Gurgaon sectors on a weeknight. Where it loses is with students who drift without someone physically present. If your child needs a person in the room to stay on task, be honest about that and prioritise home sessions.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and can it be prepared for separately?
faqs.answer: In the Cambridge sciences, schools choose between a practical examination and a written alternative-to-practical paper that tests the same skills on paper. It asks students to read scales, identify variables, spot anomalous results, describe method improvements and comment on safety. Almost all of it is pattern work, and it responds very well to focused preparation because the question types repeat across series. Six to eight sessions on past alternative-to-practical papers is usually enough to move a student who understands the theory but keeps losing these marks. Confirm with the school which component applies.

faqs.question: We are shifting from CBSE into Grade 9 IGCSE. How big is the adjustment?
faqs.answer: The content overlap in maths and science is larger than most parents fear. The adjustment is in how answers are written. IGCSE rewards explanation, structured working and precise use of terminology, where a CBSE-trained student is often used to a correct final answer being the point. Extended maths also moves faster through algebraic manipulation than many students expect. The first term is the right time to work on this, while there is no exam pressure. Students who wait until Grade 10 usually find themselves fixing habits and learning new content at the same time.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor turns out not to be right for my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and a second name goes out. This is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint, because subject knowledge and personal fit are separate things and no screening process predicts the second one. You are not asked to justify the decision at length. It helps to be specific about what did not work, since it sharpens the next match: pace too fast, too much talking, no written plan, wrong time of evening. Most families who change once do not need to change again.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense alongside a full school day?
faqs.answer: For one weak subject, two sessions a week is usually the ceiling in Grade 9 and Grade 10. More than that leaves no time to actually practise between sessions, and practice is where the learning consolidates. Two subjects at two sessions each is already a heavy week for a student travelling long distances to school. If three or four subjects genuinely need help, the honest conversation is about triage and priority order rather than adding hours. Overloading a tired student usually produces less progress than a lighter, consistent schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: What the schools around Sector 87 Gurugram expect of an IGCSE student
contentBlocks.body:
Children living in Sector 87 do not attend a neighbourhood school. They travel, most often to Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School near Golf Course Road, or out to Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School. Each runs a demanding Grade 9 and Grade 10 programme with its own internal deadlines, and each has settled on either Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel as its examining board.

That matters more than the marketing on any tutoring site. Two students in adjacent towers of Mapsko Casa Bella can be preparing for different papers, different grading scales and different sitting months, purely because of where the bus takes them each morning.

So the useful question is not who the best tutor in New Gurgaon is. It is which specification your child is entered against, at which tier, and what the school's own assessment schedule looks like between now and the final series.

The demands themselves are consistent enough. Written explanation carries marks. Command terms are taken seriously by markers. Sciences reward precision in describing method. Maths punishes unshown working. A student who has coasted on quick correct answers usually meets resistance somewhere in Grade 9, and that resistance is the signal worth acting on.

Assessment calendars differ between the four main schools here
Written explanation and command terms carry real marks

Tier and specification confirmed before planning anything

contentBlocks.heading: From enquiry to a name: what the advisor actually asks
contentBlocks.body:
The enquiry itself is short. Subject, grade, your part of Sector 87, and whether you want someone at home or online.

The questions that follow are the useful part. Which school, because the internal deadline calendar is the frame everything sits inside. Which board and which syllabus, checked on the school's own subject sheet rather than guessed from memory. Whether the student is behind on content or losing marks on content they know. What the last two report cards actually said, in the teacher's words rather than the summary grade.

And one question parents are rarely asked: what does the student want. A Grade 10 student who agreed to tutoring reluctantly needs a different first session from one who asked for it.

A shortlist follows, usually two or three tutors, each with a short description of their subject range and their real availability for your preferred slot. Fees come with the names.

From there you speak to the tutors yourself and choose. Nobody is assigned to you. If none of the three suits, that is worth saying, because it usually means one of the earlier answers needs refining rather than that no tutor exists.

Report card comments read, not just the grade
Student's own view taken into account

You choose; nobody is assigned

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and why the difference surfaces in Grade 10
contentBlocks.body:
Both boards are widely taught in Gurugram and both are accepted everywhere that matters afterwards. They are not identical, though, and the differences become practical in Grade 10.

Cambridge IGCSE examines in a June and a November series, with most international syllabuses reported on the A* to G scale, while a number have been converted to a 9 to 1 scale. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered, so a student sits either Core or Extended papers with different grade ceilings attached.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 scale and offers January as well as June sittings, which changes what a resit or an early entry can look like. Its courses are, for the most part, assessed entirely by written examination.

Coursework survives in places on the Cambridge side, as an optional route in certain subjects that some schools take up and many do not. Check your school's subject outline rather than assuming either way.

None of this is a choice you make. The school made it. What you can control is whether the tutor plans around the right papers, and whether past papers used in revision come from the correct board.
items: Cambridge: June and November series, A*-G with some 9-1 syllabuses
Edexcel International GCSE: 9-1 scale, January and June sittings
Cambridge tiering means Core or Extended entry per subject
Coursework routes exist in some Cambridge subjects only
Revision past papers must match the school's board

contentBlocks.heading: Weekday timing in Sector 87 Gurugram and what it rules out
contentBlocks.body:
The evening is short here, and pretending otherwise produces arrangements that collapse in six weeks.

A student on a long bus route reaches home somewhere between 4pm and 5pm, tired. Sports, music or a school activity takes another slice on two or three days. Homework is real and often substantial. What remains for tutoring is one usable block, usually between 6pm and 8:30pm, and it cannot be filled on every weekday without something breaking.

Home tutoring fits that block reasonably well for mainstream subjects, and Sector 87 benefits from sitting between Sector 86 and Sector 88, since a tutor already committed to one of those addresses can often add a second student here without a separate trip.

Online changes the arithmetic in two ways. It removes the tutor's travel, which makes 8:30pm or 9pm workable, and it widens the pool to specialists who would otherwise be unreachable from New Gurgaon on a weeknight.

What online does not do is impose structure on a distracted fifteen-year-old. If your child needs a person in the room, say so at the start and accept the tighter slot options that come with it.

Weekend mornings remain the least contested hours of the week.

Adjacency to Sector 86 and Sector 88 improves home availability
Online unlocks late slots and thinner subjects
Distraction-prone students still do better in person
Weekend mornings are the easiest hours to fill

contentBlocks.heading: Papers, tiers and grading across the main IGCSE subjects
contentBlocks.body:
English is where the largest planning mistake gets made. Cambridge sets First Language English and English as a Second Language as separate qualifications with different demands, and a school sometimes moves a student between them at the end of Grade 9. A tutor preparing a First Language response structure for a student entered for the second language route is wasting both their hours.

Maths sits on tiers in the Cambridge system, so establish tier before anything else. The step from a comfortable Core performance to a secure Extended one is mostly algebraic fluency, and it is not a two-week job.

Economics and Business Studies reward a specific answer shape: define the term, apply it to the case given, then evaluate. Students who write general essays lose the application and evaluation marks even when the economics is sound.

The humanities papers lean on source handling and structured argument rather than recall. History in particular tests what a source is useful for and why, which is a technique.

Sciences are usually a combination of a multiple-choice component, tiered theory papers and a practical or written practical-skills component. Confirm the exact structure on the school's specification sheet rather than trusting a general summary.

Maths tier drives every revision decision that follows
Economics and Business need define, apply, evaluate
History marks sit in source usefulness and reliability
Science paper structure confirmed from the school's specification

Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and Lancers International School near Golf Course Road pull a good number of families from the New Gurgaon sectors, while Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School sit further out towards the Sohna side. From Sector 87 all four are a commute, not a walk.

What this means in practice is that a tutor working with children from this sector ends up handling several different school calendars at once. One school's pre-boards land in December, another's in the third week of January, and a third sets project deadlines in the same fortnight. A revision plan built on the exam series alone, without reference to the school's own dates, tends to collide with an assignment week and lose two sessions.

Ask a prospective tutor whether they have taught students from your child's school before. Not because a school-specific tutor is essential, but because the answer tells you whether they will ask about internal deadlines at all.

contentBlocks.heading: The parts of a grade that tutoring cannot move
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor can teach content, repair technique, build a revision schedule and hold a student to it. There are things a tutor cannot do, and knowing them saves money.

A tutor cannot manufacture practice hours. Two sessions a week produce very little if nothing is attempted between them. The families who see the clearest change are the ones where the student does the set work, badly at first, and brings it back.

A tutor cannot override an entry decision. If the school has entered a student at Core tier, the ceiling on that paper stands regardless of how well the tutoring goes. That conversation belongs with the school, and it should happen early rather than in the final term.

A tutor cannot fix an attendance problem, a sleep problem or a phone problem. These show up as poor concentration in sessions and get misdiagnosed as weak understanding.

And no tutor can promise a grade. Anyone who does is describing a sales position rather than a professional judgement. What can reasonably be described is a starting point, a plan, and what improvement should look like by week five: cleaner working, more complete answers, fewer questions left blank.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's school uses for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The school's subject outline or the candidate entry sheet states it plainly, and the subject teacher can confirm in a line. It is worth doing before you speak to any tutor, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, use different grade scales and run different sitting months. Revision built on the wrong board's past papers looks productive and achieves very little. Some schools also enter different subjects with different boards, so check subject by subject rather than assuming one answer covers the whole timetable.

faqs.question: How do 9 to 1 grades compare with the older A* to G scale?
faqs.answer: They are not a clean one-to-one translation, and treating them as one causes confusion. The 9 to 1 scale runs with 9 at the top, and the top of that range is deliberately more finely divided than the old A* band was. Universities and schools publish their own equivalence tables for admissions, and those tables are the ones that matter for your child's next step. Ask the school counsellor which scale each subject will be reported on and what the sixth form or Diploma entry requirement is in that scale.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE subjects still involve coursework, or is everything examined?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and the subject. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses are largely assessed by written examination. Cambridge retains optional coursework routes in a limited set of subjects, and individual schools decide whether to offer them. Many do not, because the administrative load is significant. Your school's subject outline will say which components apply. If a coursework component does exist, plan tutoring around its internal deadline as well as the exam date, since the two rarely sit conveniently apart in the calendar.

faqs.question: Can a tutor already teaching in Sector 86 or Sector 88 also take a student in Sector 87?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and this is one of the practical advantages of Sector 87's position in the middle of the sector run. A tutor with an existing commitment in a neighbouring sector can often add a consecutive slot here without adding a second journey, which makes them more willing to accept the address. It also tends to mean a fixed weekday evening rather than a flexible one, since the schedule is built around that single trip. Availability still depends on current tutor schedules and is checked at the time of enquiry.

faqs.question: My child is entered for English as a Second Language and finds writing hard. What helps?
faqs.answer: The fastest gains usually come from structure rather than vocabulary. Second language English papers reward students who can identify the text type being asked for, adopt its register and organise a response in a predictable shape. Vocabulary building helps, but it works slowly and it rarely rescues a badly organised answer. A tutor should work through past papers by question type, model one answer, then have the student produce the next under timed conditions. Regular short pieces marked properly beat occasional long ones left unmarked.

faqs.question: Should we begin tutoring in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10 begins?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 is the cheaper and calmer option if there is already a visible gap. Content is still being introduced, there is room to fix underlying weaknesses in algebra or written expression, and sessions can be less frequent. Waiting until Grade 10 usually means paying for more sessions over a shorter period, with the pressure of pre-boards in the middle. If Grade 9 is going well, waiting is entirely reasonable. The decision should follow the evidence in the reports rather than a general sense of anxiety.

faqs.question: How does a private tutor coordinate with what the school is teaching?
faqs.answer: By asking. A good tutor requests the school's scheme of work or at least the current chapter list at the start, then works either alongside it or deliberately behind it if foundations need repair. Running ahead of the school is occasionally useful and often counterproductive, because it leaves the student half-familiar with material and inattentive in class. Expect the tutor to adjust when a school test or project appears, and expect them to tell you when they are diverging from the school's order and why.

faqs.question: Can two children from the same society share a tutor and a session?
faqs.answer: It can be arranged when the two students are genuinely at a similar level in the same subject and board, and it does reduce the per-family fee. The condition matters. Pairing a student who needs foundations rebuilt with one who needs exam technique produces a session that serves neither. Where the levels do match, shared sessions can work well socially, particularly for students who find one-to-one attention intense. Availability depends on the tutor's willingness and schedule, and it is discussed case by case rather than offered as a standard package.

faqs.question: What if my child is resistant to the idea of having a tutor?
faqs.answer: Say so at the enquiry stage, because it changes which tutor suits. A reluctant Grade 10 student responds badly to someone who opens with a diagnostic test and a lecture on effort. The better first session is short, focused on one topic the student already half-understands, and ends with a small visible win. Resistance usually softens once a session stops feeling like extra school. If it does not soften after three or four sessions, the match is wrong, and it is better to change than to persist out of politeness.

contentBlocks.heading: Exam-season rescue or year-long work: two ways families in Sector 88 Gurugram use a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Enquiries from this sector cluster into two shapes, and they are almost opposites.

The first arrives in January or February. A pre-board result has landed lower than anyone expected, the final papers are ten or twelve weeks out, and the request is urgent. This work is triage. A tutor identifies which topics carry the most marks across the papers still to be sat, secures those, drills timing and question interpretation, and deliberately abandons some low-yield content. It is uncomfortable to hear, but it is what produces movement in a short window.

The second arrives quietly in Grade 9, often after a first-term report that was fine but flagged something. This work is slower and cheaper per unit of progress. Foundations get rebuilt. Habits get set. Nobody is panicking.

The same tutor is not always right for both. Triage needs someone comfortable making hard calls about what to skip, and calm with a stressed teenager. Long-term work needs patience and a willingness to go backwards into Grade 7 material when that is what the diagnosis says.

So before comparing tutors, decide which of the two situations you are in. Families frequently describe the first while hoping for the results of the second.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE subjects respond to a short push, and which do not
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject moves at the same speed under pressure, and it is worth knowing which is which before allocating a limited number of weeks.

Sciences respond comparatively well. Physics and Chemistry reward pattern recognition, standard question types recur across series, and the practical-skills component, whether sat as a practical test or as a written alternative, is largely technique. A student who understands the theory but keeps losing method marks can improve inside a term.

Extended maths depends entirely on where the gap sits. Missing topics can be taught quickly. Weak algebraic manipulation running back several years cannot, because every other topic sits on top of it.

English moves slowest. Reading comprehension and writing control develop over months, not weeks, and the honest short-window strategy is narrower: response structure, timing across the paper, and making sure every question gets attempted.

Economics and Business Studies sit somewhere in between. The content is learnable at pace; the marks are in applying it to the case in front of you and evaluating properly.

Humanities depend on source technique, which is teachable, and on content recall, which is a memory workload the student has to carry themselves.

Maths: fast if topics are missing, slow if algebra is weak
English: structure and timing only, in a short window
Economics and Business: application and evaluation marks
Humanities: source skills teachable, recall is the student's load

contentBlocks.heading: What happens between your message and the first session
contentBlocks.body:
The process is short by design, because families in the urgent group do not have weeks to spend choosing.

You send the subject, the grade, the board, the date of the next major assessment and your location within Sector 88. An advisor comes back the same day or the next, with questions rather than a pitch.

Those questions establish the diagnosis. What did the last paper look like, mark by mark if you have it. Which topics were attempted and abandoned. Whether the student is entered at Core or Extended. How many subjects genuinely need help, as opposed to how many the parent is worried about.

Then a shortlist of two or three tutors, each with their subject range, their honest availability in the coming weeks, and their fee. In exam term this last point matters, because the tutors with free evening slots in February are fewer than those with free slots in August.

You speak to them and decide. If the first session shows the diagnosis was wrong, which happens, the plan gets rewritten rather than defended.

No tutor is assigned without your agreement, and no fee is taken before you have spoken to the person teaching.

Sector 88 sits towards the outer edge of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, with Sector 87 and Sector 86 on one side and Sector 89 and Sector 90 continuing outward. That position affects tutoring in a way families closer to the old city do not experience.

A tutor coming from Golf Course Road, Sohna Road or the DLF phases is committing to a long drive in each direction. In exam term, when demand peaks, that tutor will fill their calendar with nearer students first. So the practical advice for Sector 88 is to book earlier than you think necessary and to be flexible about the day rather than the time.

The compensating factor is density. Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next sit close together, and a tutor with two students in the cluster will hold the trip in their schedule far more reliably than one making a single visit.

Access is via the Dwarka Expressway corridor and the roads running towards Sohna Road. Both are fine at 8pm and difficult at 6pm.

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year IGCSE calendar, exam series and resits
contentBlocks.body:
The qualification runs across Grade 9 and Grade 10, with options chosen at the start and papers sat at the end of Grade 10. Inside that, the year has a rhythm worth planning against.

Cambridge examines in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE offers a January sitting alongside June. Schools in Gurugram overwhelmingly enter students for the main mid-year series, with the other sittings mostly used for resits or unusual cases.

The school's own calendar sits inside that. Pre-boards typically land in December or January, coursework or project deadlines cluster near them, and study leave follows. A revision plan should be built backwards from the pre-boards first, since those are the near obstacle, and then extended to the real papers.

Resits are possible, and a student can improve a grade at a later series. It is not a comfortable route. It means carrying one subject alongside the start of A Levels or the IB Diploma, which is exactly when the workload jumps. Better to treat it as a genuine fallback rather than a plan.

Students starting the two-year course from a different curriculum should expect the first term of Grade 9 to feel harder than the rest of it.

contentBlocks.heading: Checks completed before any tutor is put forward
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor goes through the same screening, and it is described here so you can judge whether it is enough for you.

Identity is verified against a government-issued document. Academic qualifications are checked against the certificates themselves. Teaching background is covered in conversation, with specific questions about boards taught, syllabuses taught, grade levels and recency. Somebody who last taught this qualification several years ago is treated differently from somebody teaching it this term.

A subject discussion follows. The tutor is asked to explain how they would handle an actual teaching problem, for example how they would run a past-paper session so that it produces learning rather than a score, or how they would prioritise topics for a student twelve weeks out. Answers that avoid specifics end the process there.

References from previous families are requested and followed up where they exist.

What this cannot verify is whether your child will respond to that particular person. Nothing can, in advance. The first session is therefore a real trial, and asking for a different tutor after it is treated as ordinary.

contentBlocks.heading: Home and online through the Sector 88 Gurugram exam term
contentBlocks.body:
Through the ordinary part of the year, either mode works for mainstream subjects and the choice comes down to preference and slot times.

Exam term changes the calculation. From January onwards, students want more frequent and shorter contact: a forty-minute doubt session two days before a paper, a walkthrough of a mistake made in a mock, a check on a marked answer. Travelling twenty-five minutes each way for forty minutes of teaching does not survive contact with a busy calendar, and tutors quietly stop offering it.

So the pattern that holds up in Sector 88 during the run-in is a longer home session at the weekend, when travel is easy and there is room for a full timed paper, combined with short online sessions midweek for doubts and marking review.

During study leave the balance shifts further online, simply because sessions become frequent and irregular.

One caution. Short online doubt sessions are useful only if the student has attempted the work first. Used as a substitute for attempting it, they become the tutor solving papers while the student watches, which feels productive and teaches almost nothing.

A tutor who builds the recall load into the commute and reserves written work for the desk is using the week properly.

contentBlocks.heading: Six weeks before the papers: what is honestly possible
contentBlocks.body:
This is the part most tutoring pages avoid, so here it is directly.

With six weeks and one weak subject, a student who works between sessions can usually make a real difference. Marks come back from careless errors, from unattempted questions, and from a better sense of how long each section should take. That is not nothing.

With six weeks and four weak subjects, no honest tutor will tell you all four can be fixed. The conversation should be about which two carry the most value for the student's next step and which two are accepted as they are. Parents dislike this conversation. It is still the right one.

With six weeks and a foundational gap, for instance a Grade 10 student who cannot reliably rearrange an equation, the ceiling is set by that gap and not by effort.

A useful way to run past papers, and a reasonable thing to ask a tutor to do: sit the paper under timed conditions, mark it against the official mark scheme, then log every lost mark under one of four causes, concept not known, method wrong, careless error, or not attempted. Two papers logged that way tell you more than a month of general revision.

Send the subject, the grade, the board, your society within Sector 88, and the date of the next assessment that matters. That last detail changes the whole shortlist, because urgency and availability are the binding constraints in this sector.

An advisor will ask about the last paper the student sat, about tier, and about how many subjects genuinely need help rather than how many are causing worry. Expect a realistic answer on availability rather than an eager one. Home slots across the New Gurgaon societies depend on which tutors currently travel this far out, and that changes month to month.

Two or three names follow, with fees attached, and you speak to them yourself before anything is agreed. There is no charge for the matching conversation, and no obligation to continue after the first session if it does not suit.

If you are early, in Grade 9 or the first half of Grade 10, the sensible move is a slower start with fewer sessions and a longer horizon. If you are late, ask directly what the tutor proposes to skip. A tutor who says nothing will be skipped has not looked at the calendar properly.

And if the student is the one resisting the idea, mention it. It changes which of the shortlisted names is likely to work in the room.
