faqs.question: We have about twelve weeks until the papers. Is it already too late to start?
faqs.answer: Twelve weeks is enough for real movement in one or two subjects, provided the student works between sessions. It is not enough to teach two years of missing content across five subjects, and anyone who suggests otherwise is selling. Expect the first session to be spent deciding what gets attention and what gets accepted as it is. Marks in a short window usually come from timing, from attempting every question, and from removing careless errors rather than from new content. Start with the subject where the next step depends most on the grade.

faqs.question: How should past papers actually be used, rather than just collected?
faqs.answer: Sit one under timed conditions with no notes. Mark it against the official mark scheme, which is stricter than self-assessment and reveals what the examiner rewards. Then classify every lost mark under one of four causes: the concept was not known, the method was wrong, it was a careless slip, or the question was not attempted. Each cause has a different fix, and only the first needs teaching. Most students who do many past papers without this step improve very little, because they never separate what they cannot do from what they simply did not do carefully.

faqs.question: Do the grade boundaries change from one exam series to another?
faqs.answer: Yes. Boundaries are set after each series so that a given grade represents a comparable standard even if that particular paper was harder or easier than usual. This means the raw mark needed for a grade is not fixed, and a boundary quoted from an older series is a rough guide rather than a target. Practically, it removes the temptation to aim for a precise mark and refocuses attention on the number of questions attempted and completed properly. Your school can share recent boundary data for the subjects it enters.

faqs.question: Can my child resit a single IGCSE subject later if the grade disappoints?
faqs.answer: Resits are permitted, and the available sitting depends on the board. Cambridge examines in June and November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE also offers a January window. The practical difficulty is timing rather than permission. A resit generally falls in the first months of Grade 11, exactly when A Level or IB Diploma work becomes demanding, so the student carries two loads at once. It is a reasonable fallback for one subject that went badly. It is a poor plan to rely on in advance.

faqs.question: How many subjects can one tutor realistically handle for the same student?
faqs.answer: Two related subjects is comfortable for many tutors, for example Physics and Chemistry, or Maths and Physics. Three starts to stretch depth, and a tutor offering to cover five subjects across sciences, maths and humanities is usually offering supervision rather than subject teaching. There is a place for supervised study, especially for a disorganised student, but it should be described accurately and priced accordingly. If several distinct subjects need real teaching, two tutors on different evenings usually works better than one generalist.

faqs.question: Is intensive daily tutoring during study leave a good idea?
faqs.answer: In moderation. Study leave exists so students can practise independently, and filling every day with sessions removes the practice the sessions are supposed to prepare them for. A workable shape is one session every second day, each ending with specific work to complete before the next. Watch for exhaustion, which shows up as sessions where the student agrees with everything and retains nothing. If that appears, reduce frequency rather than pushing harder. A rested student sitting a paper outperforms a saturated one fairly reliably.

faqs.question: Sector 88 is fairly far out. Will a tutor still travel here during exam term?
faqs.answer: Some will, and the odds improve considerably if a booking is made before demand peaks in January. Tutors fill their calendars from the nearest addresses outward, so a request made in October holds a slot that the same request in February would not get. Existing commitments in Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next also help, since a tutor already visiting the cluster will add a second student more readily. All of this remains subject to individual schedules and is confirmed at the time.

faqs.question: What is worth doing in the summer between Grade 9 and Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Repair rather than acceleration. The break is the best window for fixing algebraic manipulation, written expression or scientific terminology, because there is no school deadline competing for attention. Two or three sessions a week for a few weeks on one foundational weakness produces more value than racing ahead into Grade 10 content, which the school will teach properly anyway. A student who returns in Grade 10 able to rearrange equations confidently has removed the single most common cause of lost marks across maths and the sciences.

faqs.question: How can we tell whether the tutoring is working before results arrive?
faqs.answer: Look at the log of lost marks across successive past papers rather than at the total score, which fluctuates with paper difficulty. Concept errors should fall first, then method errors. Careless slips fall slowly and never reach zero. Also watch how the student behaves with an unfamiliar question: attempting it, even badly, is a better sign than a slightly higher mark achieved by avoiding it. And ask for the tutor's short session record. If nobody can describe what changed over four weeks, that is the answer.

mainEntity.name: We have about twelve weeks until the papers. Is it already too late to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Twelve weeks is enough for real movement in one or two subjects, provided the student works between sessions. It is not enough to teach two years of missing content across five subjects, and anyone who suggests otherwise is selling. Expect the first session to be spent deciding what gets attention and what gets accepted as it is. Marks in a short window usually come from timing, from attempting every question, and from removing careless errors rather than from new content. Start with the subject where the next step depends most on the grade.

mainEntity.name: How should past papers actually be used, rather than just collected?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sit one under timed conditions with no notes. Mark it against the official mark scheme, which is stricter than self-assessment and reveals what the examiner rewards. Then classify every lost mark under one of four causes: the concept was not known, the method was wrong, it was a careless slip, or the question was not attempted. Each cause has a different fix, and only the first needs teaching. Most students who do many past papers without this step improve very little, because they never separate what they cannot do from what they simply did not do carefully.

mainEntity.name: Do the grade boundaries change from one exam series to another?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Boundaries are set after each series so that a given grade represents a comparable standard even if that particular paper was harder or easier than usual. This means the raw mark needed for a grade is not fixed, and a boundary quoted from an older series is a rough guide rather than a target. Practically, it removes the temptation to aim for a precise mark and refocuses attention on the number of questions attempted and completed properly. Your school can share recent boundary data for the subjects it enters.

mainEntity.name: Can my child resit a single IGCSE subject later if the grade disappoints?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resits are permitted, and the available sitting depends on the board. Cambridge examines in June and November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE also offers a January window. The practical difficulty is timing rather than permission. A resit generally falls in the first months of Grade 11, exactly when A Level or IB Diploma work becomes demanding, so the student carries two loads at once. It is a reasonable fallback for one subject that went badly. It is a poor plan to rely on in advance.

mainEntity.name: How many subjects can one tutor realistically handle for the same student?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two related subjects is comfortable for many tutors, for example Physics and Chemistry, or Maths and Physics. Three starts to stretch depth, and a tutor offering to cover five subjects across sciences, maths and humanities is usually offering supervision rather than subject teaching. There is a place for supervised study, especially for a disorganised student, but it should be described accurately and priced accordingly. If several distinct subjects need real teaching, two tutors on different evenings usually works better than one generalist.

mainEntity.name: Is intensive daily tutoring during study leave a good idea?

acceptedAnswer.text: In moderation. Study leave exists so students can practise independently, and filling every day with sessions removes the practice the sessions are supposed to prepare them for. A workable shape is one session every second day, each ending with specific work to complete before the next. Watch for exhaustion, which shows up as sessions where the student agrees with everything and retains nothing. If that appears, reduce frequency rather than pushing harder. A rested student sitting a paper outperforms a saturated one fairly reliably.

contentBlocks.heading: The First Question in Sector 89 Gurugram: Cambridge or Edexcel?
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE tutors in Sector 89 Gurugram are usually being hired for one of two examination boards: Cambridge International, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. That single fact changes the syllabus code, the number of papers, the tiering and sometimes the grading scale you will be reading in the report. Confirm it before you shortlist anybody.

The quickest check is the front page of any past paper the school has handed out. A Cambridge question paper carries a four-digit subject code and the Cambridge Assessment International Education wordmark. A Pearson paper carries a longer alphanumeric code and the Edexcel name. Some schools serving New Gurgaon enter students for Cambridge in the sciences and Edexcel in mathematics, so check subject by subject rather than assuming one board covers the whole timetable.

After that the questions get smaller and far more useful. Is your child on the Core or the Extended tier in each subject. Which series is the school entering for. Is there a practical component, an alternative-to-practical written paper, or coursework sitting behind the theory papers.

A tutor who can answer those questions in the first conversation is worth more than one who simply says they teach the subject. And a tutor who asks you those questions before quoting a fee is usually the safer bet.

contentBlocks.heading: Sitting at the Dining Table in Godrej Air, or Sharing a Screen
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition in Sector 89 works well for one structural reason and struggles for another. It works because the residential blocks here are dense and self-contained. A tutor already teaching inside Godrej Air or Godrej Summit can reach a second student in the same complex without touching a main road, which makes two back-to-back evening slots realistic in a way they rarely are on Golf Course Road.

It struggles because Sector 89 sits at the western edge of New Gurgaon, and most experienced IGCSE subject teachers live closer to the older sectors. A tutor coming from Sohna Road after 6 pm is committing to a long return trip for a ninety-minute session. Fees quoted for travel like that reflect the travel, and cancellations rise in the monsoon.

Online changes the arithmetic completely. A screen share of a marked Paper 4 script, with the mark scheme open alongside it, is arguably clearer than leaning over the same sheet at a dining table. Annotation is legible. Nothing gets lost between sessions.

Many families in Vatika India Next and Mapsko Casa Bella end up splitting the week: one session at home for the subject that needs pace-setting, one online for the subject that needs a specialist. That split is worth asking about rather than choosing one mode for everything.

contentBlocks.heading: Maths 0580, the Sciences, and the Papers That Decide the Grade
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the subject Sector 89 parents ask about most often, and it is also where the tier decision bites hardest. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, syllabus 0580, is entered at either Core or Extended. Core caps the grade a student can be awarded; Extended opens the top of the scale but brings in material that is genuinely harder. A student sitting in the middle of a Core class who wants a top grade needs a tier conversation, not more worksheets. Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics runs Foundation and Higher tiers on similar logic.

The sciences separate students differently. Cambridge Biology, Chemistry and Physics each combine a multiple-choice paper, a written theory paper and a practical component that a school will either run as a laboratory test or replace with the alternative-to-practical written paper. Students who are strong in theory frequently drop marks on the practical component because nobody drilled variables, tables and graph plotting with them.

Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science reward structure rather than volume. Marks there hang on command words, data response technique and the discipline of answering only what was asked.

Exact codes, weightings and paper durations vary by syllabus year, so confirm them against your school's specification rather than trusting any tutor's memory.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 89 Sits, and Who Can Realistically Reach It
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 89 is bounded by Sector 88 and Sector 87 on one side and Sector 90 and Sector 91 on the other, all inside the same New Gurgaon residential belt. Practically, that means a tutor who accepts a slot here is drawing on a pool of students spread across four or five adjacent sectors, and their schedule is built around that geography rather than around any single family.

The Dwarka Expressway is the thing that actually matters. It pulls tutors in from Dwarka and the western Delhi border far more efficiently than the internal Gurugram roads pull them from Sohna Road or the DLF phases. Families sometimes assume a tutor from central Gurugram is closer. On a Tuesday evening they usually are not.

Sessions here also compete with distance from schools. Buses serving the international schools this catchment feeds into can put a Class 10 student home well after 4.30 pm, and a 5 pm start is optimistic for anyone with a commute of their own.

If your preferred slot is before 6 pm, say so early. It narrows the pool sharply, and it is better to know that at the shortlist stage than after two weeks of rescheduling.

contentBlocks.heading: Class 9 to Class 11: What Changes, and When to Start
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is a two-year course in most schools, and the two years behave nothing alike. The first year is about coverage and vocabulary. Students meet the syllabus content, learn the notation, and start recognising what a question is actually asking. Tutoring in this year is cheapest in effort terms because there is time to fix a weak foundation properly.

The second year is about examination technique under a clock. Content revision still happens, but the marginal mark comes from timing, from knowing which questions to leave, and from writing answers that a marker can award points to without hunting.

Younger students in Sector 89 often come from the Cambridge Lower Secondary route, and support there looks different again: reading fluency, number sense, and getting comfortable writing an explanation rather than an answer.

After the final series, students split. Some continue into AS and A Level, some into the IB Diploma at a different school. That destination should influence subject choices made two years earlier, particularly around Additional Mathematics and the sciences.

Starting in the last term before the exams is possible. It is also the least effective use of money, and an honest tutor will tell you what can and cannot be recovered in that window.
items: Year one: coverage, notation, question recognition
Year two: timing, mark scheme literacy, paper discipline
Lower Secondary support: fluency before technique
Subject picks shaped by AS Level or IB Diploma plans

contentBlocks.heading: How an Enquiry From Sector 89 Gurugram Becomes a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately short, and it runs in five steps.

One. You send the subject, the board if you know it, the year group and two time windows that genuinely work on a weekday. Two. An advisor calls and asks for something concrete: a marked paper, a term report, or a specific topic the student named as the problem. Three. That request is translated into a tutor brief, which is usually more specific than the original enquiry. A parent says maths; the brief says Extended tier, algebraic manipulation and trigonometry, Class 10, needs pace not revision.

Four. A small shortlist is prepared from tutors whose availability fits the slots you gave, with fee ranges attached. Nobody is presented as the only option. Five. You speak to the tutor before committing, and the first session is used to diagnose rather than to teach a full topic.

What this process cannot do is conjure a specialist for a rare subject into a 5 pm home slot in Sector 89. Where that clash happens, the honest answer is an online match at a later hour.

Matching is subject to tutor availability, and availability in the weeks before a series is tighter than it is in August.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the Mark Scheme Instead of the Report Card
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is long enough to judge a tutor, provided you know what to look at. School reports are too slow and too coarse for this, and a mid-term grade will not tell you whether the sessions are working.

Look at corrections instead. Ask to see the last piece of written work the tutor marked. A useful tutor's annotations quote the mark scheme language back at the student: the word the answer was missing, the working that was not shown, the unit that was dropped. A less useful tutor writes a tick and a score.

Second, listen to how the student describes the session afterwards. A student who says they did questions has had a passive hour. A student who says they finally understood why a two-mark answer needed two distinct points has had a productive one.

Third, check whether homework set by the tutor is being attempted before the next session. If it is not, the problem is usually the volume or the pitch, and it is fixable by saying so.

Progress in IGCSE subjects is uneven. A student can gain ten marks in one paper and stall in another for a month, and that is normal rather than a sign the match has failed.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Asked of a Tutor Before Their Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a set of questions, and the questions are specific enough that a generalist struggles with them.

A tutor is asked which boards they have taught the subject for, and at which tier. Cambridge Extended and Edexcel Higher are not interchangeable, and someone who has only ever taught Core will say so if asked directly. They are asked to talk through a past paper question and the marks behind it, which reveals more in three minutes than a résumé does.

Identity and qualifications are verified. Teaching history is checked, including which age groups they have actually taught rather than which ones they are willing to take. For home sessions, the areas they can genuinely reach on a weeknight are recorded, because a tutor who overstates their range becomes a cancellation four weeks later.

If a match is wrong, say it early. Changing tutors in week two costs nothing except an awkward call. Changing in month four costs a term.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is sitting Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Look at a past paper the school has issued. Cambridge papers carry a four-digit subject code and the Cambridge Assessment International Education name; Pearson papers carry a longer alphanumeric code and the Edexcel name. If you cannot find one, the subject teacher or the exams officer will confirm it in a sentence. Check per subject rather than for the school as a whole, because some schools mix boards across the timetable. The board determines the paper structure a tutor should be preparing your child for, so it is worth confirming before the first session.

faqs.question: Should we take the Core tier or the Extended tier in maths?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, which enters students, but you should understand what it means. Core covers less content and caps the grade a student can be awarded. Extended reaches the top of the scale and includes material that is meaningfully harder. A student who is comfortable in a Core class but wants a top grade needs the tier conversation with the school early, ideally in the first year rather than the second. A tutor can tell you honestly whether the jump looks realistic from where the student currently is, given the time left.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring practical inside Sector 89, or should we plan for online?
faqs.answer: Both are workable, and the deciding factor is usually the hour rather than the address. Tutors already teaching inside Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next can fit a neighbouring student in easily. A tutor travelling in from the older Gurugram sectors after 6 pm is a longer proposition, and that shows up in fees and in cancellation rates during the monsoon. For a common subject at a reasonable hour, home works. For a specialist subject or a late slot, online usually produces the stronger match.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees near Sector 89 usually depend on?
faqs.answer: Four things move the number. The subject, because specialist sciences and Additional Mathematics have a smaller pool of tutors than general maths. The year group, since final-year examination work is more demanding to prepare. The mode, because home sessions carry travel time and online does not. And the timing, since a 5 pm weekday slot is scarcer than an 8 pm one. Fee ranges are shared with the shortlist rather than quoted before anyone understands the requirement, and they are ranges because tutors set their own rates.

faqs.question: My child scores well in class tests but drops marks in the actual papers. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost always this is a mark scheme problem rather than a knowledge problem. Class tests reward recognising the topic. Board papers reward answering the specific command word, showing the working that carries method marks, and stopping when the question has been answered. A student who writes a page for a two-mark question is losing time they need elsewhere. The fix is unglamorous: timed past paper sections, marked against the real scheme, with the student doing the marking themselves for a few weeks until the pattern becomes visible.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with science practicals if the sessions are online?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it depends on which component the school enters. Where students sit the alternative-to-practical written paper, online works well because that paper tests experimental reasoning on paper: reading apparatus, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, identifying variables and sources of error. All of that can be drilled through a screen. Where a school runs an actual laboratory test, the handling skills have to be practised in the school lab, and a tutor can only prepare the thinking around them. Ask which component applies before deciding on mode.

faqs.question: Which exam series should we be planning towards?
faqs.answer: Most schools in this part of Gurugram enter students for the June series, with November available as an alternative or resit route depending on board and subject. Pearson also offers a January series for some International GCSE subjects, and Cambridge runs an India-specific series in some subjects. Your school decides which, and the answer shapes the revision calendar considerably. Ask the exams officer for the entry dates rather than working backwards from a general assumption, then build the tutoring plan around the actual timetable.

faqs.question: We are starting in Class 10 with six months left. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: Not too late to help, but late enough that the plan has to change. With six months, the realistic work is examination technique, targeted topic repair on the highest-weighted areas, and timed paper practice. Rebuilding a shaky foundation across an entire two-year syllabus is not achievable in that window, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. Choose two subjects rather than five, be specific about which papers matter, and accept that some gains will show and some will not. Nobody can guarantee a grade from this position.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to be wrong for our child?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor and the match will be changed. The signals worth acting on are early ones: the student cannot describe what was covered, the marked work has no substantive corrections on it, or sessions keep getting rescheduled from the tutor's side. None of that improves with time. Changing in week two costs an awkward conversation. Changing in the fourth month costs a term of progress. A mismatch is a scheduling and personality outcome as often as a competence one, and nobody involved should treat it as a complaint.

A student who is comfortable in a Core class but wants a top grade needs the tier conversation with the school early, ideally in the first year rather than the second. A tutor can tell you honestly whether the jump looks realistic from where the student currently is, given the time left.

mainEntity.name: Is home tutoring practical inside Sector 89, or should we plan for online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are workable, and the deciding factor is usually the hour rather than the address. Tutors already teaching inside Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next can fit a neighbouring student in easily. A tutor travelling in from the older Gurugram sectors after 6 pm is a longer proposition, and that shows up in fees and in cancellation rates during the monsoon. For a common subject at a reasonable hour, home works. For a specialist subject or a late slot, online usually produces the stronger match.

mainEntity.name: What do IGCSE tuition fees near Sector 89 usually depend on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four things move the number. The subject, because specialist sciences and Additional Mathematics have a smaller pool of tutors than general maths. The year group, since final-year examination work is more demanding to prepare. The mode, because home sessions carry travel time and online does not. And the timing, since a 5 pm weekday slot is scarcer than an 8 pm one. Fee ranges are shared with the shortlist rather than quoted before anyone understands the requirement, and they are ranges because tutors set their own rates.

mainEntity.name: My child scores well in class tests but drops marks in the actual papers. What is happening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost always this is a mark scheme problem rather than a knowledge problem. Class tests reward recognising the topic. Board papers reward answering the specific command word, showing the working that carries method marks, and stopping when the question has been answered. A student who writes a page for a two-mark question is losing time they need elsewhere. The fix is unglamorous: timed past paper sections, marked against the real scheme, with the student doing the marking themselves for a few weeks until the pattern becomes visible.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with science practicals if the sessions are online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partly, and it depends on which component the school enters. Where students sit the alternative-to-practical written paper, online works well because that paper tests experimental reasoning on paper: reading apparatus, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, identifying variables and sources of error. All of that can be drilled through a screen. Where a school runs an actual laboratory test, the handling skills have to be practised in the school lab, and a tutor can only prepare the thinking around them. Ask which component applies before deciding on mode.

mainEntity.name: Which exam series should we be planning towards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most schools in this part of Gurugram enter students for the June series, with November available as an alternative or resit route depending on board and subject. Pearson also offers a January series for some International GCSE subjects, and Cambridge runs an India-specific series in some subjects. Your school decides which, and the answer shapes the revision calendar considerably. Ask the exams officer for the entry dates rather than working backwards from a general assumption, then build the tutoring plan around the actual timetable.

mainEntity.name: We are starting in Class 10 with six months left. Is that too late?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not too late to help, but late enough that the plan has to change. With six months, the realistic work is examination technique, targeted topic repair on the highest-weighted areas, and timed paper practice. Rebuilding a shaky foundation across an entire two-year syllabus is not achievable in that window, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. Choose two subjects rather than five, be specific about which papers matter, and accept that some gains will show and some will not. Nobody can guarantee a grade from this position.

mainEntity.name: What if the tutor turns out to be wrong for our child?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell the advisor and the match will be changed. The signals worth acting on are early ones: the student cannot describe what was covered, the marked work has no substantive corrections on it, or sessions keep getting rescheduled from the tutor's side. None of that improves with time. Changing in week two costs an awkward conversation. Changing in the fourth month costs a term of progress. A mismatch is a scheduling and personality outcome as often as a competence one, and nobody involved should treat it as a complaint.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE tutors in Sector 90 Gurugram: the habits that decide the grade
contentBlocks.body:
Most families here come to tutoring after a report card, not before one. By then the problem is rarely the content. It is the habit.

A student who reads the chapter, highlights it and calls that revision will sit a Cambridge or Edexcel paper and find that almost nothing transfers. IGCSE papers do not reward recognition. They reward retrieval, under a clock, in the words the mark scheme is looking for. Highlighting produces a warm feeling of familiarity and very few marks.

So the first useful thing a tutor does is look at how the week is actually spent. Two long hours on a Sunday afternoon are worth less than four twenty-minute retrieval blocks spread across the week. An error log, kept honestly, is worth more than either. Students who write down every question they lost marks on, with a line explaining why, tend to stop repeating the same handful of mistakes by the third month.

This shapes tutor selection more than parents expect. A tutor who only re-teaches the chapter is running school again, slower and at your cost. The one worth keeping asks to see the last three school tests, marks a past paper answer in front of your child using the real mark scheme, and shows why a 'describe' answer earned two marks where 'explain' would have earned four.
items: Short retrieval blocks instead of long re-reading sessions
One error log per subject, reviewed at month end
Mark scheme opened alongside every past paper attempt
Command words drilled: state, describe, explain, suggest, calculate
Last three school tests brought to the first session

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 90 Gurugram enquiry becomes a shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
The matching runs in four steps, and none of them are automated guesses.

One. An advisor calls and asks for specifics: which board the school enters students for, the exact subject list, which two papers are the problem, the grade the school has predicted, and how many evenings a week are genuinely free after activities. Vague answers here produce vague matches later.

Two. We filter for the combination rather than the subject name. A tutor comfortable with Extended Mathematics is not automatically comfortable with the Additional Mathematics that some Sector 90 students take alongside it. A Chemistry tutor who has only taught the alternative-to-practical route is a different person from one who has run laboratory sessions.

Three. You receive a short shortlist with each tutor's teaching background, the boards they have worked with, and whether they can reach your society or would be better online. Two or three names, not twenty.

Four. A trial session, after which you say yes, no, or ask for a different profile. Changing at this stage is normal and costs you nothing but a week.

Availability depends on level, subject and the slot you need. A weekday afternoon is easier to fill than a nine o'clock Saturday. We will tell you which is which before you plan around it.
items: Advisor call covering board, papers, predicted grade and free evenings
Filtering on subject plus level, not subject name alone
Shortlist of two or three profiles with teaching background
Trial session before any commitment
Slot feasibility flagged upfront, not after you have planned

contentBlocks.heading: Maths, the sciences, and the two subjects nobody plans for
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is where most enquiries start. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics runs as syllabus 0580, split into a Core tier and an Extended tier, and the tier your child sits caps the top grade available. Students who take Additional Mathematics, syllabus 0606, alongside it are effectively carrying an extra subject with calculus in it, and that combination needs a tutor who has actually taught both.

Sciences split three ways. Separate Physics, Chemistry and Biology run as 0625, 0620 and 0610. Coordinated Sciences, the double award, is 0654. Which route your school offers changes the depth of the content and the number of papers, so confirm the route before buying any book.

The two subjects that surprise parents are English and Economics. English First Language demands directed writing and close comparison of unseen texts, and strong spoken English does not carry a student through it. Economics, syllabus 0455, punishes students who memorise definitions without being able to draw and label a diagram under time pressure.

Paper durations and weightings do get revised between syllabus cycles. Take the codes as your starting point and confirm the current paper structure with your school's subject teacher rather than an old past-paper pack picked up secondhand.
items: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Core and Extended tiers
Additional Mathematics 0606 as a genuine extra subject
Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610
Coordinated Sciences 0654 for the double award route
Economics 0455: diagrams under time pressure, not definitions
Confirm current paper structure with the school before buying material

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the board question behind every plan
contentBlocks.body:
Parents often assume IGCSE is one thing. It is two, and the difference is practical.

Cambridge International reports most IGCSE subjects on the A* to G scale, with 9 to 1 grading used on certain syllabuses. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 scale. A parent comparing a cousin's certificate to their own child's is often comparing two different scales and drawing the wrong conclusion.

Exam series differ too. Cambridge runs June and November series, with a March series available to schools in India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and June. That January window matters for a student who wants an early attempt at one subject, and it does not exist on the Cambridge side, so a family cannot simply move a plan from one board to the other.

Tiering is the decision with the longest tail. Core covers a narrower content set and caps the maximum grade. Extended opens the top grades and carries more content and harder papers. Schools usually decide by the end of Grade 9 or early Grade 10, and moving up a tier late is possible but uncomfortable.

A tutor matched for your child should know which board the school enters students for before the first session, not after it.
items: Cambridge: A* to G on most subjects, 9 to 1 on some
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: 9 to 1 grading
Cambridge series: June, November, plus March in India
Edexcel series: January and June
Core caps the top grade; Extended opens it and adds content

contentBlocks.heading: Sectors 88, 89, 91 and 92: the travel radius that actually works
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 90 sits in the newer residential belt of New Gurgaon, with Sector 89 and Sector 88 on one side and Sector 91 and Sector 92 on the other. For tutoring, that geography has one consequence worth stating plainly: a tutor already teaching a student in Sector 91 can usually add a Sector 90 slot the same evening. A tutor whose other students are on Sohna Road or nearer the Dwarka Expressway junction cannot, at least not at six in the evening.

This is why the honest answer to 'do you have a tutor near me' is often 'not for that hour'. The tutor exists. The traffic does not cooperate.

Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next are the addresses that come up most often in enquiries from this sector, and they cluster tightly enough that a tutor can string two sessions together across two societies. That works in your favour on price and on reliability, because a tutor with a second student nearby is far less likely to cancel.

What this belt does not have is the density of walk-in tuition centres found in the older sectors. Most families here end up with home sessions, online sessions, or a mix of the two.
items: Sector 89 and Sector 88 to one side, Sector 91 and Sector 92 to the other
Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella, Vatika India Next

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix for families in Sector 90 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition wins on one thing above all: a student who cannot avoid the session. For a Grade 9 student still building discipline, having someone physically at the dining table on Tuesday and Thursday does more than any app. It also lets the tutor watch the working, not the answer, and catch the moment a student silently gives up on a question.

The cost of home tuition is rigidity. The tutor's travel dictates the slot, cancellations cost you the hour, and your subject choice narrows to whoever can reach Sector 90 at the time you need.

Online reverses both. A specialist in a less common subject, or one who has taught the Edexcel papers for years, becomes available regardless of where they live. Late slots after nine become possible. And the recording of a worked solution can be replayed the night before a test.

But online asks something of the student. Fifteen minutes of pretending to listen is easier on a screen than at a table, and a weaker student can hide behind a muted microphone for a full hour.

Many families settle on a mix: home for the subject that needs supervision, online for the one that needs a specialist.
items: Home tuition for accountability and watching the working
Online for specialist subjects and post-nine slots
Recorded worked solutions for the night before a test
Home slots limited by tutor travel across New Gurgaon
Hybrid split by subject rather than by week

contentBlocks.body:
Families from this sector are usually enrolled at one of a small set of international schools spread around the city: Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School near Golf Course Road, Pathways World School, and GD Goenka World School out towards the Sohna Road side. A child leaving before seven in the morning and reaching home after four is not going to absorb a demanding Physics session at half past four. Push it to six and the same student is workable. Parents who ignore this and book the earliest slot available usually rebook within a fortnight.

These schools also differ in which board they enter students for and which science route they run, which is exactly why we ask for the school name during the first call. It tells us more about the paper structure than the subject list does.

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a tutor reaches your shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is not a badge on a profile. It is a set of questions a tutor has to answer convincingly before we send their name anywhere.

We confirm identity and academic background against documents, and we ask which boards they have actually taught, for how long, and at which levels. A candidate who has taught the state board for a decade may be excellent and still be wrong for Extended Mathematics on a Cambridge syllabus.

Then there is a subject conversation. A tutor is asked to explain how they would teach a topic that students commonly get wrong, and to talk through a mark scheme for a past paper question. This is where the difference between knowing a subject and being able to teach it under IGCSE marking conventions shows up, quickly.

We also check the practical things. Whether they can genuinely reach the societies in this sector at the hour you need. Whether their internet setup holds up for a full online session. Whether they will write a short note after each session rather than leaving you to interrogate your child.

No screening process is perfect. If a tutor turns out to be wrong for your child, tell us early and we will look again.
items: Identity and qualification documents verified
Board and level experience checked, not just subject
Live discussion of a commonly misunderstood topic
Mark scheme walkthrough during the interview
Travel feasibility and connection quality confirmed

contentBlocks.heading: Four weeks in: what should have changed
contentBlocks.body:
Nobody can promise you a grade, and any platform that does is selling something it cannot deliver. What we can describe is what a working arrangement looks like a month in, so you have something concrete to measure against.

By week four your child should be able to tell you, without being coached, which two topics they were weakest on and what changed. There should be a visible pile of attempted past paper questions with marks written on them. The tutor should have sent short notes after sessions, and those notes should name topics rather than repeating that the session went well.

You should also see a shift in the questions your child asks. Early on it is 'what is the answer'. Later it becomes 'why did the mark scheme want that word'. That change is the actual signal, and it usually appears before the marks do.

What you should not expect in four weeks is a jump of two grades. Content gaps built over a year do not close in a month, and a tutor who claims otherwise is managing your expectations badly.

If none of this is visible after a month, that is a reason to have a conversation with us, not to wait another term.
items: Student can name their two weakest topics unprompted
Attempted past paper questions with marks recorded
Post-session notes that name topics, not moods
Questions shift from answers to mark scheme reasoning
One month is not enough to close a year-long gap

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with IGCSE tutors in Sector 90 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one conversation. Share the board, the subjects, the grade the school has predicted, and the two evenings you can actually protect. An advisor will tell you honestly whether a home tutor can reach your society at that hour or whether online is the better first move.

Bring three things to that call and it goes faster. The school name, because it tells us the board and the science route. The last two report cards or test papers, because they show where marks are leaking rather than where you think they are. And a realistic weekly window, because a slot that fights with football practice will be abandoned by week three.

After the call you receive a small shortlist, not a directory. You pick one, run a trial session, and decide. If the fit is wrong, say so and we look again.

Availability varies by subject and by time of day, and the weeks before an exam series are the hardest to book into. Starting the conversation a term early costs nothing and gives you a wider choice of tutors than starting it a fortnight before mocks.

Shortlist, then a trial session, then a decision

faqs.question: My child studies for hours but the marks are not moving. What is actually going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the study method rather than the effort. Reading and highlighting build familiarity, and IGCSE papers do not test familiarity. They test whether a student can produce the right point, in the right language, against a clock. Switch to closed-book retrieval, timed past paper questions, and self-marking against the real mark scheme, and the gap between hours studied and marks earned starts to close. A tutor should be diagnosing this in the first two sessions rather than starting from chapter one again.

faqs.question: Should we begin tuition in Grade 9 or wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 is the cheaper time to start, because you are fixing habits and filling gaps while there is still slack in the calendar. Grade 10 tuition often turns into damage control, with content revision and exam technique competing for the same hours. Starting early does not mean four sessions a week. One weekly session in the subject your child finds hardest, held steadily through Grade 9, usually does more than an intensive push in the last term. Start later only if you must.

faqs.question: Which societies in Sector 90 can a home tutor realistically reach?
faqs.answer: Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next come up most often, and they sit close enough together that a tutor can teach in two of them on the same evening. Feasibility still depends on the hour. A slot before seven in the evening competes with traffic from the older sectors, so a tutor may be able to offer a later time or none at all. The advisor will tell you which hours are workable before you plan around them.

faqs.question: What does the first session with an IGCSE tutor actually cover?
faqs.answer: A good first session is mostly diagnosis. The tutor looks at recent school tests, asks the student to attempt a past paper question, and marks it aloud against the mark scheme to see where the loss is happening. Sometimes it is content. Often it is command word confusion, poor working, or running out of time. By the end of the hour you should have a rough plan naming which topics get attention first and why, rather than a promise about grades.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Mathematics and Physics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor across both subjects sees the algebra problems that show up in Physics numericals. But it depends on the level. A tutor comfortable with Extended Mathematics and Physics at 0625 is common enough. A tutor covering Additional Mathematics as well is rarer, and pushing one person across three demanding syllabuses usually thins the preparation. Two focused tutors often beat one stretched one, subject to what your schedule and budget allow.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for IGCSE tuition here?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the subject, the level, whether the session is at home or online, and how experienced the tutor is with the specific board. Home sessions cost more than online because the tutor is paying for travel time. Sciences at Extended level and Additional Mathematics usually sit at the higher end. An advisor gives you an indicative range for your exact combination before any trial is arranged, so you are not comparing quotes after the fact.

faqs.question: We are unhappy with the tutor after three sessions. What happens then?
faqs.answer: Tell us rather than pushing through. Three sessions is enough to know whether the working relationship is right, and personality mismatches are common with teenagers. We ask what specifically is not working, because 'my child does not like him' and 'he never marks anything' lead to different replacements. A fresh shortlist is arranged and you run another trial. Changing once is normal. Changing three times usually means the brief needs revisiting rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: Is Extended always the better choice over Core?
faqs.answer: No, and pushing a struggling student into Extended can cost them the grade they would have earned comfortably on Core. Extended opens the higher grades and carries harder papers and more content. Core caps the maximum grade but gives a student a realistic shot at finishing the paper. The right question is what the child needs for the next stage of schooling. Discuss it with the subject teacher, who has seen the internal test data, and treat a tutor's view as a second opinion.

faqs.question: How many past papers should be attempted before the board series?
faqs.answer: Quantity matters less than what happens after each one. A student who attempts twenty papers and never marks them properly learns little. One paper a week, done under timed conditions, self-marked against the mark scheme, with every lost mark written into an error log, builds more than daily unmarked attempts. In the last two months the frequency rises, but the marking discipline is what carries the improvement. A tutor should be checking the error log, not just supplying more papers.

contentBlocks.heading: Online IGCSE tutors in Sector 91 Gurugram: what a screen does well
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the honest version, because most pages skip it.

Online tutoring has three real advantages and they are not the ones usually advertised. The first is match. A family in Sector 91 looking for someone who has taught the Pearson Edexcel Physics papers for eight years is choosing from the whole country online, and from a handful of people within driving distance otherwise. The second is time of day. Sessions after nine in the evening are ordinary online and nearly impossible at home, because no tutor wants to drive back across New Gurgaon at eleven. The third is repeatability. A worked solution captured on screen can be watched again the night before a test, which a whiteboard at your dining table cannot.

Now the other side. A screen makes it easy for a fifteen-year-old to look engaged while doing nothing at all. Practical technique cannot be taught properly through a webcam. And a student who writes slowly, or whose working is a mess, will hide both unless the tutor insists on seeing the page.

The families who get the most out of online are the ones who use it selectively, keep a camera on the notebook rather than only the face, and pick a room without a television in it.

Post-nine evening slots that home tutors cannot offer
Worked solutions replayable before a test

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE subjects survive a screen and which fight it
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics adapts best. A shared whiteboard, a tutor watching each line of algebra as it appears, and immediate correction of a sign error works as well remotely as in person, provided the student writes where the camera can see.

Economics and Business Studies adapt almost as well, since both live on structured written answers and diagrams that can be annotated live. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics Specification A, coded 4MA1, and the Cambridge equivalents both revolve around question-by-question technique that a screen handles fine.

Sciences are split. Theory papers work online. Practical work does not. If your school enters students for the practical test rather than the alternative-to-practical paper, a tutor cannot substitute for time in the laboratory, and anyone claiming otherwise is overselling. What a tutor can do remotely is drill the reasoning: identifying variables, spotting the flaw in a described method, reading a results table for the anomaly.

Languages are the hardest case. Speaking components and unseen comprehension both benefit from a person in the room, and long writing tasks are painful to mark over a video call unless the student photographs and sends the work in advance.

Syllabus codes and paper structures do change between cycles. Confirm the exact specification your school follows before building a plan around any of this.
items: Mathematics: strongest fit for online, if working stays visible
Economics and Business Studies: diagrams annotate well live
Science theory online, practical technique in the laboratory
Edexcel Mathematics Specification A carries the code 4MA1
Languages: speaking and long writing need more effort remotely

contentBlocks.heading: Core, Extended, and a tier decision that is hard to reverse
contentBlocks.body:
Two boards dominate IGCSE entries in this part of the city, and they behave differently enough to matter.

Cambridge International offers many subjects at two tiers. Core covers a reduced content set and limits the highest grade a candidate can earn. Extended covers more and opens the top of the scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses Foundation and Higher tiers in the same spirit on subjects such as Mathematics. Whichever the school follows, the tier is generally settled well before the final year, and moving a student up late means covering extra content while everyone else is revising.

Grading also differs. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 scale. Cambridge reports most subjects on A* to G, with 9 to 1 on certain syllabuses. Parents comparing certificates across two schools are often comparing two different scales.

The series calendar is the third difference. Pearson Edexcel runs January and June sittings. Cambridge runs June and November, with a March series available to schools in India. A January attempt at one subject is a genuine option on one board and not on the other.

Ask your school which board, which tier and which series before you shortlist a tutor. Those three answers change who is suitable.

Tier decisions taken early and awkward to reverse
Edexcel reports 9 to 1; Cambridge mostly A* to G
Edexcel sittings in January and June
Cambridge sittings in June and November, March in India

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition in Sector 91 Gurugram when the tutor has to drive
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor gives you something online cannot fake: a person your child cannot mute. For students who need supervision more than they need explanation, that alone justifies the higher fee.

The constraint is arithmetic. A tutor coming into Sector 91 spends time on the road that nobody is paying for, so they will want either a longer session or a second student nearby. Both of those shape what you can book. Ask for a forty-five minute slot at six in the evening and you will find very few takers. Ask for ninety minutes twice a week, and the same tutor becomes interested.

Society access adds friction that families underestimate. Gate registration at Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next takes a few minutes on the first visit and occasionally longer if the tutor is not pre-registered. Sorting that out before session one saves an argument at the gate.

Hybrid is what most families in this sector eventually run. One subject at home where the student needs a physical presence, one online where the specialist lives elsewhere. It is less tidy than picking a single mode, and it works better.

Home availability stays subject to tutor schedules and is thinner during exam months.

contentBlocks.heading: From the first call to the trial session
contentBlocks.body:
Matching is deliberately a conversation rather than a form.

An advisor asks which board the school enters students for, the subject list, the tier, the papers causing trouble, and what the weekly calendar really looks like once school transport and activities are removed. Parents often quote availability that includes hours the child spends travelling. We would rather find that out on the call than after two cancelled sessions.

We then look for tutors matched on the combination rather than the label. Somebody who has taught Cambridge Chemistry theory is not automatically the right person for a student sitting the practical test route. A tutor strong at Foundation tier Mathematics may be the wrong choice for a student aiming at the top of the Higher tier.

You get two or three profiles with teaching background, board experience and mode. Then a trial session, which exists so you can judge the teaching rather than the CV. Ask the tutor afterwards what they think the actual problem is. A useful answer names a topic or a technique. A vague answer tells you something too.

Availability depends on subject, level and the slot you want, and can be reviewed with an advisor before you rearrange anything at home.

contentBlocks.heading: Screening a tutor you may never meet in person
contentBlocks.body:
Online matching raises the bar on checks, because you lose the informal read you get from a person standing at your door.

Identity and academic documents are verified first. Beyond that we ask for specifics that are hard to bluff: which boards, which syllabuses, which tiers, over how many years, and what the tutor does differently for a student on Extended compared with one on Core. Answers that stay general do not progress.

Each candidate then talks through a past paper question and its mark scheme. Marking is where teaching ability shows. A tutor who can explain why an answer scored two out of four, and what wording would have earned the other two, is worth more than one who can solve the question quickly and cannot explain the marking.

For online work we also check the boring infrastructure: a stable connection, a writing surface the camera can see, and a habit of sending a short written note after the session. Parents who never receive notes end up relying on their child's summary of how it went, which is not a reliable source.

Screening reduces risk. It does not remove it, and we would rather hear early that a match is not working.

School calendars matter as much as timings. Internal assessments, mock weeks and project deadlines cluster, and a tutor who has taught students from the same school knows when those weeks fall and adjusts rather than pushing new content into them.

When you call, name the school. It tells us the board, the likely science route and the rhythm of the term far more efficiently than a subject list does.

contentBlocks.heading: The things we will not put in writing
contentBlocks.body:
We do not promise grades. Not a 9, not an A*, not a fixed improvement over a term. Anyone who does is guessing with your money, because the outcome depends on the student's starting point, the time left, and how much of the work happens between sessions rather than during them.

We also do not publish tutor counts or claim to be endorsed by any school or examination board. IB Gram is an independent platform. It arranges tutors and checks them, and that is the whole of the offer.

What can be described honestly is process. You get an advisor call, a short shortlist, a trial session, and the option to change if the fit is wrong. Sessions get written notes. Fees are quoted as a range for your specific subject and level before anything is booked, so there is no discovery later.

The honest limitation: a tutor cannot compensate for a student who does nothing between sessions. Two hours a week against a syllabus built over two years only works if the practice happens in the gaps. Families who accept that early tend to be happier at the end of the year than families who expected the tutor to carry it alone.

contentBlocks.body:
One call sets this up. Tell an advisor the school, the board, the tier if you know it, the subjects that are slipping, and which evenings survive after transport and activities. faqs.question: Does online tuition genuinely work for a Grade 10 student who gets distracted easily?
faqs.answer: It can, but only with structure around it. Put the session in a room without a television, angle the camera at the notebook rather than the face, and ask the tutor to make the student narrate their working aloud. A student explaining each step cannot drift for long. If none of that helps after three or four sessions, that is useful information, and a home tutor who is physically present is probably the better spend for that particular child.

faqs.question: How is practical work handled if the tutor is never in the room?
faqs.answer: It is handled partly, and it is fair to say so. Laboratory technique needs the laboratory, and school is where that happens. A remote tutor can still do a great deal of the thinking that practical papers assess: choosing variables, spotting the weakness in a described method, reading a results table for the anomalous value, calculating uncertainty and writing conclusions that answer the question asked. If your school enters students for the practical test rather than the written alternative, treat online support as a complement to school work, not a substitute.

faqs.question: What do we need at home in Sector 91 for online sessions to work properly?
faqs.answer: Less than most people expect. A reliable connection, a laptop or tablet with a usable microphone, a quiet room, and something to write on that the camera can see. A cheap phone stand pointed at the notebook solves the single biggest problem in online tutoring, which is a tutor who cannot see the working. Headphones help in a busy flat. A second screen is a luxury, not a requirement, and no paid software is needed from your side.

faqs.question: Can we start online and move to home sessions later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families in this sector do exactly that, usually when a subject turns out to need closer supervision than expected. Moving mode may mean moving tutor, since the person teaching your child online may live nowhere near New Gurgaon. Tell the advisor early so the shortlist accounts for it. Where an existing tutor can travel to your society, continuity is preserved and only the fee and the timing change, both of which are agreed before the switch.

faqs.question: My child writes slowly. Will online sessions make that worse?
faqs.answer: Only if the sessions are run badly. A tutor who lets the student type everything is quietly training the wrong skill, because the exam is still handwritten. Ask for handwritten work photographed and shared, and for at least one timed written section every week. Slow writing is a real exam risk and it improves with deliberate practice against a clock. Raise it in the trial session so the tutor builds it into the plan rather than discovering it in March.

faqs.question: Do you support Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, or only one board?
faqs.answer: Both, and the board is one of the first things an advisor asks about, because it changes the paper structure, the grading scale and the exam series. Tutors are shortlisted against the board your school actually enters students for. If you are unsure which one it is, the answer sits on your child's statement of entry or with the school office, and it is worth confirming before the first session so nobody prepares from the wrong specification.

faqs.question: Are online sessions recorded, and can we watch them?
faqs.answer: Recording depends on the tutor and on what everyone agrees at the start. Many tutors are comfortable recording worked solutions or a specific explanation for later revision, which is one of the genuine benefits of online work. Full recording of every session is a separate matter and needs consent from both sides. Agree the position before the first session rather than asking mid-term, and treat any recordings as revision material for the student rather than something to circulate.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a session?
faqs.answer: Short interruptions are normal and tutors usually reconnect within a minute or two. For a longer outage the standard expectation is that the lost time is made up, either by extending a later session or by rescheduling. Agree this in the first week so it is not an argument later. If drops become frequent from the tutor's side, tell us, because reliability is part of what we screen for and repeated failures are grounds to look at another profile.

faqs.question: Are late evening slots available for students in this sector?
faqs.answer: Online, often yes, and that is one of the clearer advantages of remote sessions here. A tutor teaching at nine in the evening online is not facing a drive back afterwards. Home tutors rarely offer that hour, and the ones who do usually want a longer session to justify the trip. Availability still depends on subject and level, and the later slots fill first during exam months, so ask early if a late timing is the only one that works.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE tutors in Sector 92 Gurugram: this week, this month, this term
contentBlocks.body:
Three different decisions get bundled into one phone call, and separating them makes the whole thing easier.

This week is about diagnosis. Pull out the last two graded papers and find out where the marks actually went. Not the subject. The topic, and the type of error. A student losing four marks a paper to unit conversion has a different problem from one who never finishes the last question. Ten minutes with a red pen tells you more than a month of worrying.

This month is about arrangement. Finding a tutor, running a trial, agreeing a slot the family can keep, and settling the fee before anyone starts. Rushing this produces a tutor who is convenient rather than suitable, and you discover the difference in week six.

This term is about the calendar. When are the mocks. When does the school confirm entries. Which series is your child sitting. A plan built backwards from those dates survives contact with reality; a plan built forwards from today's enthusiasm does not.

Families in Sector 92 tend to call in the second category and skip the first. Do the red pen exercise before you call and the conversation gets much shorter and much more useful.

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year IGCSE arc and where your child is on it
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is normally a two-year course, and the useful thing to know is that each stretch of it rewards different work.

The first year is content and habit. Nobody is thinking about grade boundaries yet, and that is exactly when tutoring is cheapest in effort. A weak foundation in algebra fixed now costs a fraction of what it costs to patch during revision.

The first half of the final year is where technique overtakes content. Students who know the material still lose marks to command word confusion, missing units, unlabelled diagrams and answers that describe when the question asked them to explain. This is the phase where a tutor adds the most, because the fix is teachable and quick.

The last stretch is triage. Past papers under timed conditions, marking against the real mark scheme, and choosing deliberately which topics to leave alone. Trying to cover everything in the final six weeks is how students end up thin across the board.

Boards differ on the series available. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and June sittings. Cambridge runs June and November, with a March series available to schools in India. Where the school allows it, a November sitting gives a route to reattempt one subject, and that possibility should be discussed with the school rather than assumed.
items: Year one: content gaps and study habits, cheapest to fix
Early final year: command words, units, diagram labelling
Final stretch: timed papers and deliberate topic triage

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 92 Gurugram on the map: Dwarka Expressway and the 93 side
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 92 sits with Sector 91 and Sector 90 on one flank and Sector 93 on the other, inside the newer residential belt of New Gurgaon, with the Dwarka Expressway corridor shaping most of the traffic patterns around it. That geography quietly sets your session timings.

A tutor arriving from the older sectors during the evening peak will either be late or will price the trip into the fee. A tutor already teaching in Sector 91 or Sector 93 that evening is a different proposition entirely, and that is the tutor worth waiting a week for.

Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next are the addresses we see most often from this sector. Their proximity is genuinely useful, because a tutor who can take two students in adjacent societies on the same evening has a strong reason to keep your slot rather than drop it when something closer to home appears.

The drawback of a newer belt is thinner infrastructure. There are fewer established coaching classrooms within walking distance here than in the older parts of the city, so the realistic options are a tutor at your dining table or a tutor on a screen. contentBlocks.heading: Choosing the two subjects to fix first
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every family arrives wanting help in four subjects and a budget for two. Choosing badly here wastes a term.

Pick the subject where the gap is widest first, not the one the child dislikes most. Those are often different. A student who hates Economics but scores a solid grade in it needs less help than one who is quietly two grades below expectation in Chemistry and has stopped mentioning it.

Second, pick for leverage. Mathematics is the classic case, because weakness there drags Physics numericals and parts of Business Studies with it. Fixing the algebra improves three subjects at once. English First Language is another lever, since the ability to read a question precisely and write a structured answer affects every written paper on the timetable.

Subjects with a coursework or portfolio component behave differently. Where a syllabus carries coursework, the work is produced through the year under school supervision, and a tutor's role is to support planning and review rather than to touch the submitted work. That boundary is not negotiable, and any tutor unclear about it is the wrong tutor.

Syllabus codes and component structures are revised between cycles. Confirm the current specification with the subject teacher before building a revision plan around any assumption.
items: Widest gap first, not the least-liked subject
Mathematics as a lever into Physics and Business Studies
English First Language improves every written paper
Coursework is supported, never produced, by a tutor
Confirm the current specification with the subject teacher

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars that set the pace in Sector 92 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Children from this sector travel to a familiar group of schools, among them Scottish High International School, Lancers International School, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School. Each runs its own calendar, and the calendar matters more to your tutoring plan than the syllabus does.

Mock weeks are the pivot. A tutor who knows the mock dates works backwards from them, front-loading past papers and easing off new content in the fortnight before. A tutor who does not know them introduces a new topic three days before a mock and undoes their own work.

Entry deadlines are the second date to have written down. Once entries are confirmed, tier decisions and subject counts are effectively fixed for the year, and a tutoring plan built on the assumption that something can still be changed is built on sand.

Long bus journeys are the third factor. A student leaving early and returning in the late afternoon has a short usable window before concentration goes, and the honest answer is that some evenings are simply not worth booking.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Tutors are matched to students, never presented as school staff.
items: Mock weeks decide when new content stops
Entry deadlines fix tier and subject count for the year
Long bus runs shorten the usable evening window
Some evenings are genuinely not worth booking
Independent platform, no school affiliation implied

contentBlocks.heading: A week-by-week view of getting matched
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the realistic timeline, so you can plan around it instead of hoping.

Day one, an advisor call. Board, subject list, tier, the papers causing trouble, the school, and the hours that genuinely exist in your week. Fifteen to twenty minutes if you have the marked papers open in front of you.

Within two to four days, a shortlist. Two or three tutors, each with their teaching background, the boards and levels they have worked with, and whether they can reach your society or would work better online. Not a directory to sift through.

Within the first week, a trial session. This is the part parents rush and should not. Sit near enough to hear how the tutor handles a wrong answer. Impatience shows up immediately and does not improve later.

Week two onwards, a settled rhythm with written notes after each session. By the end of week four you should be able to see attempted papers with marks on them and hear your child name their weakest topics without prompting.

Availability depends on subject, level and the slot you need, and can be reviewed with an advisor. Rare subject and awkward hour together is the combination that takes longest to fill.
