Two to four days: shortlist of two or three profiles
Week one: trial session, watched rather than assumed
Week two: settled rhythm, written notes after sessions
Rare subject plus awkward hour takes longest to fill

contentBlocks.heading: Evening slots, traffic and the case for a split week
contentBlocks.body:
The practical question is not home versus online. It is which hour you are trying to fill.

Between five and seven in the evening, a home tutor is competing with the worst traffic of the day, and the pool of people willing to make that trip into this sector is smaller than families expect. After eight, home tutors become scarce for the obvious reason that they still have to get back. Online has no such problem, which is why late slots and remote sessions go together so naturally.

Home sessions earn their higher fee where supervision is the real need. A student who will not open a book alone benefits from a person at the table more than from a better explanation. That is a behavioural problem, and it needs a physical solution.

A split week solves most of this. One home session for the subject that needs someone in the room, one online session later in the evening for the subject that needs a specialist. Fewer cancellations, better matches, and the family stops negotiating with traffic twice a week.

Home availability across Sector 92 stays subject to tutor schedules and gets noticeably tighter in the months before a series.
items: Five to seven is the hardest window to fill at home
After eight, online is realistically the only option
Home sessions justified by supervision, not explanation
Split week: one at the table, one on screen
Home slots tighten in the months before a series

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, cancellations and changing a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Money and logistics cause more friction than teaching does, so it is worth settling them in the first week.

Fees vary by subject, level, mode and the tutor's experience with your board. Sciences at the higher tier and Additional Mathematics sit at the upper end. Home sessions cost more than online because travel time is real time. An advisor gives an indicative range for your exact combination before a trial is arranged, so nothing is discovered after the fact.

Cancellations need a rule agreed on day one. Who gives notice, how much, and whether a missed session is made up or forfeited. Families that leave this vague end up arguing in exam month, when tempers are already short.

Changing a tutor is normal and should not feel like a complaint. Tell us what specifically is not working. A student who finds the tutor boring needs a different fix from one whose tutor never marks anything. A new shortlist and another trial follow.

We do not promise grades, publish tutor numbers, or claim any board or school endorsement. What is offered is a screened match, a trial, written session notes, and the option to change if it is wrong.
items: Indicative fee range given before any trial
Cancellation rule agreed in the first week
Higher tier sciences and Additional Mathematics cost more
Changing tutor is routine, not a complaint
No grade promises, no tutor counts, no claimed endorsement

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before you see anyone
contentBlocks.body:
By the time a profile reaches your inbox, several things have already been established.

Identity and academic qualifications are verified against documents. Teaching history is checked for specifics rather than adjectives: which boards, which syllabuses, which tiers, and for how many years. Somebody who has taught a national board for fifteen years may be a fine teacher and still be unfamiliar with how an international paper is marked, which is a different skill.

The subject interview is where most candidates are separated. A tutor is asked to mark a real past paper answer and justify the marks. Then to explain a topic that students routinely misunderstand, out loud, at the level of a student who has already been confused once by a teacher.

We check logistics too. Whether they can genuinely reach the societies in this sector at the hour you have asked for, or whether they are saying yes and will be late every week. Whether their setup supports a full online session. Whether they write session notes without being chased.

And we ask them what they would do if a student made no progress for a month. The answer to that is unusually revealing.
items: Documents checked before the profile is shared
Board, syllabus and tier history probed for specifics
Live marking of a past paper answer during the interview
Travel and connection realism checked, not assumed
Asked how they would handle a month of no progress

contentBlocks.heading: Talk to an advisor about IGCSE tutors in Sector 92 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the calendar rather than the wish list. Tell an advisor when the mocks fall, which series your child is entered for, and how many weeks are genuinely left. That single piece of information changes the recommendation more than anything else you can share.

Then the practical details: the school, the board, the subjects losing marks, and the two evenings that survive after transport and activities. If you have the last two marked papers, keep them open during the call.

You receive a short shortlist, then a trial session, then a decision that is yours to make. If the tutor is wrong, say so in the first fortnight rather than the second month.

One small thing that saves trouble later: register the tutor at your society gate before the first visit, and agree the cancellation notice in the same week you agree the fee. Both take five minutes now and prevent an argument during exam month, which is the worst possible time to have one.

Booking is easiest well before an exam term and hardest in the weeks immediately before one, when the good slots have already gone. Asking now what is open for your subject and your hour costs nothing and gives you a real answer instead of an optimistic one.

School, board, weak subjects, two protected evenings
Marked papers open during the advisor call
Shortlist, trial, then your decision
Ask early: the good slots go first before a series

faqs.question: We have about eight weeks until the mocks. Is it too late to begin now?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change technique on one or two subjects, and not enough to rebuild a syllabus from scratch. Used well, that time goes into timed past paper work, correcting command word errors, and cleaning up the two or three topics that appear most reliably. Used badly, it goes into racing through chapters nobody will retain. Be explicit with the tutor that the goal is marks recovered per hour rather than coverage, and expect them to skip material deliberately.

faqs.question: How soon after we enquire can sessions actually start?
faqs.answer: A shortlist usually reaches you within a few days of the advisor call, and a trial is often arranged inside the first week. The variable is the slot you want. A weekday afternoon fills quickly; a specific hour on a Saturday evening for a less common subject can take longer. Availability depends on subject, level and timing and can be reviewed with an advisor before you rearrange the family calendar around a start date that has not been confirmed yet.

faqs.question: If a grade goes badly in June, is there a route to reattempt the subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes, depending on the board and on what your school permits. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson Edexcel offers January as well as June, so a single weak subject need not sit on the certificate unchallenged. The decision is the school's to administer, since entries go through them, so raise it with the coordinator rather than assuming. Tutoring for a reattempt is usually narrow and paper-focused, which makes it shorter and cheaper than a full year of support.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to fix Mathematics or Chemistry first?
faqs.answer: Look at leverage and at the size of the gap. Mathematics tends to pull other subjects up with it, because algebra weakness shows up again in Physics numericals and in quantitative Chemistry. If both gaps are similar, start with Mathematics. If the Chemistry gap is much larger, or if a specific component such as the written practical alternative is the problem, start there. An advisor will ask for both sets of marks before suggesting a sequence rather than guessing from subject names.

faqs.question: Is the trial session charged?
faqs.answer: Trial arrangements vary by tutor, and the position is confirmed with you before it is scheduled rather than left ambiguous. What matters more is using the hour properly. Give the tutor a marked paper in advance, sit close enough to hear how they respond to a wrong answer, and ask afterwards what they think the underlying problem is. A specific diagnosis is worth paying for. A confident promise about grades is not, and should make you cautious.

faqs.question: Our society has strict gate rules. How does a home tutor get in?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor with the society office or through your visitor management app before the first session and the problem disappears. Turning up unregistered at Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next can cost fifteen minutes of a paid hour and starts the relationship badly. Ask the tutor for the name and number they will use for entry, share it with the gate in advance, and confirm whether repeat entries need renewing monthly.

faqs.question: Can sessions be paused during school exam weeks or family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, with notice. Most tutors are used to pauses around school assessments and holidays, and many prefer them to sessions where the student arrives exhausted. Agree the notice period in the first week so a pause does not turn into a disagreement about payment. One caution: pausing through a long summer break and restarting in the final year is where a lot of momentum is lost, so consider a reduced schedule instead of a complete stop.

faqs.question: Does every IGCSE subject include coursework?
faqs.answer: No. Many subjects are assessed entirely by written examination, while others carry a coursework or portfolio component that is produced during the year under school supervision. Which applies depends on the syllabus and on the route your school has chosen, so confirm it with the subject teacher rather than assuming from another student's experience. Where coursework exists, a tutor may help with planning, structure and review, but the work must be the student's own and the school's rules on it apply.

faqs.question: How far in advance should we book for the exam term?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. The months immediately before a series are when demand peaks, and the tutors with strong board experience are the first to fill. A family arranging support a full term ahead usually gets a choice of profiles and a preferred slot. A family calling six weeks before papers begin gets whatever remains, which may mean a different hour or an online match instead of a home tutor. Availability is subject to tutor schedules throughout.

heroSubtitle: Sector 93 sits deep in New Gurgaon, which makes the evening clock the first thing worth solving. We check which tutors can realistically reach Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next at the hour you need, then match by board, tier and the exact papers your child sits.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 93 Gurugram can be arranged at home inside the New Gurgaon societies or online across the city, for Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE students in Grade 9 and Grade 10, with younger and older siblings supported from Grade 1 to Grade 12. Matching starts with the board and tier your school has entered your child for, then the evening window that actually works from Sector 93. Availability depends on subject, level and schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: Quarter Past Six on a School Night in Sector 93, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
It is quarter past six. Your daughter came through the Godrej Air gate a little after half four, has eaten, and there is a Cambridge IGCSE Physics structured-question paper due tomorrow that she has not opened. The tutor a neighbour recommended teaches near Sohna Road and cannot reach Sector 93 before eight. That is the real problem most families here bring us, and it is a timetable problem before it is an academic one.

Sector 93 is one of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, well away from the older parts of the city, and the travel arithmetic is unforgiving. A tutor coming across from Golf Course Road gives up close to an hour each way on a weekday. So the first question we ask is not which subject. It is which window: weekday evening, early morning before the bus, or a longer weekend afternoon.

Once that window is fixed, the rest becomes solvable. IGCSE tutors in Sector 93 Gurugram can be matched by board first, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, then by tier, then by the specific papers your child has been entered for. A student on Core Mathematics needs different practice from one on Extended, and swapping a tutor between the two without noticing is a common and expensive mistake.

We will also say plainly when a slot is not realistic. Some combinations of subject and hour simply do not exist near this cluster.

Board confirmed: Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
Core or Extended tier checked at the start

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 93 Sits Between Sector 92, Sector 91 and Sector 95
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 93 belongs to a run of New Gurgaon residential sectors built out at roughly the same time, so its immediate neighbours matter far more than the city-level address does. Sector 92 and Sector 91 sit alongside it. Sector 95 is the next stop along. The whole cluster feeds onto shared approach roads that run towards the Dwarka Expressway on one side and Sohna Road on the other.

For tutoring, that geography has a blunt consequence. A tutor already teaching a student inside Mapsko Casa Bella or Vatika India Next can often add a second family in Godrej Summit without adding any travel at all, which is why back-to-back slots within the same cluster are the ones most likely to be offered and the least likely to be cancelled. A request for one isolated hour at an awkward time is much harder to fill.

Parents who have moved here from South City 1, Nirvana Country or DLF Phase 1 usually notice the difference within a month. There are fewer walk-in options nearby than in the older sectors, and the centres that do exist tend to be board-agnostic rather than built around Cambridge or Edexcel specifications.

That gap is real and we would rather name it. It is also why online tuition carries more weight from Sector 93 than it does for a family living beside the Rapid Metro corridor.

Approach roads towards Dwarka Expressway and Sohna Road

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions Inside Godrej Air, or a Screen After Dinner
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition suits younger students and anyone who needs a person sitting beside them while they actually write. A Grade 9 student working through Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry structured questions often needs someone watching the pen rather than the screen, catching the moment a mole calculation goes sideways instead of reading about it a week later in a marked script.

It works badly after about eight in the evening. A tutor who has spent an hour getting into New Gurgaon arrives flat, the student is already tired, and the session quality drops in a way nobody mentions on the phone afterwards.

Online is the honest answer in three situations. Late slots, where travel would eat the session. Unusual subject and paper combinations, such as a second language option or Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics, where the pool of local specialists is thin. And the fortnight before a series, when short frequent contact beats one long weekly visit.

Hybrid is common inside these societies: one home session a week for supervised writing practice, one shorter online session for doubt-solving and feedback on marked work. Families in Vatika India Next often build this around a working parent's return time.

Before the first session, ask what the tutor uses to write on screen. A tablet and stylus changes an online maths lesson entirely, and a webcam pointed at a notebook does not.

After eight in the evening, quality usually drops
Online: late slots, scarce subjects, pre-exam revision bursts
Hybrid: one home session plus one online doubt-solving slot
Ask about stylus and screen-sharing setup before booking

contentBlocks.heading: The IGCSE Subjects Sector 93 Gurugram Parents Ask About First
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics dominates the enquiries. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) is tiered: Core is capped well below the top grades, while Extended gives access to the full range. Recent series have split the assessment across a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, so confirm the exact paper numbers your school enters with the school itself before buying any practice material. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A (4MA1) runs on Foundation and Higher tiers instead, with two papers per tier. An IGCSE maths tutor in Sector 93 should know which of these your child is sitting before the first lesson, not after it.

Sciences come next. Cambridge Physics (0625), Chemistry (0620) and Biology (0610) each pair a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper matched to the tier with a practical component, and that component is either a laboratory practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Which one a student sits is a school decision, and it changes how the last two months of revision should be spent.

English splits in a way parents often miss. First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510 or 0511) are different qualifications with different demands, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful for the other.

Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science round out most requests. Marks in all of them are lost on command words rather than content.

Edexcel International GCSE Maths Spec A (4MA1): Foundation and Higher
Sciences 0625 / 0620 / 0610 with practical or alternative-to-practical

contentBlocks.heading: From Your First Message to a Shortlist of Two or Three Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
The process is short on purpose. First, you tell us the board, the syllabus codes if the school has shared them, the grade, the tier and the two or three time windows that genuinely work from Sector 93. Second, we filter for tutors who can serve this part of New Gurgaon in those windows, either in person or online. Third, you get a shortlist of two or three profiles, each with what that tutor has actually taught and where they can reach. Fourth, there is an introductory conversation or a trial session so the student meets them before anything is committed. Fifth, we check in at around four weeks.

That fourth week matters more than the first. By then a working arrangement shows three things: the student can attempt a full past-paper question without prompting, the tutor can point to specific marks being gained rather than general improvement, and homework between sessions is being done.

If none of that is visible, we would rather change the tutor than wait out a term. Changing early costs a fortnight. Changing in February costs a grade.

We do not send a long list. Three names a parent can actually compare beats twelve profiles nobody reads.

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 and Grade 10 Are Not the Whole Cambridge Pathway
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE occupies two years, usually Grade 9 and Grade 10, but the difficulties that surface there are often built earlier and paid for later. Most Cambridge schools run a lower secondary stage before it, with an internal or external checkpoint assessment around Grade 8. Students who coasted through that stage on memory rather than method tend to hit a wall in the first term of Grade 9, when questions stop asking what and start asking why.

The other pressure point sits at the far end. What a student takes at IGCSE shapes what they can pick up in Grade 11, whether that is A Level or an IB Diploma. Dropping a science at Grade 9 because it looked hard closes doors that reopen only with difficulty two years later. A tutor worth having will raise this in October of Grade 10, not in June.

Support is available from Grade 1 upwards, and younger siblings in these societies are often taught in the same visit. Primary work looks different: reading fluency, number sense, written expression. It should not become a worksheet factory.

Older students in Grade 11 and Grade 12 can also be matched, though those requests need more lead time because the specialist pool is smaller.

The Grade 8 to Grade 9 jump: method replaces memory
Grade 10 subject choices shape Grade 11 options
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported, siblings often in one visit
Grade 11 and 12 requests need longer lead time

contentBlocks.heading: The Schools Behind Most IGCSE Enquiries from Sector 93, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Families in this cluster send children to a fairly predictable set of campuses. contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Reaches Your Door
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers what can actually be verified, and we are specific about the boundary. Identity documents are checked. Claimed qualifications are checked against certificates. Teaching history is discussed in detail, including which boards and which grade levels, because someone who has taught Class 10 CBSE Mathematics for a decade is not automatically ready for Extended 0580 question papers.

There is a subject conversation with each tutor, not a form. It usually includes marking a short piece of student work or talking through how they would explain one topic that students commonly get wrong, such as electrolysis products or rearranging a formula with a variable on both sides. That conversation filters more candidates than any document does.

References are requested where a tutor has taught in a school or with another platform. Not everyone has them, and a tutor without references is not automatically rejected, but the gap is noted on the profile you see.

What we cannot do is guarantee character or outcomes. No screening process predicts whether a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will work well together. That is what the trial session and the four-week review are for, and you should use both.

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Honest Limits and What We Will Not Promise
contentBlocks.body:
Fees are not a single number, and anyone quoting one before hearing the details is guessing. What moves them: the tier and grade, how scarce the subject is, whether sessions run at home or online, travel distance into New Gurgaon, session length, and how experienced the tutor is with the specific board. A weekly Extended Mathematics slot at seven in the evening and a Saturday morning ESL slot are not priced the same, and they should not be.

Here is the part we will not soften. Nobody can guarantee a grade. We do not publish success rates, we do not quote score improvements, and we will not tell you a number of sessions that produces a 9. What we will describe is process, and what you should be able to see after four weeks.

Starting late limits what is realistic. A student who begins in March for a June series can usually repair technique and exam approach across one or two subjects. Rebuilding two years of missing foundations in three subjects at that point is not something honest tutoring can offer, and we will say so rather than take the booking.

Availability is always conditional. Some slots can be reviewed but not confirmed until a tutor's own schedule settles.

faqs.question: We live in Godrej Summit. Can a tutor come inside the society, or do sessions happen elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Home sessions inside the society are usually the arrangement, held in your own flat with a parent at home or nearby. Entry follows whatever the society gate procedure is, so you will need to register the tutor as a regular visitor in the app or register your building uses. We do not book common-area rooms or club spaces on your behalf, and we have no arrangement with the society management. If in-flat sessions are not workable for you, online is the practical alternative from this cluster.

faqs.question: My son is on Core Mathematics and wants a top grade. Can he move to Extended part way through the year?
faqs.answer: Only the school can change the entry, and there is a deadline for it, so speak to the maths coordinator before doing anything else. Core caps the grade a student can be awarded, which is why the request comes up so often around Grade 10. Whether the move is wise depends on how much of the Extended-only content he has never seen: it is genuinely more material, not just harder questions. A tutor can assess that gap in two sessions and give you an honest read before you commit.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Ask the science department directly, because it is decided by the school and not by the student. The distinction matters more than most parents expect. A laboratory practical test rewards handling apparatus, recording readings and working safely under time pressure. The written alternative rewards reading an experimental description, spotting the variable that was not controlled, and interpreting a table you never collected yourself. Revision for the two looks quite different in the final six weeks, so it is worth confirming early rather than in April.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who has taught Cambridge IGCSE handle a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE student?
faqs.answer: Often yes for the content, less often for the exam technique, and the second one is where marks live. The two boards overlap heavily on syllabus material but differ on paper structure, tier naming, calculator rules and the phrasing of questions. A tutor who has only marked Cambridge scripts may miss what an Edexcel examiner rewards. When you enquire, name the board explicitly and we will filter for it rather than assuming the syllabus content is close enough.

faqs.question: We are three months from the June series. Is that enough time to fix two subjects?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the problem is technique rather than missing content. Three months of focused past-paper work, with proper marking against the mark scheme, moves students who understand the material but answer the wrong question. If your child has genuinely not covered whole topics, three months across two subjects is tight and something will be sacrificed. A tutor should tell you which of those two situations you are in after the first two sessions, and you should ask for that assessment directly.

faqs.question: What does a first session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Usually a diagnostic rather than teaching. The tutor will ask what the school has covered, look at recent marked work or a mock script, and set a few questions across different difficulty levels to see where the answers break down. Expect them to watch how your child writes an answer, not only whether the answer is right. By the end you should get a short verbal summary: what is solid, what is shaky, and what the first four sessions will target. If none of that happens, say so early.

faqs.question: Sector 93 is far from the older sectors. Does that push fees up?
faqs.answer: Travel distance is one of the things that affects a home tuition fee, so a tutor coming from Golf Course Road for a single hour will usually quote higher than one already teaching two families in your cluster. That is the main reason we try to place tutors who can hold back-to-back slots nearby. Online removes the travel factor entirely and often opens a wider choice of specialist for the same budget. Fees are discussed openly before any trial, not after.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the concept but keeps losing marks in exams. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command word. An IGCSE question that says describe wants observations, one that says explain wants a reason, and one that says suggest will accept a sensible answer that was never taught in class. Students who answer the question they expected rather than the question printed lose marks on material they know perfectly well. Working through past papers with the mark scheme open, line by line, fixes this faster than re-teaching the topic does.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named because Sector 93 families genuinely attend them and it helps us match a tutor to the specification and pace your child is working at. We do not represent any school, we cannot influence admissions or internal assessment, and we do not pass information to a school office unless you ask us to and arrange it yourself.

contentBlocks.heading: What Sector 95 Gurugram Parents Search For, and What Actually Moves the Grade
contentBlocks.body:
The typical search is a subject plus a pin code. IGCSE maths tutor Sector 95. Science tuition near me. It is a reasonable way to start, and it is almost never the thing that turns a 5 into a 7.

Open a marked script and the cause is usually one of four. Content that was never covered properly, often two or three topics rather than the whole syllabus. Method marks dropped because working was skipped and only a final answer written down. Timing, where the last twelve marks are attempted in four minutes. Or a misread instruction, where a student explains when the paper asked them to describe.

Those four need different tutors. Someone excellent at re-teaching electrolysis is not automatically the person who trains a student to lay out working so an examiner can award partial credit. Booking generic extra hours against the wrong cause is how a family spends a term and sees nothing change.

So IGCSE tutors in Sector 95 Gurugram get matched after a look at recent work, not before it. Send a mock script, a class test, anything with a marker's pen on it. Ten minutes with that beats an hour of description on a call.

And if the marked work suggests the school is already handling it well, we will say that too.
items: Four common causes: content gaps, method marks, timing, misread instructions
Marked script requested before any tutor is suggested
Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE both supported
Grade 1 to Grade 12, concentrated in Grade 9 and Grade 10

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 95 Enquiry Becomes Two or Three Named Profiles
contentBlocks.body:
There are five questions we need answered, and they take about six minutes on a call.

Which board and which syllabus codes. Cambridge and Edexcel look similar from outside and behave differently inside, particularly on tier names, calculator rules and paper timings. Which tier the school has entered the student for. Which grade and which term, because November of Grade 10 is a different brief from August of Grade 9. What the marked work shows. And which hours are genuinely free once school, transport and the one activity nobody will drop are accounted for.

With those answers we search tutors who match the diagnosis, not just the subject label, and who can serve this part of New Gurgaon at the hour named. You then receive two or three profiles. Each says what that tutor has taught, which boards, which grade levels, and whether they can attend in person or work online only.

After that it is a trial session, then a review at roughly four weeks. The review is where most of the value sits, because a tutor who cannot yet point to a specific improvement after four weeks is unlikely to produce one in twelve. Changing at that point is normal and costs very little.

Search runs on the diagnosis, not the subject label alone
Two or three profiles with real teaching history
Trial session, then a four-week review
Changing tutor early is treated as normal, not failure

contentBlocks.heading: Checkpoint, IGCSE, and the Fork at the End of Grade 10
contentBlocks.body:
Cambridge schools generally run a lower secondary stage up to Grade 8, sometimes with a checkpoint assessment at the end of it, before the two IGCSE years begin. That earlier stage is where study habits form. A student who reached Grade 8 by remembering worked examples usually copes until the first Grade 9 paper asks for an explanation, and then the marks drop sharply while the parent is told nothing has changed.

The two IGCSE years then carry an unusual load: six to nine subjects assessed externally, often for the first time in a child's life.

At the end of Grade 10 there is a fork. A Level, or an IB Diploma, or another route entirely. Subjects dropped at IGCSE narrow that choice, and a student who let Physics go in Grade 9 will find Physics at Grade 11 painful rather than impossible. This is worth a conversation in the autumn term of Grade 10, while options are still open.

Below all of this, primary and middle-grade tutoring is a different craft. Reading stamina, number fluency, writing a paragraph that holds together. Handing a nine-year-old a worksheet pile is easy and mostly useless, so ask any tutor how they would spend a Grade 4 session before you book one.
items: Lower secondary and checkpoint stage precede Grade 9
Six to nine externally assessed subjects across the IGCSE years
Grade 10 subject drops narrow Grade 11 choices
A Level or IB Diploma decision made while IGCSE is still running
Primary sessions judged by method, not worksheet volume

contentBlocks.heading: Three Ways Sessions Run in Sector 95, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition is the default request and it earns its place for a particular kind of student: the one who will not start work unless someone is physically present, or who is young enough that a screen becomes a toy. Sessions run in your flat, at a table, with a parent somewhere in the house.

Online suits a different student. Independent enough to sit alone for an hour, needing a specialist rather than a generalist, or wanting frequent short contact rather than one weekly appointment. It also removes the travel penalty, and from Sector 95 that penalty is real, since a tutor crossing from the older parts of the city loses most of an hour each way.

Hybrid is the arrangement families settle into most often after a month. One in-person session for supervised written practice under something like exam conditions, one shorter online slot for marking feedback and doubt-solving before a class test.

One honest warning about online: it fails for students who are actively avoiding the subject. A camera is easy to sit behind while nothing happens. If your child has been quietly not doing homework for two months, book in person first and move online later once the habit is rebuilt.
items: In person: reluctant starters and younger students
Online: independent students, scarce specialisms, short frequent contact
Hybrid: supervised writing plus marking feedback
Travel penalty from older sectors is substantial
Online is a poor first choice for avoidance behaviour

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by Subject: Where IGCSE Marks Leak Away
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) runs on Core and Extended tiers, with Core capped below the top grades and Extended covering additional content rather than merely harder versions of the same questions. Recent series separate a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper, so confirm the paper numbers with the school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A (4MA1) uses Foundation and Higher tiers across two papers. The leak here is almost always unshown working.

Sciences. Physics (0625), Chemistry (0620) and Biology (0610) each combine a multiple-choice paper, a tier-matched theory paper, and a practical component that is either a laboratory test or a written alternative-to-practical. Students revise the theory and ignore the practical component until April. That is the leak.

English. First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510 or 0511) are separate qualifications. Reading responses lose marks for retelling the passage instead of analysing it.

Economics and Business Studies. Data-response and case-study questions reward using the stimulus material. Students who answer from memory, ignoring the extract in front of them, cap themselves.

Across all of them, an IGCSE science tutor in Sector 95 should be working from past papers and the mark scheme by the second month, not from notes alone.

Working shown earns method marks even when the answer is wrong
Practical or alternative-to-practical: confirm which one with the school

Data-response answers must use the extract provided
Mark schemes in use from month two onwards

Fees vary with tier, subject scarcity, session length, mode and travel distance into New Gurgaon. They are quoted before a trial rather than after a month, and a tutor who will not discuss them plainly is not one to book.

contentBlocks.heading: The Screening a Tutor Passes Before You Meet Them
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor goes through an identity check and has claimed qualifications matched against documents. That part is administrative and unremarkable.

The conversation is where candidates fall away. A tutor is asked which boards they have taught, which grade levels, how many cohorts, and what they would do with a specific weak answer. Someone applying to teach Extended Mathematics might be shown a script where a student has written a correct final answer with no working, and asked what they would say next. The useful replies are concrete. The unhelpful ones talk about building confidence and never mention the mark scheme.

References are requested where a tutor has worked in a school or through another platform. Plenty of good tutors have none, so their absence is disclosed on the profile rather than treated as disqualifying.

Two things are outside our reach and we would rather state them than imply otherwise. We cannot verify how a tutor will behave over six months, and we cannot predict chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular teenager. The trial session exists precisely because paperwork does not answer either question, and you are entitled to say no after it without explaining why.

Trial session is the real test of fit

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IGCSE Tutor in Sector 95, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start by sending the board, the subjects, the grade and, if you have it, a photograph of a recent marked paper. That last item does more work than anything else you can share. A script with a marker's comments on it tells us within minutes whether the problem is content, method, timing or instruction-reading, and that determines which tutor is worth your evening.

Then tell us the hours that are actually free from your building on a weekday, and whether a Saturday block is possible. We would rather hear two honest windows than five optimistic ones that collapse in week three.

An advisor comes back with what Sector 95 can genuinely support: which windows can be filled in person from within the cluster, which are better served online, and where a specialist simply is not available at that hour. faqs.question: Why do you ask for a marked paper before suggesting a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because two students with the same score usually need different help. One has gaps in three topics. Another understands everything and writes answers so compressed that method marks vanish. A third runs out of time and leaves the last page blank. A marked script shows which of those you are dealing with in about ten minutes, and it stops us matching on subject name alone. If you have no marked work, a short diagnostic in the first session serves the same purpose.

faqs.question: Is Sector 95 too new to have enough IGCSE tutors nearby?
faqs.answer: The local pool is thinner than in the older sectors, which is honest rather than fatal. Tutors already teaching in Sector 93 or inside the same societies can usually add a slot without extra travel, so timings next to an existing booking get filled quickly. Awkward isolated hours are harder. Online removes the constraint completely and often gives access to a stronger subject specialist than the immediate area holds, particularly for less common subjects or the Edexcel specifications.

faqs.question: My child writes only the final answer. Does that really cost marks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more than most parents expect. Extended and Higher tier questions carrying three or more marks are structured so that partial credit is available for correct method even when the arithmetic fails at the end. A student who writes one line loses everything on a slip that would otherwise have cost a single mark. Retraining this takes a few weeks of supervised written practice, and it is one of the fastest sources of improvement available in a maths or physics paper.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week are sensible for a Grade 10 student?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one weekly session with real homework between is usually enough, moving to two in the final two months. For two subjects, two sessions on different days works better than doubling up on one evening. Beyond three tutored subjects the child stops having time to consolidate anything, and school work starts slipping to make room. If you feel you need four, the honest conversation is about the school fit, not the tutoring schedule.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover both Mathematics and Physics?
faqs.answer: Often yes at IGCSE level, and it can be convenient for scheduling and cost. The overlap in algebra, graphs and rearranging equations is genuine, so a good maths and physics tutor reinforces both. The risk is dilution when both subjects are weak, since an hour split across two subjects becomes two half-lessons. Where both are seriously behind, separate tutors and separate days generally produce better results, and we will say which situation your marked work suggests.

faqs.question: What if my child does not get on with the tutor after two sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor. There is no argument to be had about it, and you do not owe a detailed justification. Fit between a teenager and a tutor is not predictable from a profile, which is why the trial session and the four-week check exist. Changing early costs a fortnight of momentum. Persisting with a bad match through a full term costs considerably more, and we would rather absorb the first than watch you pay the second.

faqs.question: Do sessions continue during school holidays and study leave?
faqs.answer: They can, and study leave is often when tutoring earns most, because the student finally has daytime hours free. Many families increase to two or three sessions a week during that period and use them for timed past papers rather than teaching. Long holidays are different. Some tutors travel, so continuity through Diwali or the summer break should be agreed in advance rather than assumed. Ask about it at the trial stage so nobody is surprised in the middle of a plan.

faqs.question: My daughter attends Scottish High International School. Do you work with the school directly?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. We match tutors to the syllabus and tier a student is following, using information you share with us. We have no access to school records, we do not speak to teachers on your behalf, and we cannot influence internal assessment or reporting. If you want the tutor and the school in contact, arrange that yourself and both sides will usually cooperate.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in Grade 9, or should we wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 is the cheaper time to fix things, because the content is still being taught rather than revised. A student who builds the habit of showing working and reading command words in Grade 9 carries it into the whole of Grade 10 at no extra cost. Waiting means paying for the same correction under deadline pressure, alongside revision. If Grade 9 marks are holding up and the study habits look sound, waiting is perfectly reasonable.

h1: IGCSE Tutors in Sector 99, Gurugram: Working Backwards from the Exam Date
heroSubtitle: Every useful tutoring decision here starts with a date. Which series the school has entered, when the mocks fall, when practical and coursework deadlines land. We build the plan backwards from that, then find a Cambridge or Edexcel tutor who can hold the schedule from Sector 99.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sector 99 Gurugram can be arranged for Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE students at home along the Dwarka Expressway sectors or online across the city, covering Grade 1 to Grade 12. The first question is always the calendar: which exam series the school has entered your child for, how many weeks remain, and what is due inside school before then. That answer decides session frequency, subject count and whether a late start is worth making at all.

contentBlocks.heading: The IGCSE Calendar as It Looks from Sector 99, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Parents usually ring us in one of two months: October, or February. October callers are worried after the first reports. February callers have seen a mock result and realised how little time is left. The February call is the harder one, and the difference between them is not the child. It is the calendar.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a March series available in India for a number of syllabuses, and schools decide which one a cohort enters. Pearson Edexcel works to January and June sittings. Whichever applies, the entry is confirmed by the school months before anyone sits a paper, and it is worth asking the coordinator outright rather than guessing.

Working backwards from that date changes everything about a tutoring plan. Twenty weeks out, you can rebuild a topic properly. Eight weeks out, you are choosing which topics to abandon so the rest are secure. Three weeks out, the only honest work is timed papers and question selection.

So IGCSE tutors in Sector 99 Gurugram are booked against a date, not a vague intention to improve. Tell us the series and the subjects and we can say what a term will realistically deliver.

And sometimes the answer is that you should have started in Grade 9.

Edexcel International GCSE sittings in January and June
Entry decided by the school, well before the exams
Twenty weeks, eight weeks and three weeks are three different plans

contentBlocks.heading: Which Papers Land Where in the Year
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics carries the most requests. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) is entered at either Core or Extended, and Extended includes content Core students never meet, so a late tier change is a content problem rather than a difficulty problem. Recent series split assessment between a non-calculator and a calculator paper; check the paper numbers your school uses. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A (4MA1) runs Foundation and Higher tiers over two papers.

The sciences are where calendar pressure bites hardest. Physics (0625), Chemistry (0620) and Biology (0610) each pair theory papers with a practical component that is either a laboratory test or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Schools fix which one well in advance. Students who leave that component until the final month find it is a distinct skill, not a revision topic.

English divides into First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510 or 0511), and some literature and language options carry a coursework element with an internal deadline months ahead of the written papers. Miss it and no amount of tutoring recovers those marks.

Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science round out the usual list. Each rewards a student who can read a stimulus and answer the printed question rather than the remembered one.
items: 0580 Core versus Extended: different content, not just harder questions
4MA1 Foundation and Higher tiers, two papers each
Practical test or alternative-to-practical, decided by the school
Coursework deadlines fall months before written papers
0500 and 0510 or 0511 need different preparation

contentBlocks.heading: Booking Against a Deadline Rather Than a Vague Term
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is short and specific. We ask for the board, the syllabus codes if the school has published them, the tier, the subjects, the series being sat, and the weeks that remain. Then we ask what is already fixed in the school calendar: mocks, internal deadlines, practical assessments, any trip that removes a fortnight.

From that we set a session pattern rather than a session count. A student twenty weeks out from a June series usually needs one weekly hour per subject with proper work between. The same student eight weeks out needs two shorter sessions a week and timed papers rather than teaching.

Only then do we look at tutors. Two or three profiles come back, each showing boards taught, grade levels, and whether they can reach the Dwarka Expressway sectors in person or work online. A trial session follows.

The first checkpoint is set at the fourth week and put in the calendar at the start, so nobody has to raise it awkwardly. By then you should be able to see unprompted attempts at full questions and hear the tutor name specific marks being recovered. If not, a change is made then rather than in the last term.
items: Intake covers board, tier, subjects, series and weeks remaining
School calendar mapped: mocks, coursework, practicals, trips
Session pattern set by the deadline, not by habit
Two or three profiles with boards and grade levels stated
Fourth-week checkpoint diarised in advance

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 99 on the Dwarka Expressway Side of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 99 belongs to the northern Gurugram sectors that grew up along the Dwarka Expressway, with Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon making up much of the residential base. Palam Vihar lies to one side, the New Gurgaon sectors to the other, and Delhi is closer from here than from most of the older city.

That last point shapes tutoring in a way parents from Golf Course Road do not expect. A tutor living in Dwarka or west Delhi can sometimes reach Sector 99 more easily than one living in Sushant Lok, which widens the pool in one direction while narrowing it in another. When you enquire, it helps to say which evenings you can take a later start, because the expressway at half past five and at half past seven are two different roads.

Within the sector itself, the practical unit is the society. A tutor already visiting ATS Kocoon can usually add a family in ATS Triumph without meaningful travel, so adjacent bookings hold better through the term.

The honest limitation: walk-in tuition centres nearby mostly teach Indian boards. For Cambridge or Edexcel specifics, a matched tutor or an online specialist is the realistic route.

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 1 to Grade 12: Where the IGCSE Years Sit in the Sequence
contentBlocks.body:
The IGCSE years occupy Grade 9 and Grade 10, but they are a middle chapter rather than the whole book.

Before them, Cambridge schools generally run a lower secondary stage through to Grade 8, often ending in a checkpoint assessment. Its results are quietly predictive. A student who scores respectably there by memorising examples tends to stall in the first term of Grade 9, when questions begin asking for reasons rather than recall.

After them comes Grade 11, and the choice between A Level, an IB Diploma or another route. That decision is made in the same year the IGCSE papers are being prepared for, which is why families here often want a tutor who can talk sensibly about both the immediate exam and the subject combination waiting on the other side of it.

Primary and middle grade work runs on a different clock entirely, with no external deadline pulling it. Sessions are better judged by whether a child reads for longer, writes more coherently and stops counting on fingers than by any paper. If a tutor's plan for a Grade 3 student is a stack of printed worksheets, keep looking.

Grade 11 and Grade 12 requests are supported, though specialist availability is thinner and needs more notice.

IGCSE across Grade 9 and Grade 10
Grade 11 route decided during the IGCSE years
Primary sessions measured by fluency, not worksheet count

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Run Before a Name Reaches a Sector 99 Family
contentBlocks.body:
Documents come first and take the least time. Identity is verified, and qualifications are checked against the certificates rather than accepted from a summary.

The teaching interview is the filter that matters. Tutors are asked which boards they have taught, over how many cohorts, at which grade levels, and how they would handle a specific weakness. A candidate for Extended Mathematics may be given a student answer with the right result and no working and asked what they would say in the next five minutes. Answers that reference the mark scheme and partial credit pass. Answers about motivation and confidence, with nothing concrete underneath, do not.

Where a tutor has taught in a school or through another platform, references are requested. Many capable tutors have none, so the absence is written on the profile you receive instead of being smoothed over.

What screening cannot establish is fit. No document predicts whether a fifteen-year-old will work with a particular adult, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. The trial session and the fourth-week checkpoint exist to answer that question in practice, and you may end an arrangement at either point without justifying it.

contentBlocks.heading: Sobha City at Six, or a Screen at Nine
contentBlocks.body:
In-person sessions inside the society are the common choice for Grade 9 students and for anyone who needs supervision to start working at all. They also suit subjects where the tutor must watch a hand move: setting out a stoichiometry calculation, drawing a ray diagram to scale, laying out an algebraic proof line by line.

Online earns its place at the two ends of the clock. Early morning slots before the school bus, which some Grade 10 students take surprisingly well in the weeks before a series. And late evening, where travel across the expressway would otherwise consume more time than the lesson.

There is also a seasonal argument. In the run-up to a June sitting, families often shift from one long weekly visit to three short online sessions, each built around one timed paper and its marking. Short and frequent beats long and weekly once revision replaces teaching.

A caution worth stating. Online works badly when the underlying issue is avoidance. A student who has been quietly skipping homework will sit through a video call producing nothing, and a parent in another room will not notice for weeks. Start in person in that situation, then move online once work is actually happening.

contentBlocks.heading: School Runs from Sector 99, Gurugram to the IGCSE Campuses
contentBlocks.body:
Enquiries from these societies point at a familiar set of campuses: Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School near Golf Course Road, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School.

All of them involve a long ride from the northern sectors. A child boarding a bus before seven and reaching home past four has already worked a full adult day, and it is worth being blunt about what that leaves. Ninety-minute weekday sessions are usually a poor investment for these students. Sixty or seventy-five minutes on a school night, with the longer effort moved to Saturday or Sunday morning, produces more.

School calendars also decide when tutoring is useful. Mock examinations for a June entry generally sit in the winter term, and a tutor engaged in November can act on those papers. One engaged in March is mostly triaging.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. contentBlocks.heading: Late Starts, Realistic Gains and Where We Say No
contentBlocks.body:
No grade is promised. Not a 9, not a specific number of marks, not a percentage. We publish no success rates, quote no student outcomes and carry no testimonials, because none of it could be substantiated and a page that invents them is worse than a page that stays quiet.

What we will do is answer the late-start question honestly, because in Sector 99 it is the question we get most. Ten weeks before a series, one weak subject can usually be moved meaningfully if the content is largely present and the problem is technique or timing. Two subjects is stretching. Three subjects, with genuine content gaps in each, is not something tutoring fixes, and we would rather decline than take the booking and let a family discover that in June.

Fees depend on tier, how scarce the subject is, session length, mode and travel into the northern sectors. They are agreed before a trial rather than after the first month.

Availability stays conditional throughout. A slot can be reviewed, and often filled, but tutor schedules shift across a term and we will not confirm what we cannot hold.

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging IGCSE Tutors in Sector 99, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with three pieces of information: the board, the subjects with their tier, and the exam series the school has entered your child for. If you are unsure of the last one, ask the coordinator before you write to us, because it changes every recommendation that follows.

Add the weeks that are already spoken for. Mock dates, a coursework submission, a school trip, a family visit abroad. A plan built around a term that quietly loses three weeks is a plan that fails in April, and it is easier to design around those gaps than to repair them later.

Then name the hours that work from your building. Be conservative. Two windows you can genuinely protect are worth more than five that look good in September and collapse by October.

An advisor will come back with what the Dwarka Expressway sectors can support in person, what is better handled online, and a shortlist of two or three tutors with their boards and grade levels shown. A trial session follows, fees are agreed in advance, and the fourth-week checkpoint goes in the calendar at the start.

Where the timeline does not allow a sensible plan, we will tell you that instead.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam series my child has been entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer or the subject coordinator at the school, and ask in writing so you have the reply. Entries are made by the school well ahead of the papers, and they cover the series, the subject codes and the tier. Parents often assume June and discover a different arrangement, particularly where a March or November sitting applies. Once you have that confirmation, everything else about a tutoring plan, including how many subjects are realistic, follows from it.

faqs.question: We are ten weeks from the papers and two subjects are weak. What can honestly be done?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the content exists in your child's head. If the topics were taught and the marks are being lost to timing, working or misread instructions, ten weeks of timed papers with proper marking moves both subjects. If whole topics were never learned, ten weeks across two subjects means choosing which one gets rescued. A tutor should give you that verdict after two sessions, and you should insist on hearing it rather than a reassurance.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a coursework component, or is that only for written papers?
faqs.answer: Support is possible, within limits that matter. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, discuss structure, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor must not write, dictate or substantially rework the piece, because the school has to certify it as the student's own. Ask the school what help is permitted before starting, since practice varies by subject and by centre. The deadline is usually months ahead of the written papers, so plan around it early.

faqs.question: Does living near the Dwarka Expressway limit which tutors can reach us?
faqs.answer: It changes the pool rather than shrinking it. Tutors based in Dwarka or west Delhi often reach Sector 99 faster than someone from the older Gurugram sectors, which opens options a Golf Course Road family would not have. What suffers is the early evening, when the corridor is slow. If you can take a later start on one or two days, the choice of tutor widens noticeably. Online removes the question entirely for subjects where it suits.

faqs.question: Our son moved here from a CBSE school last year. How different is IGCSE for him?
faqs.answer: The content overlap in Mathematics and the sciences is larger than most families expect. The assessment style is where the difficulty sits. Questions are wordier, they ask for application to unfamiliar contexts, and the command word governs what earns credit. Students arriving from an Indian board often know more than their marks suggest and simply answer in the wrong register. That gap usually closes in a term of past-paper practice, which is faster than re-teaching content would be.

faqs.question: Can sessions be held in the mornings before school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some Grade 10 students it works better than the evening. A six-thirty or seven o'clock online session before the bus catches a student who is alert, and it protects the evening for school homework. It fails for students who are not morning people, and forcing it produces attendance rather than learning. Try it for two weeks before committing to a term. In-person morning slots are harder to arrange because of travel timing on the expressway.

faqs.question: What happens if a tutor is unavailable close to the exams?
faqs.answer: Tell us early and we look for a replacement, though late in a series the honest position is that options narrow. This is one reason we set the fourth-week checkpoint and discourage a single tutor covering three subjects for one student. Where a tutor knows in advance about travel or a change in availability, that goes on the record when they are matched, so you are not learning about a six-week gap in April. Continuity is worth asking about at the trial.

faqs.question: Is there any link between IB Gram and Pathways World School or GD Goenka World School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named because families in Sobha City, ATS Triumph and the surrounding societies attend them, and knowing the campus helps us understand the pace and specification a student is working to. We hold no agreement with any school, receive nothing from them, and cannot act on your behalf with a school office.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring for Grade 9 or wait for the Grade 10 mocks?
faqs.answer: Waiting for mocks is the most common and most expensive decision families make here. Mock results arrive in the winter term of Grade 10, which leaves a few months to correct habits formed over eighteen. Starting in Grade 9 costs less per outcome because the content is still being taught and there is room to build technique without deadline pressure. If Grade 9 marks are solid and homework is being done properly, waiting is a fair judgement to make.

mainEntity.name: How do I find out which exam series my child has been entered for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask the examinations officer or the subject coordinator at the school, and ask in writing so you have the reply. Entries are made by the school well ahead of the papers, and they cover the series, the subject codes and the tier. Parents often assume June and discover a different arrangement, particularly where a March or November sitting applies. Once you have that confirmation, everything else about a tutoring plan, including how many subjects are realistic, follows from it.

mainEntity.name: We are ten weeks from the papers and two subjects are weak. What can honestly be done?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends entirely on whether the content exists in your child's head. If the topics were taught and the marks are being lost to timing, working or misread instructions, ten weeks of timed papers with proper marking moves both subjects. If whole topics were never learned, ten weeks across two subjects means choosing which one gets rescued. A tutor should give you that verdict after two sessions, and you should insist on hearing it rather than a reassurance.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with a coursework component, or is that only for written papers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Support is possible, within limits that matter. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, discuss structure, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor must not write, dictate or substantially rework the piece, because the school has to certify it as the student's own. Ask the school what help is permitted before starting, since practice varies by subject and by centre. The deadline is usually months ahead of the written papers, so plan around it early.

mainEntity.name: Does living near the Dwarka Expressway limit which tutors can reach us?

acceptedAnswer.text: It changes the pool rather than shrinking it. Tutors based in Dwarka or west Delhi often reach Sector 99 faster than someone from the older Gurugram sectors, which opens options a Golf Course Road family would not have. What suffers is the early evening, when the corridor is slow. If you can take a later start on one or two days, the choice of tutor widens noticeably. Online removes the question entirely for subjects where it suits.

mainEntity.name: Our son moved here from a CBSE school last year. How different is IGCSE for him?

acceptedAnswer.text: The content overlap in Mathematics and the sciences is larger than most families expect. The assessment style is where the difficulty sits. Questions are wordier, they ask for application to unfamiliar contexts, and the command word governs what earns credit. Students arriving from an Indian board often know more than their marks suggest and simply answer in the wrong register. That gap usually closes in a term of past-paper practice, which is faster than re-teaching content would be.

mainEntity.name: Can sessions be held in the mornings before school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and for some Grade 10 students it works better than the evening. A six-thirty or seven o'clock online session before the bus catches a student who is alert, and it protects the evening for school homework. It fails for students who are not morning people, and forcing it produces attendance rather than learning. Try it for two weeks before committing to a term. In-person morning slots are harder to arrange because of travel timing on the expressway.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a tutor is unavailable close to the exams?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us early and we look for a replacement, though late in a series the honest position is that options narrow. This is one reason we set the fourth-week checkpoint and discourage a single tutor covering three subjects for one student. Where a tutor knows in advance about travel or a change in availability, that goes on the record when they are matched, so you are not learning about a six-week gap in April. Continuity is worth asking about at the trial.

mainEntity.name: Is there any link between IB Gram and Pathways World School or GD Goenka World School?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named because families in Sobha City, ATS Triumph and the surrounding societies attend them, and knowing the campus helps us understand the pace and specification a student is working to. We hold no agreement with any school, receive nothing from them, and cannot act on your behalf with a school office.

mainEntity.name: Should we book tutoring for Grade 9 or wait for the Grade 10 mocks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waiting for mocks is the most common and most expensive decision families make here. Mock results arrive in the winter term of Grade 10, which leaves a few months to correct habits formed over eighteen. Starting in Grade 9 costs less per outcome because the content is still being taught and there is room to build technique without deadline pressure. If Grade 9 marks are solid and homework is being done properly, waiting is a fair judgement to make.

finalCta: Send the board, the subjects with their tier, and the exam series your school has entered. An advisor will map what the remaining weeks allow, say which sessions can run in person across the Dwarka Expressway sectors and which suit online, and share two or three tutor profiles before any trial.
